I will open new issues for any other problems. ### Describe the bug On Linux/X11, when I resize a window quickly, the window content shakes (in a vertical direction). When the window height grows, the window content is too low. When the window height shrinks, the window content is too high. I think, this happens only when a redraw is too slow and the window size has changed in the meantime. The problem is that the now too large or too small window content is anchored at the bottom left corner window corner. We should shift the window content (the framebuffer) to compensate for the grown/shrunk window and make sure the top left corner always stays at the same position. This issue sounds similar to #3660. But this issue is on Linux and about vertical movement, while #3660 is on macOS and about horizontal stretching. ### How to reproduce 1. Run Fyne Demo on Linux/X11. 2. Select the "Theme Icons" tab. 3. Resize quickly (both in X and Y direction because the delay happens only when the icons grows). ### Screenshots ### Example code See Fyne Demo for example. ### Fyne version develop ### Go compiler version 1.27.1 ### Operating system and version Arch Linux with X11 (dwm) ### Additional Information _No response_

fyne-io/fyne.title: TextGrid under ThemeOverride draws letters in mixed fonts and sizes
fyne-io/fyne.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the issue tracker for open issues that relate to the same problem, before opening a new one.
- [x] This issue only relates to a single bug. I will open new issues for any other problems.

### Describe the bug

A `TextGrid` inside a `container.ThemeOverride` that changes the monospace font and text size draws letters in mixed fonts and sizes (uppercase larger, some rows unlike others) once its text grows or rows are reused.

### How to reproduce

1. Put a `widget.TextGrid` in a `container.ThemeOverride` whose theme returns another monospace font (e.g. Courier Prime) and another text size.
2. Show the same letters elsewhere in the window (a monospace label).
3. Grow the grid's text, resize the window, or replace rows.
4. Letters come out in mixed sizes and fonts: uppercase larger, and early rows differ from later ones.

Reproduced on develop (1001840c) with the software painter (`test.NewWindow` + `Capture`); first seen in an app on GL.

### Example code

```go
type monoTheme struct {
	fyne.Theme
	mono fyne.Resource
	size float32
}

func (m *monoTheme) Font(s fyne.TextStyle) fyne.Resource {
	if s.Monospace {
		return m.mono // any monospace .ttf other than the default
	}
	return m.Theme.Font(s)
}

func (m *monoTheme) Size(n fyne.ThemeSizeName) float32 {
	if n == theme.SizeNameText {
		return m.size
	}
	return m.Theme.Size(n)
}

// in a test:
grid := widget.NewTextGridFromString("Line one is here.\n")
label := widget.NewLabel("Line many is here. ABCDEFG")
label.TextStyle.Monospace = true
w := test.NewWindow(container.NewBorder(label, nil, nil, nil,
	container.NewThemeOverride(grid, &monoTheme{Theme: theme.DefaultTheme(), mono: mono, size: 21})))
w.Resize(fyne.NewSize(500, 420))
w.Canvas().Capture()
grid.SetText(strings.Repeat("Line many is here. ABCDEFG\n", 12))
img := w.Canvas().Capture() // mixed sizes and fonts across rows, uppercase larger
```

### Fix

Rows and cells the grid makes after the override was applied are not in its scope, so they use the app theme. Making them join it with `cache.OverrideThemeMatchingScope`, as List and Tree do, fixes it: #6594 (10 lines plus a test).

Separately, text under an override was measured in the app theme's font, and the text size and texture caches don't key on the scope: #6593 (not needed for this bug).

### Device (please complete the following information):
 - **OS:** Linux (ChromeOS Crostini, X11); reproduced with the software painter in tests
 - **Version:** develop (2.8 line)
 - **Go version:** 1.26
 - **Fyne version:** develop at 1001840c

fyne-io/fyne.title: Wayland touchpad gestures
fyne-io/fyne.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://github.com/fyne-io/fyne/issues) for open issues that relate to the same feature, before opening a new one.
- [x] This issue only relates to a single feature. I will open new issues for any other features.

### Is your feature request related to a problem?

I'm building a Fyne app targeting Linux/Wayland and want to react to touchpad gestures (pinch, swipe, hold). Wayland exposes these through the protocol, but there is currently no way for a Fyne application to read them.

### Is it possible to construct a solution with the existing API?

Not cleanly. The window's `wl_surface`, `wl_display` and seat are owned by GLFW, so an application can't get gesture events by opening its own Wayland connection (events are delivered to the client that owns the surface). A workaround needs GLFW's native Wayland handles, a cgo binding of the gesture protocol on that connection, and a way to hand events back to the app safely.

### Describe the solution you'd like to see.

Any of these would solve it for me, in order of preference:

1. **A simple way to receive the raw gesture events**, for example a window-level callback or channel carrying begin/update/end events with the fields the protocol provides (finger count, scale, rotation, delta).
2. **Expose the native Wayland handles** (`wl_display`, `wl_surface`, `wl_seat`) from the driver/window, so applications can bind `zwp_pointer_gestures_v1` themselves.
3. Guidance on a supported way to do this with the current driver, if one already exists.

fyne-io/fyne.title: macOS: every new theme-override scope runs `defaults read -g AppleLocale` on the main thread
fyne-io/fyne.body:
### Checklist
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://github.com/fyne-io/fyne/issues) for open issues that relate to the same problem.
- [x] This issue only relates to a single bug.

### Describe the bug

Font faces are cached per `cacheID{style, scope}` (`internal/painter/font.go`, `CachedFontFace`). `container.NewThemeOverride`, its `CreateRenderer` and its `Refresh` each mint a new scope (`cache.OverrideTheme` → `overrideCount.Add(1)`). The first text painted in a new scope misses, and `lookupFaces` → `lookupLangFont` → `lang.SystemLocale()` → `go-locale.GetLocale()` runs on the main thread inside the paint.

On macOS, go-locale only answers via NSBundle when the bundle has >1 localization. Otherwise it runs `exec.Command("defaults", "read", "-g", "AppleLocale")`. That fallback became the normal path for most apps with jeandeaual/go-locale@0ef82f2 ("Don't use app localisations if they are not supported"), the fix for #5760. So the system locale, which does not depend on scope, is resolved with a fork+exec once per scope × text style.

Cost: ~11 ms per call in a minimal app. In our app (3 GB whisper model resident) each call is ~200 ms; a Settings window with 16 overrides blocked the main thread ~3.6 s (beachball), and a hover that `Refresh`es an override paid it again.

### How to reproduce
1. Put a counting shim first on `PATH`:
   `mkdir -p shim; printf '#!/bin/sh\necho x >> /tmp/calls\nexec /usr/bin/defaults "$@"\n' > shim/defaults; chmod +x shim/defaults`
2. Run the example with `PATH=$PWD/shim:$PATH go run .`
3. `wc -l /tmp/calls`: 18 with 16 overrides, 2 with none. Open + first paint: ~410 ms vs ~215 ms.

### Example code

```go
package main

import (
	"fmt"
	"time"

	"fyne.io/fyne/v2"
	"fyne.io/fyne/v2/app"
	"fyne.io/fyne/v2/container"
	"fyne.io/fyne/v2/theme"
	"fyne.io/fyne/v2/widget"
)

func main() {
	a := app.New()
	w := a.NewWindow("Repro")
	w.SetContent(widget.NewLabel("main"))
	go func() {
		time.Sleep(time.Second)
		fyne.Do(func() {
			start := time.Now()
			box := container.NewVBox()
			for i := range 16 { // 0 here: 16 fewer `defaults` calls
				box.Add(container.NewThemeOverride(widget.NewLabel(fmt.Sprint("row ", i)), theme.DefaultTheme()))
			}
			w2 := a.NewWindow("16 overrides")
			w2.SetContent(box)
			w2.Show()
			go func() {
				fyne.DoAndWait(func() {}) // after the first paint
				fmt.Println("open + first paint:", time.Since(start))
				fyne.Do(a.Quit)
			}()
		})
	}()
	w.ShowAndRun()
}
```

### Fyne version

v2.8.1 (also present on `develop` as of 2026-10-08)

### Go compiler version

1.27.1

### Operating system and version

macOS 27.0.1 (arm64)

### Additional Information

Possible fixes, any one helps:
- Resolve the locale once in `lookupLangFont` (e.g. `sync.OnceValue`, reset on settings change).
- Key the language-fallback face by style + family, not scope; it does not depend on the theme.
- go-locale: ask `NSLocale` before shelling out when the bundle has no translations.

Related: #5760, jeandeaual/go-locale@0ef82f2. #6555 (font parse caching) does not cover this.

fyne-io/fyne.title: Update golang.org/x/image to address TIFF resource exhaustion vulnerability
fyne-io/fyne.body:
The `develop` branch currently requires `golang.org/x/image v0.24.0`, which is affected by a published high-severity TIFF decoder vulnerability:

- [GHSA-q675-qj96-32m9](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-q675-qj96-32m9) / [CVE-2026-46599](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-46599)
- [Go vulnerability GO-2026-5032](https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-5032)
- Affected versions: `< v0.41.0`
- Fixed version: `v0.41.0`

The advisory describes excessive resource consumption when decoding malicious PackBits-compressed TIFF data.

Dependabot already proposed the required update in #6399, but that PR was closed because `golang.org/x/image v0.41.0` requires Go 1.25, which Fyne does not require yet. The earlier v0.38.0 update in #6238 was closed for the same minimum-Go-version reason and would not fix this newer advisory anyway.

This issue tracks choosing and completing a remediation, such as updating Fyne's supported Go version so `x/image` can be upgraded, or applying another compatible mitigation until that is possible.

fyne-io/fyne.title: Preferences directory created on app startup even when preferences are not used
fyne-io/fyne.body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the issue tracker for open issues that relate to the same problem.
- [X] This issue only relates to a single bug. I will open new issues for any other problems.

### Describe the bug

Fyne creates the preferences storage directory (`~/.config/fyne/<app-id>/` on Linux) during `app.New()` initialization, even if the application never uses Fyne's Preferences API.

This happens because `newPreferences()` calls `p.load()` which triggers `storageReaderForPath()`, and that function calls `os.MkdirAll()` even when the preferences file doesn't exist:

```go
// In app/preferences_nonweb.go
func (p *preferences) storageReaderForPath(path string) (io.ReadCloser, error) {
    file, err := os.Open(path)
    if err != nil {
        if os.IsNotExist(err) {
            if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(path), 0o700); err != nil {  // <-- creates directory
                return nil, err
            }
            return nil, errEmptyPreferencesStore
        }
        return nil, err
    }
    return file, nil
}
```

### How to reproduce

1. Create a minimal Fyne app with an app ID but no preferences usage:
```go
package main

import (
    "fyne.io/fyne/v2/app"
    "fyne.io/fyne/v2/widget"
)

func main() {
    a := app.NewWithID("com.example.test")
    w := a.NewWindow("Test")
    w.SetContent(widget.NewLabel("Hello"))
    w.ShowAndRun()
}
```
2. Run the app on Linux
3. Observe that `~/.config/fyne/com.example.test/` is created, even though no preferences were set or read

### Screenshots

N/A

### Example code

See above.

### Fyne version

2.8.1

### Go compiler version

1.23.x

### Operating system and version

Linux (Ubuntu, Fedora, etc.)

### Additional Information

This is problematic for applications that:
- Use their own configuration storage instead of Fyne's Preferences API
- Want to keep users' config directories clean
- Follow XDG conventions with their own directory structure

**Suggested fix:** Only create the directory when actually writing preferences, not when attempting to read them. The `storageReaderForPath` function shouldn't need to create directories — it's a read operation.

Related downstream issue: https://github.com/Strobotti/linkquisition/issues/194

fyne-io/fyne.title: Web backend calls preventDefault on every key, so the browser cannot handle Cmd+1–9 or reload
fyne-io/fyne.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://github.com/fyne-io/fyne/issues) for open issues that relate to the same problem, before opening a new one.
- [x] This issue only relates to a single bug. I will open new issues for any other problems.

### Describe the bug

A Fyne app packaged for the web calls `preventDefault()` on every `keydown` and `keyup`. Chrome then skips shortcuts it still allows a page to override.

Blocked while the canvas is focused:

- Cmd+1 through Cmd+9 (jump to a browser tab). Ctrl+1–9 on other platforms.
- Cmd+R and Cmd+Shift+R (reload and force reload). Ctrl+R / Ctrl+Shift+R elsewhere.
- F5.

Ctrl+Tab still changes tabs. Chrome treats that shortcut as reserved and ignores `preventDefault`.

The call is in `fyne-io/glfw-js` v0.4.0, `browser_wasm.go`, in the document `keydown` and `keyup` listeners. The key callback is started with `go` and returns nothing, so an app cannot decline the event before `preventDefault()` runs. `Canvas.AddShortcut` only delivers shortcuts into the app. It cannot give the key back to the browser.

### How to reproduce

1. Package any Fyne app with `fyne package -os web` and open it in Chrome on macOS.
2. Click the canvas so it has focus.
3. Press Cmd+2. The browser stays on this tab.
4. Press Cmd+Shift+R. The page does not reload.
5. Press Ctrl+Tab. The browser switches tabs.

### Example code

```go
package main

import (
	"fyne.io/fyne/v2"
	"fyne.io/fyne/v2/app"
	"fyne.io/fyne/v2/widget"
)

func main() {
	a := app.New()
	w := a.NewWindow("shortcut check")
	w.SetContent(widget.NewLabel("Click here, then press Cmd+2 or Cmd+Shift+R"))
	w.Resize(fyne.NewSize(480, 240))
	w.ShowAndRun()
}
```

Build with `fyne package -os web` and open the generated page. No shortcut has to be registered. The backend consumes the keys on its own.

### Fyne version

2.8.1 (`fyne.io/fyne/v2`), with `github.com/fyne-io/glfw-js` v0.4.0

### Go compiler version

go1.27.1

### Operating system and version

macOS, Chrome. The same `preventDefault()` runs for every browser, so Ctrl+number and Ctrl+R are affected on Windows and Linux too.

### Additional Information

A page can work around this with a capture-phase listener that calls `stopImmediatePropagation()` for those shortcuts before the GLFW listener runs. The fix belongs in `glfw-js`: skip `preventDefault()` for browser chrome shortcuts, or call it only when the app reports that it consumed the key. That decision has to happen in the event handler, before the goroutine.

Reported by Grok.

fyne-io/fyne.title: Wayland: SIGSEGV in PollEvents when the window's monitor is switched away

labels.name: unverified
labels.description: A bug that has been reported but not verified

fyne-io/fyne.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://github.com/fyne-io/fyne/issues) for open issues that relate to the same problem, before opening a new one.
- [x] This issue only relates to a single bug. I will open new issues for any other problems.

### Describe the bug

### Describe the bug

On Wayland, if the Fyne window sits on a monitor that goes away (KVM switch or unplug), the process dies. The crash is a SIGSEGV inside `glfw.PollEvents`, while GLFW handles `wl_registry.global_remove` for that output. `recover()` cannot catch it.

A window on a different monitor is fine.
A KVM often leaves DRM `status=connected` and only sets `enabled=disabled`.

Hiding the window does not help. `PollEvents` still crashes on the events that arrived while the output was down. `glfw.Terminate()` drops those events without reading them. A new `glfw.Init()` and a new window can then be shown when the output is back.

### How to reproduce

1. Run a Fyne app on Wayland, with the window on one monitor.
2. Switch that monitor away with a KVM, or unplug it.
3. The process dies in `glfw.PollEvents`.

### Screenshots

```go
package main

import "fyne.io/fyne/v2/app"

func main() {
	w := app.New().NewWindow("repro")
	w.ShowAndRun()
}
```

Fyne 2.8.1, go-gl/glfw v3.4 (`v0.1.0-pre.2`), Linux Wayland.

fyne-io/fyne.title: Modal PopUp/dialog content re-centers on every canvas resize (regression since 2.8.0) — Android soft keyboard causes buttons to shift under finger mid-tap

labels.name: unverified
labels.description: A bug that has been reported but not verified

fyne-io/fyne.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://github.com/fyne-io/fyne/issues) for open issues that relate to the same problem, before opening a new one.
- [x] This issue only relates to a single bug. I will open new issues for any other problems.

### Describe the bug


A modal dialog/PopUp containing a focusable text `Entry` re-centers its content
every time the canvas resizes. On Android, opening/closing the on-screen
keyboard resizes the app canvas, so **the dialog's buttons visibly move
vertically while the keyboard opens/closes**.

Because tapping any button in the dialog while the Entry still has focus
first triggers focus loss (closing the keyboard) as part of the same
touch-down/touch-up gesture, the button positions can shift *during* that
gesture. The result is unreliable tap handling: sometimes the tap only
closes the keyboard, sometimes it lands on a different button than the one
under the finger.

### Root cause (found by bisecting the source between 2.7.4 and 2.8.1)

`internal/widget/overlay_container.go`, `overlayRenderer.Layout`:

**2.7.4** — no-op, does not touch the content on canvas layout:
```go
func (r *overlayRenderer) Layout(fyne.Size) {
}
```

**2.8.0/2.8.1** — actively resizes and re-centers the content on every layout pass:
```go
func (r *overlayRenderer) Layout(s fyne.Size) {
	size := internal.MinSizes(internal.MaxSizes(r.o.Content.Size(), r.o.Content.MinSize()), s)
	r.o.Content.Resize(size)
	if r.o.Background != nil {
		r.o.Background.Resize(s)
	}
	if r.o.manual { // position is overridden
		return
	}
	midX := s.Width/2 - size.Width/2
	midY := s.Height/2 - size.Height/2
	r.o.Content.Move(fyne.NewPos(midX, midY))
}
```

In 2.7.4 the `OverlayContainer` never forwarded a canvas resize down to its
`Content` (the dialog's `PopUp`), so the popup only positioned itself once
(at `Show()`/`Refresh()`), never again on a later canvas resize. In 2.8 this
was changed so `overlayRenderer.Layout` calls `Content.Resize(...)` and
re-centers on *every* layout pass — which the canvas engine runs whenever
the canvas itself resizes, including the resize Android performs when the
soft keyboard opens/closes.

This looks like an unintended side effect of the padding/positioning
rework mentioned in the 2.8.0 changelog ("Popups (modal and regular) no
longer include padding by default"), rather than an intentional behavior
change — I couldn't find any changelog entry describing "dialogs now
re-center on every resize" as a deliberate feature.


### How to reproduce

### Steps to reproduce

1. On Android, show a modal dialog (`dialog.NewCustomWithoutButtons` or
   similar) containing a focusable `widget.Entry` and one or more buttons
   below it.
2. Tap the entry to give it focus and open the soft keyboard.
3. Type something, then tap one of the dialog's buttons.
4. Observe: the keyboard closing and the dialog re-centering happen as part
   of the same tap gesture. Depending on timing, either only the keyboard
   closes (button doesn't fire), or a different button than the one tapped
   receives the `Tapped` event because it moved into that screen position
   during the gesture.


### Expected behavior

A dialog's on-screen position should not silently change in response to an
unrelated canvas resize (e.g. a soft keyboard opening/closing) unless it
was explicitly resized/repositioned by the app. At minimum, this
recentering should not happen synchronously with an in-flight tap gesture,
since it makes tap targeting non-deterministic.

### Screenshots

_No response_

### Example code

### Example code

```go
package main

import (
	"fyne.io/fyne/v2"
	"fyne.io/fyne/v2/app"
	"fyne.io/fyne/v2/container"
	"fyne.io/fyne/v2/dialog"
	"fyne.io/fyne/v2/widget"
)

func main() {
	a := app.New()
	w := a.NewWindow("Overlay recenter repro")
	w.Resize(fyne.NewSize(400, 600))

	entry := widget.NewPasswordEntry()
	entry.SetPlaceHolder("PIN")

	var d dialog.Dialog

	btn1 := widget.NewButton("Button 1", func() {
		w.SetTitle("Button 1 tapped")
	})
	btn2 := widget.NewButton("Button 2", func() {
		w.SetTitle("Button 2 tapped")
	})
	cancel := widget.NewButton("Cancel", func() {
		d.Hide()
	})

	content := container.NewVBox(
		widget.NewLabel("Focus the entry, open the keyboard, type something,\nthen tap any button below."),
		entry,
		widget.NewSeparator(),
		btn1,
		btn2,
		cancel,
	)

	d = dialog.NewCustomWithoutButtons("Repro", content, w)
	d.Resize(fyne.NewSize(300, 0))

	open := widget.NewButton("Open dialog", func() {
		d.Show()
	})

	w.SetContent(container.NewCenter(open))
	w.ShowAndRun()
}
```

On Android: tap "Open dialog", tap the entry, type a couple of characters,
then tap Button 1/Button 2/Cancel. The dialog shifts down as the keyboard
closes, and the tap can miss its target or hit the wrong button — the
window title (set by whichever button's callback actually fired, if any)
shows which one really received the tap.

fyne-io/fyne.title: Cache entries touched after a long idle are immediately expired
fyne-io/fyne.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched the issue tracker for related open issues.
- [x] This report covers one bug.

### Describe the bug

Starting with Fyne 2.8.1, cache entries touched after the driver has gone longer than `cache.ValidDuration` without painting can be deleted by the next `cache.Clean` call even though they were just used.

PR #6465 changed `expiringCache.setAlive` to calculate deadlines from `cachedNow`. That sample is refreshed by `Clean`, which normally runs once per frame. After a long gap, however, work performed before the next `Clean` uses the old sample and receives a deadline that is already in the past. The next cleanup then removes both genuinely stale entries and entries used immediately before that cleanup.

This is reproducible in long-running suites using the test/windowless driver. It can also affect the first frame after a real driver has been idle because the GLFW and mobile paths paint or mark entries alive before calling `Clean`.

Fyne 2.8.0 passes the downstream test; Fyne 2.8.1 fails. The same cache implementation is currently present on `develop`.

### How to reproduce

The downstream failure can be accelerated from one minute to 100 ms:

```console
git clone https://github.com/frathe/picfetch.git
cd picfetch
git checkout bd79a46
FYNE_CACHE=100ms go test -race -run '^(TestBuildMainMenu_ActionsItemsDisplayTheirAccelerators|TestE2E_InitialLaunchShowsWelcome)$' -count=1 ./internal/ui
```

`TestE2E_InitialLaunchShowsWelcome` then renders the nested drop-zone text at the top-left instead of its laid-out position. Running that test alone before the cache lifetime expires passes.

The cache behavior itself can be reproduced deterministically with a mock clock in `internal/cache`: create one canvas association, advance `timeNow` by more than `ValidDuration` without refreshing `cachedNow`, create another association, then call `Clean(true)`. Both associations are currently deleted, including the one created immediately before `Clean`.

Failing downstream CI example: https://github.com/frathe/picfetch/actions/runs/33233688520/job/99100802574

### Example code

```go
tm := &timeMock{}
tm.setTime(10, 10)
canvas := &dummyCanvas{}
oldObject := &dummyWidget{}
recentObject := &dummyWidget{}
SetCanvasForObject(oldObject, canvas, nil)

// Advance the real/mock clock without refreshing cachedNow.
tm.now = tm.now.Add(ValidDuration + time.Second)
SetCanvasForObject(recentObject, canvas, nil)
Clean(true)

_, recentFound := canvases.Load(recentObject)
assert.True(t, recentFound) // fails: the just-used entry was deleted
```

### Fyne version

2.8.1; also reproduced on `develop` at 3c6ad39a3537c74a8e9eca873858d01720acb71e.

### Go compiler version

go1.27.0 darwin/arm64 locally; the downstream GitHub Actions failure also reproduces on its Linux runner.

### Operating system and version

macOS 26.6.2 locally and Ubuntu on GitHub Actions.

### Additional information

A minimal fix is to detect when the clock sample is older than the complete cache lifetime and defer deletion for one cleanup pass. `cachedNow` is refreshed immediately, active entries are restamped from it during the following frame, and genuinely stale entries are removed on the next eligible cleanup. This keeps the per-object path free of `time.Now()` calls.

fyne-io/fyne.title: perf(test): support reusable image buffer in test.Canvas.Capture() to reduce heap churn in test suites
fyne-io/fyne.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://github.com/fyne-io/fyne/issues) for open issues that relate to the same feature, before opening a new one.
- [x] This issue only relates to a single feature. I will open new issues for any other features.

### Is your feature request related to a problem?

In `fyne.io/fyne/v2/test`, calling `Canvas.Capture()` allocates a new `image.NewNRGBA` on every invocation:
- For a standard 1280x800 headless window, each capture allocates **~4.10 MB** of heap memory.
- In automated test suites executing continuous visual checks, frame telemetry, or regression loops (e.g. 100+ frames), this creates significant GC pressure (~410 MB allocated for 100 frames) and frequent GC pauses during testing.

### Is it possible to construct a solution with the existing API?

Currently, `test.Canvas.Capture()` returns a freshly allocated `image.Image` without exposing an option to write into an existing or pooled buffer.

### Describe the solution you'd like to see.

Add a non-breaking helper method or allow buffer reuse, for example:
- Adding `CaptureTo(dst *image.NRGBA)` (or `CaptureTo(dst draw.Image)`) on `test.WindowlessCanvas` / `test.Canvas` to allow test runners and harnesses to reuse pre-allocated framebuffers across frames.
- Or utilizing an internal buffer pool (`sync.Pool`) for software rendering passes where appropriate.

**Benchmark comparison (1280x800 Canvas Capture):**
- Current `c.Capture()`: **4,101,144 B/op**, 304 allocs/op (~5.13 ms/op).
- Reusable buffer / zero-alloc path: **0 B/op**, 0 allocs/op (~2.27 ms/op, ~2.2x speedup).

fyne-io/fyne.title: Accessibility: macOS system tray item has no AX label or description
fyne-io/fyne.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched the Fyne and `fyne-io/systray` issue trackers for an existing accessibility-label report.
- [x] This report covers one accessibility defect.

### Describe the bug

A Fyne v2.8.0 application built with `-tags accessibility` and configured with `desktop.App.SetSystemTrayIcon`, `SetSystemTrayWindow`, and `SetSystemTrayMenu` exposes its macOS status item as an `AXMenuBarItem` / `AXMenuExtra` with an empty title and no description. VoiceOver and other AX clients therefore have no application name for the tray control.

The underlying `fyne-io/systray` package provides `SetTooltip`, but Fyne does not expose a tray tooltip/accessibility-label API and does not set one from app metadata or the `fyne.Menu` title.

### To reproduce

```go
package main

import (
    "fyne.io/fyne/v2"
    "fyne.io/fyne/v2/app"
    "fyne.io/fyne/v2/driver/desktop"
    "fyne.io/fyne/v2/theme"
)

func main() {
    a := app.NewWithID("dev.example.tray-ax")
    w := a.NewWindow("Tray AX")
    d := a.(desktop.App)
    d.SetSystemTrayIcon(theme.FolderIcon())
    d.SetSystemTrayWindow(w)
    d.SetSystemTrayMenu(fyne.NewMenu("Tray AX", fyne.NewMenuItem("Show", w.Show)))
    w.ShowAndRun()
}
```

Build with `go build -tags accessibility`. In Accessibility Inspector, or via `AXUIElementCopyAttributeValue`, the status item reports:

```text
role=AXMenuBarItem
subrole=AXMenuExtra
title=""
description=nil
```

### Expected behavior

The system-tray item should have an accessible name, preferably derived from application metadata / the menu title. Alternatively, `desktop.App` should expose a cross-platform method to set a tray tooltip/accessibility label.

### Environment

- Fyne: v2.8.0
- Go: 1.25.1
- macOS: 26.5.2 arm64
- Build tag: `accessibility`

### Impact

The tray is the primary control surface for background applications. An unnamed status item prevents a screen-reader audit from passing even when the main window labels are exposed.

fyne-io/fyne.title: Accessibility: widget.Card content is omitted from macOS AX tree in v2.8.0

labels.name: blocker
labels.description: Items that would block a forthcoming release

fyne-io/fyne.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched the issue tracker for an existing `widget.Card` accessibility report.
- [x] This report covers one accessibility-tree defect.

### Describe the bug

With Fyne v2.8.0 built using `-tags accessibility`, labels nested in a `widget.Card` are absent from the macOS Accessibility (AX) tree. A sibling `widget.Label` outside the Card is exposed correctly.

The current Darwin walker returns immediately for a canvas object that does not implement `fyne.Accessible`, and only recurses into `*fyne.Container`. `widget.Card` does not implement `fyne.Accessible`, and its title, subtitle, and content live in its renderer. Consequently the entire Card subtree is dropped.

This blocks VoiceOver qualification for an otherwise static status panel.

### To reproduce

```go
package main

import (
    "fyne.io/fyne/v2/app"
    "fyne.io/fyne/v2/container"
    "fyne.io/fyne/v2/widget"
)

func main() {
    a := app.NewWithID("dev.example.card-ax")
    w := a.NewWindow("Card AX")
    w.SetContent(container.NewVBox(
        widget.NewLabel("Visible sibling"),
        widget.NewCard("Missing title", "Missing subtitle",
            widget.NewLabel("Missing content")),
    ))
    w.ShowAndRun()
}
```

Build and run on macOS:

```sh
go build -tags accessibility .
./card-ax
```

Inspect the application with Accessibility Inspector or `AXUIElement`. `Visible sibling` appears; `Missing title`, `Missing subtitle`, and `Missing content` do not.

### Expected behavior

The Card should expose its title/subtitle and descend into its accessible content, or the shared accessibility walker should traverse accessible descendants through renderer-backed widgets.

### Environment

- Fyne: v2.8.0
- Go: 1.25.1
- macOS: 26.5.2 arm64
- Build tag: `accessibility`

### Workaround

Replace `widget.Card` with a tree composed only of `*fyne.Container` and accessible child widgets. This preserves labels in the AX tree but requires applications to reimplement Card presentation.

fyne-io/fyne.title: Problem with Modifier keys on Windows
fyne-io/fyne.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://github.com/fyne-io/fyne/issues) for open issues that relate to the same problem, before opening a new one.
- [x] This issue only relates to a single bug. I will open new issues for any other problems.

### Describe the bug

# `CurrentKeyModifiers()` reports no modifier while a modifier key is still held (Windows, X11)

## Describe the bug

`desktop.Driver.CurrentKeyModifiers()` clears a modifier's bit while that modifier key
is still physically held down. It reports the modifier correctly for roughly the
keyboard auto-repeat delay (~500 ms on a default Windows configuration), then reports
`0` until the key is released and pressed again.

The cause is that a held key auto-repeats, GLFW delivers those repeats as
`glfw.Repeat`, and `desktopModifierCorrected` treats every action that is not
`glfw.Press` as a release.

This breaks any gesture that asks for the modifier state at a moment that is not
itself a key event — modifier+click and modifier+scroll being the obvious ones, since
neither `fyne.PointEvent` nor `fyne.ScrollEvent` carries modifiers, so
`CurrentKeyModifiers()` is the only way to read them.

## To Reproduce

Save as `main.go` in an empty module with `fyne.io/fyne/v2 v2.8.0`:

```go
// Minimal reproducer: desktop.Driver.CurrentKeyModifiers() reports no modifier
// while a modifier key is still physically held down.
package main

import (
        "strings"
        "time"

        "fyne.io/fyne/v2"
        "fyne.io/fyne/v2/app"
        "fyne.io/fyne/v2/container"
        "fyne.io/fyne/v2/driver/desktop"
        "fyne.io/fyne/v2/widget"
)

func main() {
        a := app.New()
        w := a.NewWindow("CurrentKeyModifiers repro")

        live := widget.NewLabel("live: (waiting)")
        atClick := widget.NewLabel("at click: (no click yet)")

        btn := widget.NewButton("click me while holding the modifier", func() {
                atClick.SetText("at click: " + describe(currentModifiers()))
        })

        w.SetContent(container.NewVBox(
                widget.NewLabel("Press and HOLD Ctrl (Cmd on macOS). Press nothing else."),
                live,
                btn,
                atClick,
        ))

        // Poll rather than hook a key event: the point is what the accessor reports
        // to a caller that asks at an arbitrary moment, which is exactly what a tap
        // or scroll handler does.
        go func() {
                for range time.Tick(100 * time.Millisecond) {
                        text := "live: " + describe(currentModifiers())
                        fyne.Do(func() { live.SetText(text) })
                }
        }()

        w.Resize(fyne.NewSize(520, 180))
        w.ShowAndRun()
}

func currentModifiers() fyne.KeyModifier {
        if d, ok := fyne.CurrentApp().Driver().(desktop.Driver); ok {
                return d.CurrentKeyModifiers()
        }

        return 0
}

func describe(m fyne.KeyModifier) string {
        var held []string
        if m&fyne.KeyModifierShift != 0 {
                held = append(held, "Shift")
        }
        if m&fyne.KeyModifierControl != 0 {
                held = append(held, "Control")
        }
        if m&fyne.KeyModifierAlt != 0 {
                held = append(held, "Alt")
        }
        if m&fyne.KeyModifierSuper != 0 {
                held = append(held, "Super")
        }
        if len(held) == 0 {
                return "(none)"
        }

        return strings.Join(held, "+")
}
```

Steps:

1. Run it on Windows.
2. Press and **hold** Ctrl. Press nothing else.
3. Watch the `live:` line for two seconds.
4. Still holding Ctrl, click the button.

## Expected behaviour

`live:` reports `Control` continuously for as long as Ctrl is held, and the click
reports `at click: Control`.

## Actual behaviour

`live:` reports `Control` briefly, then flips to `(none)` while Ctrl is still held
down. The click reports `at click: (none)`.

Clicking *within* the auto-repeat delay — pressing Ctrl and clicking near-simultaneously
— does report `Control`, which is the tell-tale timing signature of this bug.

## Root cause

[`internal/driver/glfw/window_desktop.go`](https://github.com/fyne-io/fyne/blob/master/internal/driver/glfw/window_desktop.go),
`desktopModifierCorrected`:

```go
func desktopModifierCorrected(mods glfw.ModifierKey, key glfw.Key, action glfw.Action) fyne.KeyModifier {
        // On X11, pressing/releasing modifier keys does not include newly pressed/released keys in 'mod' mask.
        // https://github.com/glfw/glfw/issues/1630
        if action == glfw.Press {
                mods |= glfwKeyToModifier(key)
        } else {
                mods &= ^glfwKeyToModifier(key)   // <-- glfw.Repeat lands here
        }
        return desktopModifier(mods)
}
```

`glfw.Repeat` is neither `Press` nor `Release`, so it takes the `else` branch and
clears the bit for its own key. `keyPressed` assigns the result straight to the
driver-wide latch that `CurrentKeyModifiers()` returns:

```go
w.driver.currentKeyModifiers = desktopModifierCorrected(mods, key, action)
```

The chain on Windows:

1. Windows auto-repeats a held key as further `WM_KEYDOWN` messages.
2. `_glfwInputKey` promotes a press of an already-pressed key to a repeat
   ([`glfw/src/input.c`](https://github.com/glfw/glfw/blob/master/src/input.c)):
   ```c
   if (action == GLFW_PRESS && window->keys[key] == GLFW_PRESS)
       repeated = GLFW_TRUE;
   ...
   if (repeated) action = GLFW_REPEAT;
   ```
3. The incoming `mods` on that repeat **does** contain `GLFW_MOD_CONTROL` —
   `getKeyMods()` in `glfw/src/win32_window.c` reads live physical state via
   `GetKeyState(VK_CONTROL) & 0x8000`.
4. So `desktopModifierCorrected` receives `mods = ModControl, key = KeyLeftControl,
   action = Repeat`, takes the `else` branch, and returns `0`.

The bit is only restored on the next genuine `glfw.Press`, i.e. after the user
releases and re-presses the key.

### Why macOS is unaffected

On macOS, modifier keys arrive through `flagsChanged:` in `glfw/src/cocoa_window.m`,
which only ever calls `_glfwInputKey` with `GLFW_PRESS` or `GLFW_RELEASE` — a modifier
key never produces a `GLFW_REPEAT`. So the `else` branch is only reached on a real
release, and the latch stays correct.

X11 auto-repeats too, so Linux is expected to be affected on the same path, though I
have only confirmed the failure on Windows.

### Scope

Only `CurrentKeyModifiers()` is affected. `processKeyPressed` receives the separate,
uncorrected `keyDesktopModifier := desktopModifier(mods)`, so shortcut dispatch and
`fyne.KeyEvent` handling are fine. Consumers that read the modifier state during a
*key* event are also fine, because that event writes the latch from its own `mods`.
The breakage is specific to consumers reading it during a mouse or scroll event.

## Impact

Any modifier+click or modifier+scroll gesture silently degrades to the unmodified
gesture after the user has held the key for half a second — which is the normal way
people perform these gestures. In the app where I hit this, Ctrl+click to multi-select
a thumbnail opened the image instead, and Shift+scroll to pan a zoomed image scrolled
normally. Both work on macOS, which made it look like an app bug rather than a driver
one.

## Proposed fix

Invert the condition so that only a genuine release clears the bit — `Press` and
`Repeat` both mean "this key is down":

```diff
 func desktopModifierCorrected(mods glfw.ModifierKey, key glfw.Key, action glfw.Action) fyne.KeyModifier {
        // On X11, pressing/releasing modifier keys does not include newly pressed/released keys in 'mod' mask.
        // https://github.com/glfw/glfw/issues/1630
-       if action == glfw.Press {
-               mods |= glfwKeyToModifier(key)
-       } else {
+       if action == glfw.Release {
                mods &= ^glfwKeyToModifier(key)
+       } else {
+               // Press and Repeat both mean the key is down. A held modifier key
+               // auto-repeats on Windows and X11, and clearing its bit here would
+               // report the modifier as released while it is still held.
+               mods |= glfwKeyToModifier(key)
        }
        return desktopModifier(mods)
 }
```

This preserves the glfw#1630 workaround the function exists for: on X11 a modifier
key's own press/release still does not appear in the incoming `mods` mask, and both
branches still correct for that. The only behaviour that changes is `glfw.Repeat`,
which previously cleared the bit and now sets it.

## Device and debug info

- Fyne version: v2.8.0, and confirmed still present on `master` at the time of writing
- Go version: go1.26.6
- `github.com/go-gl/glfw/v3.4/glfw v0.1.0-pre.1.0.20260707082822-2a407d02d01a`
- OS: Windows (reproduced); macOS confirmed unaffected; Linux/X11 expected affected but
  not verified

### How to reproduce


## Expected behaviour

### Screenshots

_No response_

### Example code

see above

### Fyne version

2.8.0

### Go compiler version

1.26.6

### Operating system and version

Windows 11

### Additional Information

_No response_

fyne-io/fyne.title: Windows on ARM: desktop builds request OpenGL ES over WGL, with no way to select desktop GL or EGL
fyne-io/fyne.body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://github.com/fyne-io/fyne/issues) for open issues that relate to the same problem, before opening a new one.
- [X] This issue only relates to a single bug. I will open new issues for any other problems.

### Describe the bug

On `windows/arm64` the GLES painter is selected by **architecture**, not by platform, so a desktop Windows-on-ARM binary always asks GLFW for an OpenGL ES 2.0 context through **WGL**. Where the display driver does not expose `WGL_EXT_create_context_es2_profile`, window creation fails and the application has no way to recover.

```
Fyne error: window creation error
  Cause: VersionUnavailable: WGL: Failed to create OpenGL ES context
```

This is the Windows instance of #4782, which reports the same failure on the GLX side. I am opening it separately because that issue is framed around software rendering in a devcontainer, and the discussion there turned on whether that use case is in scope. Windows on ARM is not a niche setup: it is a shipping consumer platform, and the failure needs no container and no emulation to reach.

**Why it happens.** `internal/painter/gl/gl_es.go` is selected by:

```
//go:build (gles || arm || arm64) && !android && !ios && !mobile && !darwin && !wasm && !test_web_driver
```

and `internal/painter/gl/gl_core.go` carries an explicit `!arm && !arm64`. Between them, **no combination of build tags selects desktop GL on arm64**. `internal/driver/glfw/glfw_es.go` then sets:

```go
glfw.WindowHint(glfw.ClientAPI, glfw.OpenGLESAPI)
glfw.WindowHint(glfw.ContextVersionMajor, 2)
glfw.WindowHint(glfw.ContextVersionMinor, 0)
```

Keying on architecture is right for ARM single-board computers and for mobile, where GLES is what exists. It is the wrong axis for Windows on ARM, which is a desktop platform that happens to be ARM. There, requesting GLES through WGL requires an extension that Windows drivers commonly do not expose; GLES on Windows normally arrives through ANGLE's EGL instead.

@Bluebugs reached this diagnosis in [one line on #4782](https://github.com/fyne-io/fyne/issues/4782#issuecomment-2050845835) in April 2024: *"on ARM we are picking GLES, while we should pick GL"*. The build constraints above are what makes that unfixable from outside the toolkit.

**An application cannot work around it.** In `internal/driver/glfw/window_desktop.go`, `initWindowHints()` and `glfw.CreateWindow` are a few lines apart inside `(*window).create`, with nothing in between that calls out to application code, and GLFW hints are thread-local to the GLFW thread. There is no point at which an application can set a hint of its own.

**Bundling ANGLE does not help either.** Placing `libEGL.dll` and `libGLESv2.dll` beside the executable, the way Chromium ships them, changes nothing: the error still names WGL. GLFW does not consult EGL unless asked, and `glfw_es.go` sets only `ClientAPI` and the context version, never `ContextCreationAPI`.

One small thing that may have sent #4782 sideways: `-tags egl` was suggested there and reported not to help. There is no `egl` build tag in the desktop driver in v2.6.3 — every `egl` reference in the tree is under `internal/driver/mobile`, which is a different driver. So that suggestion could not have had any effect.

### How to reproduce

1. Cross-compile a minimal Fyne application for `windows/arm64` (llvm-mingw works).
2. Run it on a Windows-on-ARM system whose display driver does not expose `WGL_EXT_create_context_es2_profile`.
3. No window appears; the error above is printed.

### Screenshots

_No response_

### Example code

```go
func main() {
	a := app.New()
	w := a.NewWindow("Hello")
	w.ShowAndRun()
}
```

### Fyne version

2.6.3

### Go compiler version

1.25.1

### Operating system and version

Windows 11 Pro ARM64, Build 28000

### Additional Information

**Suggested fix.** Retry through EGL when the native context API refuses, rather than requesting EGL unconditionally. A fallback costs nothing on systems that work today, and it fixes the GLX case in #4782 by the same path. I have opened a PR that does this.

Requesting EGL unconditionally on Windows would be the wrong shape: a physical Snapdragon device with Adreno drivers may well expose the WGL extension, and forcing EGL there would break a working configuration and require every application to ship ANGLE. A fallback only runs once the platform has already refused, so it cannot regress anything.

`glfw.ContextCreationAPI` and `glfw.EGLContextAPI` already exist in the GLFW binding Fyne depends on, and `egl_context.c` is compiled into its Windows build and looks for `libEGL.dll` by name. So no new dependency is involved, and bundling ANGLE becomes a working answer for applications once the hint can be reached.

**The limits of my evidence, stated plainly.** I have not been able to test on a physical Windows-on-ARM device.

- My own observation is from a Windows 11 ARM64 guest under QEMU TCG with **no GPU** (ramfb framebuffer only). That guest cannot distinguish a driver refusing a GLES context from the absence of any accelerated graphics stack.
- Independently, [netbirdio/netbird#4691](https://github.com/netbirdio/netbird/issues/4691) reports a shipping Fyne application failing on Windows 11 Pro ARM64 build 26100 under Parallels with `APIUnavailable: WGL: OpenGL ES requested but WGL_ARB_create_context_es2_profile is unavailable`. Parallels on Apple Silicon runs ARM64 natively, so the ARM code there is executing on real ARM hardware, though the GPU is still virtual.

So: two independent reports, neither on a physical Snapdragon. If a maintainer has such a device, the single question is whether a Fyne window opens on it at all.

The build-constraint finding is not subject to that caveat. It was read directly from v2.6.3 and holds regardless of any particular machine.

(For completeness, the extension names in the two error strings differ because of a quirk in GLFW itself: `wgl_context.c` checks for `WGL_EXT_create_context_es2_profile` but its error message says `ARB`. Same check.)

**Secondary, and I will open it separately if you prefer.** After the error is printed the process stays resident, with no window and no prompt returned to the console. The run loop appears to block with nothing to service. Since `NewWindow` returns no error, an application cannot detect this and exit cleanly on its own. A non-zero exit would let CI and scripted launches fail rather than hang.

fyne-io/fyne.title: MultipleWindows also overwrites OnDragged/OnResized set before a window is added
fyne-io/fyne.body:
### Describe the bug

While fixing #6433 (which is about `OnTappedBar` being unconditionally overwritten
by `MultipleWindows.setupChild()`), I noticed `InnerWindow.OnDragged` and
`InnerWindow.OnResized` have the exact same problem: `setupChild()` runs on every
`refreshChildren()` call (i.e. on `Add`, `RaiseToTop` and `Refresh`) and
unconditionally replaces both callbacks, so any handler set by the caller before
the window is shown inside a `MultipleWindows` is silently discarded — same
symptom as #6433, just for the other two callbacks.

### How to reproduce

```go
win1 := container.NewInnerWindow("inner window", container.New(layout.NewVBoxLayout()))
win1.OnDragged = func(ev *fyne.DragEvent) {
	fmt.Println("custom drag handling")
}

windows := container.NewMultipleWindows(win1) // does not itself trigger setup
w.SetContent(windows) // first render -> refreshChildren -> setupChild(win1)
                       // -> win1.OnDragged is now MultipleWindows' own handler only,
                       //    the custom callback set above is gone
```

### Additional Information

#6433 fixes this for `OnTappedBar` by wrapping the existing callback once (guarded
by a private flag on `InnerWindow` so repeated `Refresh()`/`Add()` calls don't
chain-wrap it) instead of unconditionally overwriting it. The same approach should
work for `OnDragged`/`OnResized`, kept out of that PR to keep it scoped to the
single reported symptom — see the discussion on #6433 for context.

labels.name: unverified

fyne-io/fyne.body: ### Checklist - [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://github.com/fyne-io/fyne/issues) for open issues that relate to the same problem, before opening a new one. - [x] This issue only relates to a single bug. I will open new issues for any other problems. ### Describe the bug When opening a window that contains a `widget.List` as its content, items are rendered with an incorrect (much larger) font size on startup. Moving the mouse cursor over a list item triggers a re-render that corrects the font and layout. On v2.7.4, the same code renders correctly on startup without any mouse interaction. This is similar to the previously fixed #645 ("Initial window display is blank on Gnome until hover or resize"), but that issue was resolved in 2020 and this appears to be a new regression in v2.8.0. ### How to reproduce 1. Save the example code below as `main.go` in a new directory 2. Initialize and build for v2.8.0: ``` go mod init fyne28test go get fyne.io/fyne/v2@v2.8.0 go mod tidy CGO_ENABLED=1 go build -o list-test-280 . ``` 3. Build for v2.7.4 (same directory): ``` go get fyne.io/fyne/v2@v2.7.4 go mod tidy CGO_ENABLED=1 go build -o list-test-274 . ``` 4. Run `./list-test-280` 5. Observe: items appear with an incorrect (much larger) font size 6. Move the mouse cursor over a list item — the font and layout correct themselves 7. Close the window, run `./list-test-274` 8. Observe: the list renders correctly on startup without any mouse interaction ### Screenshots ### Example code ```go package main import ( "fmt" "fyne.io/fyne/v2" "fyne.io/fyne/v2/app" "fyne.io/fyne/v2/widget" ) func main() { a := app.New() w := a.NewWindow("List font test") w.Resize(fyne.NewSize(400, 300)) data := make([]string, 20) for i := range data { data[i] = fmt.Sprintf("Item %d", i) } list := widget.NewList( func() int { return len(data) }, func() fyne.CanvasObject { return widget.NewLabel("template") }, func(id widget.ListItemID, obj fyne.CanvasObject) { obj.(*widget.Label).SetText(data[id]) }, ) w.SetContent(list) w.ShowAndRun() } ``` ### Fyne version v2.8.0 (works correctly on v2.7.4) ### Go compiler version go1.23.0 linux/amd64 ### Operating system and version Ubuntu-based (Pop!_OS), Linux 6.16.3, GNOME desktop, Wayland ### Additional Information The terminal prints the following warning on startup (not seen on v2.7.4): ``` *** This application has not been migrated to the fyne.Do threading model *** *** The next major Fyne release will remove this safety! *** *** Read more at https://docs.fyne.io/started/goroutines *** ``` Setting `fyneDo = true` in `FyneApp.toml` does not resolve the issue. The application does not use any goroutines for UI updates; all widget construction and `SetContent` happen on the main goroutine before `ShowAndRun`. In a more complex application where the `widget.List` is wrapped inside a custom focusable widget, the same underlying issue manifests as a completely blank list area (no items rendered at all) until hover. This suggests the initial layout/theme pass is incomplete, with the severity depending on the widget hierarchy.

When inserting something in a container using the `Add()` function, the size of the container doesn't get updated, so the `Layout()` function get a incorrect size for it.

```go
package main

import (
	"fmt"

	"fyne.io/fyne/v2"
	"fyne.io/fyne/v2/app"
	"fyne.io/fyne/v2/container"
	"fyne.io/fyne/v2/widget"
)

type diagonal struct {
}

func (d *diagonal) MinSize(objects []fyne.CanvasObject) fyne.Size {
	w, h := float32(0), float32(0)
	for _, o := range objects {
		childSize := o.MinSize()

		w += childSize.Width
		h += childSize.Height
	}
	return fyne.NewSize(w, h)
}

func (d *diagonal) Layout(objects []fyne.CanvasObject, containerSize fyne.Size) {
	pos := fyne.NewPos(0, containerSize.Height-d.MinSize(objects).Height)

	fmt.Println("Size:", containerSize) // Starts as {0 0}
	
	for idx, o := range objects {
		size := o.MinSize()
		o.Resize(size)
		o.Move(pos)
		
		fmt.Printf("Object %d: %v\n", idx, pos)
		pos = pos.Add(fyne.NewPos(size.Width, size.Height))
	}
}

func main() {
	a := app.New()
	w := a.NewWindow("Diagonal")

	text1 := widget.NewLabel("topleft")
	text2 := widget.NewLabel("Middle Label")
	text3 := widget.NewLabel("bottomright")

	diagonalContainer := container.New(&diagonal{}, text1, text2)
	diagonalContainer.Add(text3) // Calls layout() without defining containerSize

	w.SetContent(diagonalContainer) // Calls layout() again with a containerSize 
	w.ShowAndRun()
}
```

v2.8.0

go1.25.10

Adding a line `c.size = c.Layout.MinSize(c.Objects)` right before calling the layout in the implementation for `Add()` in `vendor/fyne.io/fyne/v2/container.go` seems to solve it.

fyne-io/fyne.title: Need a way to query for the current locale's text direction

milestone.title: "I" Release - late 2026
milestone.description:
* Text select / full edit for Rich Text
* Accessibility on by default
* List multi-select
* Background processes for mobile
* Sensor integration - Camera and Location
* Share menu

fyne-io/fyne.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://github.com/fyne-io/fyne/issues) for open issues that relate to the same feature, before opening a new one.
- [x] This issue only relates to a single feature. I will open new issues for any other features.

### Is your feature request related to a problem?

I need to be able to query for text direction given the current user's locale, to express visual hierarchy in a way that is intuitive to the user. I know that RTL text support is ongoing, based on #90 being in an open state, so this might already be in the works and just not released yet.

I'm opening a separate issue because this isn't specifically about text layout, but more general visual layout that is informed by text direction. The specific use-case in mind is using the [CustomPaddedLayout](https://docs.fyne.io/api/v2/layout/custompaddedlayout/) to indent a set of elements to show a visual hierarchy. In that case, text direction dictates to which side that padding should be applied to conform to reader expectations.

### Is it possible to construct a solution with the existing API?

It's possible to get the current locale string, but Fyne doesn't provide a means to query the text direction that locale implies. The solution remaining is for the application to maintain a set of `Locale` (base) strings for known/supported RTL languages, and check against that. It seems like this is something that will already be needed internally for RTL support in Fyne, so I wanted to bring it up as an additional facet of a planned feature set so applications can react to it when making layout choices outside of text layout too.

### Describe the solution you'd like to see.

It seems like there are at least a couple different solutions. The preferred solution would be adding a method to `Locale` that returns an enum value indicating text direction. This would encourage a consistent source for locale dependent decisions and seems consistent with existing conventions.

Looking at [x/text/unicode/bidi](https://pkg.go.dev/golang.org/x/text@v0.40.0/unicode/bidi#Direction) for prior representation, it looks like `LeftToRight` and `RightToLeft` are defined, and a couple more that are dependent on a given text string. Since the expected text direction for a given `Locale` isn't dependent on specific text, it makes the most sense to me - for this case - to just define `LeftToRight` and `RightToLeft`. It looks like these values could live alongside the other text enums (`TextAlign`, `TextTruncation`, `TextWrap`) as a new `TextDirection` type in the base `fyne` package for ease of discovery without risk of import cycles.

Since mixed direction support is called out in the RTL support issue, it seems like there are at least two distinct cases for understanding text direction: locale default direction and text dependent direction. This might lead us to conclude that a single type should describe both cases, but I think that could lead to some ambiguity/confusion about the range of values that a method like `Locale.TextDirection()` could return. It seems like this is a case where the answer depends on the specific question being asked, and it might be better to express these concepts separately as distinct enums. Maybe something like `TextDirection` and `TextLocaleDirection` to be clear about what is being described. The former could describe text direction derived from text, while the latter could be the expected text direction derived from the Locale.

fyne-io/fyne.title: Disabled button does not fade emoji (bitmap glyph) text content
fyne-io/fyne.body:
### Context

Spun off from #6217 — that issue mixed two related problems:

1. **PNG/bitmap icon resource on a disabled button is not faded** — being addressed in #6381.
2. **Emoji glyphs in disabled button text are not faded** — this issue.

### Describe the bug

A button whose text is an emoji (e.g. `🔝`) stays at full brightness when disabled. Regular text glyphs and Unicode triangle (`▲`) get colored with `theme.ColorNameDisabled` correctly, but emoji is rasterised by the font fallback (see comment from @andydotxyz on #6217) so it doesn't honor the text color.

### How to reproduce

```go
package main

import (
    "fyne.io/fyne/v2/app"
    "fyne.io/fyne/v2/container"
    "fyne.io/fyne/v2/widget"
)

func main() {
    a := app.New()
    w := a.NewWindow("Disable test")

    btn1 := widget.NewButton("🔝", nil)
    btn2 := widget.NewButton("▲", nil)

    btn1.Disable()
    btn2.Disable()

    w.SetContent(container.NewHBox(btn1, btn2))
    w.ShowAndRun()
}
```

`btn2` (`▲`) appears grayed out, `btn1` (`🔝`) does not.

### Why this needs a separate PR

The fix lives in the text/painter pipeline rather than the button renderer: emoji glyphs are drawn through the emoji font fallback in `internal/painter/font.go`, and a fade or grayscale would need to be propagated from the parent disabled state into the painter. The bitmap-icon fix in #6381 only covers `Button.Icon` and explicitly leaves this part out of scope.

### Fyne version

develop branch (as of #6381).

### Checklist

- [x] This issue only relates to a single bug. I will open new issues for any other problems.

### Describe the bug

Fyne applications on Windows become intermittently unresponsive when resizing the window by dragging from the corners or edges.

In the Fyne demo code, it is enough to replace the split box in main with two simple labels to cause this behaviour:
`split := container.NewHSplit(widget.NewLabel("left"), widget.NewLabel("right"))`

I am unsure why the normal demo code doesn't do this - I would think more widgets needing to be redrawn in the window would cause greater impacts, but it seems to get worse the fewer things there are that need redrawing. 

For example, changing only the 'tutorial' content to a label causes this behaviour, but to a lesser extent than the first example:
`split := container.NewHSplit(makeNav(setTutorial, true), widget.NewLabel("right"))`

This issue has existed for several prior versions of Fyne but has now become a major hindrance.

### How to reproduce

1. Start an arbitrary Fyne application on Windows
2. Attempt to resize the window by dragging from the corners or edges

### Screenshots

N/A

### Example code

```go
package main
```

fyne-io/fyne.title: Wayland: canvas keeps stale layout after window auto-expands for content min-size change

fyne-io/fyne.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://github.com/fyne-io/fyne/issues) for open issues that relate to the same problem, before opening a new one.
- [x] This issue only relates to a single bug. I will open new issues for any other problems.

### Describe the bug

On native Wayland (-tags wayland), when a widget's min size grows so the window auto-expands to fit it, and the min size later shrinks back (e.g. a button label temporarily becomes longer), the window snaps back to its previous width but the canvas keeps the expanded layout. Everything anchored to the right edge is cropped/clipped until the user manually resizes the window, which instantly fixes it. Does not reproduce on X11/XWayland.

### How to reproduce

see example code

### Screenshots

_No response_

### Example code

```go
package main

import (
      "time"

      "fyne.io/fyne/v2"
      "fyne.io/fyne/v2/app"
      "fyne.io/fyne/v2/widget"
)

func main() {
      a := app.New()
      w := a.NewWindow("Stale layout after auto-expand")

      btn := widget.NewButton("Play Button", nil)
      w.SetContent(btn)

      time.AfterFunc(2*time.Second, func() {
              fyne.Do(func() { btn.SetText("A temporarily much longer button label") })
      })
      time.AfterFunc(4*time.Second, func() {
              fyne.Do(func() { btn.SetText("Play Button") })
      })

      w.ShowAndRun()
}
```

fyne-io/fyne.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://github.com/fyne-io/fyne/issues) for open issues that relate to the same feature, before opening a new one.
- [x] This issue only relates to a single feature. I will open new issues for any other features.

### Is your feature request related to a problem?

I believe so. When I create a `*widget.RichText` from markdown and put it in a `*layout.Stack` with word wrapping and vertical scrolling turned on I would expect there to be some hook-in point for me to `PgUp`/`PgDown` or use arrow keys to scroll. I have searched existing issues and it seems at first glance that this is possible. @andydotxyz has mentioned listening for keypress on the canvas. Okay. No problem, I am doing that for other things already. The key-press isn't the issue: as best as I can tell `*widget.RichText` does not expose any ability to control scrolling (while collection items have `ScrollTo()` and friends).

### Is it possible to construct a solution with the existing API?

Not to my knowledge. I have searched the api docs and done a lot of object printing looking for something to do this. So, I think no. Not without changes that add scrolling receivers to `widget.RichText` that mimic those available to collections objects.

### Describe the solution you'd like to see.

I am writing an ebook reader. I would like to be able to listen on the window's canvas for key presses and respond to those by scrolling the `widget.RichText` containing the book chapter's content. This would likely look something like `ScrollToEnd`, `ScrollToBeginning`, and some form of smaller scoll incrementation along with something to report scroll position and prevent overscroll/out of bound for object.

### Describe the bug

Using a scroll bar on Android is so difficult that I first thought the scrollbar was only meant as a visual feedback for dragging the canvas.

Of course, the obvious solution is to make the scrollbar wider. In my app, I have set `SizeNameScrollBar` and `SizeNameScrollBarSmall` both to 20 using a custom theme.

This issue isn't about changing the default sizes but about increasing the scrollbar's "touchable" area. By default (when the scrollbar isn't being used), it is drawn as wide as set in `theme.SizeNameScrollBarSmall`. When scrolling, it's drawn as wide as the larger `theme.SizeNameScrollBar`. But for grabbing the scrollbar, the smaller size counts.

I'm proposing to make the "touchable" area as wide as `theme.SizeNameScrollBar`. This way, scrollbars could be easier to hit while not being visually intrusive.

### How to reproduce

Try any Fyne an Android with a scrollbar.

fyne-io/fyne.title: Mouse wheel scrolling disabled when the pointer is over a sticky column in widget.Table

labels.name: unverified
labels.description: A bug that has been reported but not verified

fyne-io/fyne.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://github.com/fyne-io/fyne/issues) for open issues that relate to the same problem, before opening a new one.
- [x] This issue only relates to a single bug. I will open new issues for any other problems.

### Describe the bug

Mouse wheel scrolling does not work when the pointer is over a sticky (pinned) column in `widget.Table`. The internal clip type used for the sticky column area embeds `widget.Scroll` with `Direction = ScrollNone`, which causes `Scrolled()` to silently discard scroll events instead of forwarding them to the table's main content scroller.

This is inconsistent with how drag events are handled: `clip.Dragged` already forwards to `t.Dragged`, but there is no corresponding `Scrolled` override.

### How to reproduce

1. Create a `widget.Table` with `StickyColumnCount >= 1`
2. Populate it with enough rows to require vertical scrolling
3. Hover the mouse over one of the sticky columns
4. Scroll the mouse wheel: nothing happens
5. Move the pointer to a non-sticky column: scrolling works normally


### Screenshots

_No response_

### Example code

```go
package main

import (
	"fmt"

	"fyne.io/fyne/v2"
	"fyne.io/fyne/v2/app"
	"fyne.io/fyne/v2/widget"
)

func main() {
	a := app.New()
	w := a.NewWindow("Sticky Scroll Bug")
	w.Resize(fyne.NewSize(400, 300))

	t := widget.NewTable(
		func() (int, int) { return 100, 5 },
		func() fyne.CanvasObject { return widget.NewLabel("R0 C0") },
		func(id widget.TableCellID, o fyne.CanvasObject) {
			o.(*widget.Label).SetText(fmt.Sprintf("R%d C%d", id.Row, id.Col))
		},
	)
	t.StickyColumnCount = 2

	w.SetContent(t)
	w.ShowAndRun()
}
```

### Fyne version

2.7.1

### Go compiler version

1.24.1

### Operating system and version

macOS 15.5 (Darwin 24.6.0), arm64

### Additional Information

The fix would be a one-line addition to the `clip` type in widget/table.go:

```go
func (c *clip) Scrolled(ev *fyne.ScrollEvent) {
	c.t.content.Scrolled(ev)
}
```

This mirrors the existing pattern where `clip.Dragged` forwards to `t.Dragged`. The same issue likely affects StickyRowCount (the top clip) and the corner clip.

### Describe the bug

Somehow this slipped through the net...

Mobile contexts (Android, AndroidWindow and Unknown (should add an iOSWindow one, am looking at that)) use a pointer context.

Desktop contexts (MacWindow, WindowsWindow, X11Window, WaylandWindow) use non-pointer values EXCEPT the non-window version which is *UnknownContext

### How to reproduce

Try to switch the context in RunNativeWindow and see what types are passed in between desktop and mobile.

### Screenshots

_No response_

### Example code

```go
nw.RunNative(func(ctx any) {
		switch c := ctx.(type) {
		case driver.MacWindowContext:
			web = doMacThing(c)
		case driver.WindowsWindowContext:
			web = doWindowsThing(c)
		case driver.X11WindowContext:
			web = doX11Thing(c)
		case *driver.AndroidWindowContext:
			web = doAndroidThing(c)
		default:
			err = fmt.Errorf("unexpected context type: %T\n", ctx)
		}
	})
```

### Fyne version

2.7.3

1.21

any

I feel we should fix this but I cannot think of a way to do it without a (small?) break...

fyne-io/fyne.title: Button styles Elevated and Outlined
fyne-io/fyne.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://github.com/fyne-io/fyne/issues) for open issues that relate to the same feature, before opening a new one.
- [x] This issue only relates to a single feature. I will open new issues for any other features.

### Is your feature request related to a problem?

Currently, Fyne's Button widget supports three main levels of importance (High, Medium, and Low), which map to Material Design's Filled, Filled Tonal, and Text buttons. However, Material Design describes 5 distinct styles. Specifically, Elevated and Outlined buttons are missing as built-in options.

### Is it possible to construct a solution with the existing API?

Achieving an Outlined button is possible with a custom widget however shadowed Elevated button with rounded corners is not possible.

### Describe the solution you'd like to see.

New `Importance` options along with new Theme Variables (e.g., `OutlineColor`, `OutlineWidth`) for `Elevated` and `Outlined` styles so users can customize these styles globally across their apps. Both styles may also apply to other widgets like cards.

fyne-io/fyne.title: Proposal: UX/A11y - Make widget/Entry select all text when tabbed into
fyne-io/fyne.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://github.com/fyne-io/fyne/issues) for open issues that relate to the same feature, before opening a new one.
- [x] This issue only relates to a single feature. I will open new issues for any other features.

### Is your feature request related to a problem?

Currently, when tabbing through multiple fyne widget.Entry form fields, text of active entry will not be selected. In contrast to (most? all?) web browsers - they will select the content when tabbing from one `<input type="text">` field to the next; users might be used to this behavior and it's probably more efficient.

HTML form example that displays said behavior:
```html
<form>
  <input type="text"> 
  <input type="text" value="test 123">
  <input type="text">
  <textarea>Foo bar</textarea>
</form>
```

### Is it possible to construct a solution with the existing API?

I don't think that it's currently possible, as there are no public Entry methods to e.g. SelectAllText().

### Describe the solution you'd like to see.

It would possibly be a rather small change in the FocusGained() method:
https://github.com/fyne-io/fyne/blob/5a3f552118ca92f5ba6b96e9edb9789e6bf0eef6/widget/entry.go#L304
```go
	if !e.MultiLine {
		e.sel.selecting = true
		e.sel.selectCurrentRow(true)
	}
```
This would keep behavior consistent with browsers, who also do not select textarea contents on focus.
It seemingly doesn't interfere with e.g. mouse clicking into an Entry -- no selection happening.

If enabling this by default is not desired, having a bool toggle on the Entry widget would be great, too.

### Describe the bug

I have a accordion in a VScroll container.
There are problems when items open and size changes (one item contains a tree in a HSplit)



### How to reproduce

I have a accordion in a VScroll container.
There are problems when items open and size changes (one item contains a tree in a HSplit)


### Screenshots

_No response_

### Example code

Here my fix (ugly):
```go
func fixScroll(scroll *container.Scroll) {
	go func() {
		var oldSize fyne.Size
		for {
			time.Sleep(100 * time.Millisecond)
			fyne.Do(func() {
				c := scroll.Content
				if c != nil {
					ms := c.MinSize()
					if oldSize != ms {
						c.Resize(ms)
						scroll.Refresh()
						oldSize = ms
					}
				}
			})
		}
	}()
}
```


### Fyne version

2.7.1

### Go compiler version

1.25.5

### Operating system and version

Linux Mint

### Additional Information

It would be nice that this will be done internally.
Or the is an OnChange in Accordion - so we get notification when an item opens - so we can do it manually.

I will open new issues for any other features. ### Is your feature request related to a problem? I'm making an app that includes an HSV range picker via (lightly modified) slider widgets. It allows selecting min/max Hue, Saturation, and Value. This ends up requiring six widgets because I need separate sliders for each axis. While this does work, it's frustrating to need so much vertical space to allow selecting a range of values. Compare to a similar widget in Davinci Resolve: Obviously that's much more complex than what I'm asking for - all I want is the ability to set a lower and upper bound with a single slider. ### Is it possible to construct a solution with the existing API? Theoretically, I think it should be possible to do by writing a fully custom widget. I don't think extending Slider with a custom renderer would be sufficient, because the base implementation has baked-in assumptions about how many values it sets (1) hard-coded into private methods, binding logic, etc. (which probably don't make sense to try to make more generic IMO.) I think it could be valuable to include as a default widget. ### Describe the solution you'd like to see. I want to be able to set lower and upper bounds with a single slider. Visually, this would look like: Usage would be something like: ```golang min := float64(0) max := float64(255) // basic range slider widget.NewRangeSlider(min, max) // bound lower := binding.NewFloat() upper := binding.NewFloat() widget.NewRangeSliderWithData(min, max, lower, upper) ```

fyne-io/fyne.title: lang: unable to translate "description"
fyne-io/fyne.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://github.com/fyne-io/fyne/issues) for open issues that relate to the same problem, before opening a new one.
- [x] This issue only relates to a single bug. I will open new issues for any other problems.

### Describe the bug

When my translation file `ru.json` contains the key "Description", loading translations fails with the error:

```
Failed to load translations reserved keys [Description] mixed with unreserved keys [Name Type]
```

Looking at the source, it seems like the error is generated by `i18n.isMessage` which reserves quite a number of regular words like "description", "hash", "one", "two", "many" and some more.

The documentation does not mention this limitation. Internally these seem to be related to some "messages" but those are not documented either.

IMO a translation file should not have any limitations on what can be a key.

### How to reproduce

1. Build the program shown in the Example code.
2. Put `en.json` from Example code in the same directory.
3. Run the program.

### Screenshots

_No response_

### Example code

main.go
```go
package main

import (
        "log"

        "fyne.io/fyne/v2"
        "fyne.io/fyne/v2/lang"
)

func main() {
        res, err := fyne.LoadResourceFromPath("en.json")
        if err != nil {
                log.Panic(err)
        }
        err = lang.AddTranslations(res)
        if err != nil {
                log.Panic(err)
        }
        log.Print("success")
}
```

en.json
```json
{
  "description": "abcd",
  "hello": "hi"
}
```

Output on my machine:
```
panic: reserved keys [description] mixed with unreserved keys [hello]
```

fyne-io/fyne.title: Focus events cause multiline entry to change scroll position to show cursor

labels.name: unverified
labels.description: A bug that has been reported but not verified

fyne-io/fyne.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://github.com/fyne-io/fyne/issues) for open issues that relate to the same problem, before opening a new one.
- [x] This issue only relates to a single bug. I will open new issues for any other problems.

### Describe the bug

If a multiline entry has enough text for a scrollbar to appear, whenever this entry gains or loses focus the widget automatically scrolls the text so that the cursor position is visible. Typically this behavior is very far from user's expectation. The entry should automatically scroll to the cursor position only when something happens at the cursor (e.g., user inputs something or changes the cursor position with arrow keys).

Example scenario: user has edited some part of the text in the multiline entry and wants to edit something below. User scrolls to see the location of the next planned edit. However, before clicking there, user does something with other widgets in the window (imagine clicking on the `save` icon, for example). At this moment, the entry scrolls back to the location of the first edit, to user's annoyance.

I have provided a toy example of this scenario below. However, the same issue can appear in other scenarios. For example, the scrolling to the cursor position also happens when the entry _gains_ focus. This leads to very inconvenient behavior when user scrolls a currently _unfocused_ multiline entry to find the place for a next edit, then clicks there expecting the cursor to jump to that position, but at this moment the entry scrolls back to the _previous_ cursor position and the click lands at an unexpected position.

### How to reproduce

1. Run the code fragment below. If necessary, shrink the window so that the text in the multiline entry on the right can be scrolled.
2. Put cursor somewhere in the first paragraph in the multiline entry.
3. Without changing the cursor position, scroll the text downwards (via mouse wheel or equivalent). It's easiest to see the bug effect when scrolled to the very end.
4. Click on the left-side entry.
5. Observe that the multiline entry has jumped back to the cursor position.

### Screenshots

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c155c01d-9262-4299-9e2d-696a83f63612

### Example code

(This example is AI generated, but works OK)

```go
package main

import (
	"fyne.io/fyne/v2"
	"fyne.io/fyne/v2/app"
	"fyne.io/fyne/v2/container"
	"fyne.io/fyne/v2/widget"
)

func main() {
	myApp := app.New()
	myWindow := myApp.NewWindow("Fyne Bug Demo")
	myWindow.Resize(fyne.NewSize(800, 600))

	// Left side: single line text entry
	leftEntry := widget.NewEntry()
	leftEntry.SetPlaceHolder("Enter text here...")

	// Right side: multiline text entry
	rightEntry := widget.NewMultiLineEntry()
	rightEntry.SetText(generateFixedText())
	rightEntry.Wrapping = fyne.TextWrapWord

	// Create horizontal split container
	split := container.NewHSplit(
		leftEntry,
		rightEntry,
	)
	split.Offset = 0.3 // 30% left, 70% right

	myWindow.SetContent(split)
	myWindow.ShowAndRun()
}

func rotText(s string, n int) string {
	runes := []rune(s)
	for i, r := range runes {
		switch {
		case r >= 'A' && r <= 'Z':
			runes[i] = 'A' + (r-'A'+rune(n))%26
		case r >= 'a' && r <= 'z':
			runes[i] = 'a' + (r-'a'+rune(n))%26
		}
	}
	return string(runes)
}

func generateFixedText() string {
	fragment := "Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipiscing elit. Sed do eiusmod tempor incididunt ut labore et dolore magna aliqua.\n" +
		"Ut enim ad minim veniam, quis nostrud exercitation ullamco laboris nisi ut aliquip ex ea commodo consequat. Duis aute irure " +
		"dolor in reprehenderit in voluptate velit esse cillum dolore eu fugiat nulla pariatur.\n\n"

	text := fragment
	text += rotText(fragment, 4)
	text += rotText(fragment, 8)
	text += rotText(fragment, 12)
	text += rotText(fragment, 16)

	return text
}
```

### Fyne version

2.7.1

### Go compiler version

1.19

### Operating system and version

Pop OS 22.04

### Additional Information

_No response_
