### Describe the bug

When using the fyne cli to package an application for Linux the StartupWMClass specified under [LinuxAndBSD] is removed, regardless of how it is configured.

This results in the window icon in the dock being the default one. (on Ubuntu at least)

### How to reproduce

1. Create a FyneApp.toml containing a StartUpWMClass entry, for example:
[LinuxAndBSD]
GenericName = "Test"
StartupWMClass = "Test Window"

2.  Run "fyne package -os linux -icon icon.png"
3. StartupWMClass is removed from toml and not present in resulting .desktop file

### Screenshots

_No response_

### Example code

```go
func main() {
	a := app.NewWithID("test")
	w := a.NewWindow("Test Window")

	logText := widget.NewLabel("")
	logText.Wrapping = fyne.TextWrapBreak
	logScrollContainer := container.NewScroll(logText)

	w.SetContent(logScrollContainer)
	w.Resize(fyne.NewSize(500, 400))
	w.Hide()

	if desk, ok := a.(desktop.App); ok {
		iconResource := fyne.NewStaticResource("app-icon.png", embeddedIcon)
		desk.SetSystemTrayIcon(iconResource)

		m := fyne.NewMenu("Menu",
			fyne.NewMenuItem("Quit", func() {
				a.Quit()
			}),
		)
		desk.SetSystemTrayMenu(m)

		w.SetCloseIntercept(func() {
			w.Hide()
		})
	}

	a.Run()
}

```

go1.25.3

Running Ubuntu on wayland so maybe related to https://github.com/fyne-io/fyne/issues/5983. Regardless, adding the StartUpWMClass to the .desktop file resolves the issues of the icon not showing only on the window and fyne should respect the [LinuxAndBSD] properties added.

fyne-io/fyne.title: Support removing, or overriding builtin application shortcuts
fyne-io/fyne.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://github.com/fyne-io/fyne/issues) for open issues that relate to the same feature, before opening a new one.
- [x] This issue only relates to a single feature. I will open new issues for any other features.

### Is your feature request related to a problem?

# Request

Allow developers control over application shortcuts rather than have them hard-coded into the driver.

I've no issue with Fyne setting sensible and common defaults, but as a developer who wants control over what my application does (and in this case, actually needs that control), I'd like to be able to override (or remove entirely) the baked in shortcut handling found in the driver.

# Background

Due to some (probably fairly unique) requirements of an application I'm writing using Fyne, I require that the `Shift + Insert` is *not* interpreted as a `^V` (PasteShortcut) at the driver level. The program is a terminal emulator targeted at running a single piece of terminal based software, that software needs to handle `^V` it self as it's a built-in shortcut for a special menu, and we want `Shift + Insert` to behave as normal paste.

I didn't realise what the Fyne driver was doing and spent considerable time trying to work out why my registered shortcut handler for "Shift + Insert" wasn't working, or indeed why the key event wasn't even triggering for it.

A PR related to this has been opened (https://github.com/fyne-io/fyne/pull/6001/files) which would allow me to write the behaviour I want, the code would be a little weird looking.

# See Also

https://github.com/fyne-io/terminal/issues/134

### Is it possible to construct a solution with the existing API?

No

### Describe the solution you'd like to see.

A shortcut manager that can override the driver defaults when a developer wants/needs to, or remove a defined shortcut entirely.

fyne-io/fyne.body:

- [x] This issue only relates to a single feature. I will open new issues for any other features.

### Is your feature request related to a problem?

Fyne currently doesn't support the XDG Desktop Portal FileTransfer mechanism for drag-and-drop operations in sandboxed environments (like Flatpak). This prevents applications from receiving files via drag-and-drop when running in Flatpak.

According to the [XDG Desktop Portal FileTransfer specification](https://flatpak.github.io/xdg-desktop-portal/docs/doc-org.freedesktop.portal.FileTransfer.html), 

> toolkits are expected to use the `application/vnd.portal.filetransfer` MIME type when using this mechanism for file exchange via copy-paste or drag-and-drop.

Thanks,
Alex

### Is it possible to construct a solution with the existing API?

_No response_

### Describe the solution you'd like to see.

From a quick investigation the implementation would need to:

1. **Detect FileTransfer MIME type** in drag-and-drop events
2. **Extract transfer key** from the drag data
3. **Call FileTransfer portal** to retrieve actual file paths
4. **Convert retrieved paths** to Fyne URIs for the application

I will open new issues for any other problems. ### Describe the bug When I build and install the example bellow with : `fyne package -os android -app-id Fyne.MyApp -icon ./icon.png && adb install ./MyApp.apk` On my mobile (Pixel 6a), the scroll is unusable. But the same code builded on desktop works fine. I believe the lag is propotionnal to the size of the list. If there are more widgets, there is more lag. I dig up few informations with `go tool pprof` : The CPU profile on desktop : (`go tool pprof -png http://localhost:6060/debug/pprof/profile?seconds=10 > cpu_desktop.png `) The CPU profile on mobile : (`go tool pprof -png http://${ip}:6060/debug/pprof/profile?seconds=10 > cpu_mobile.png `) If I understand correctly, there is a bottleneck on the `runtime.futex` only on mobile that creates the lag. What I don't know is, does that bottleneck created by the Fyne runtime (wrong use of that futex) or does the futex is bugged on ARM ? If it's the second case, I would glady open an issue on the Go project but I would like an hand to be sure about that. Does anyone familliar with the Fyne runtime can confirm that ? I'm more incline to believe it's the futex because when I pprof the futex on the mobile I get that : ``` $ go tool pprof http://${ip}:6060/debug/pprof/profile?seconds=10 (pprof) list futex Total: 12.12s ROUTINE ======================== runtime.futex in /usr/lib/go/src/runtime/sys_linux_arm64.s 4.97s 4.97s (flat, cum) 41.01% of Total . . 643:TEXT runtime·futex(SB),NOSPLIT|NOFRAME,$0 . . 644: MOVD addr+0(FP), R0 . . 645: MOVW op+8(FP), R1 . . 646: MOVW val+12(FP), R2 . . 647: MOVD ts+16(FP), R3 . . 648: MOVD addr2+24(FP), R4 . . 649: MOVW val3+32(FP), R5 . . 650: MOVD $SYS_futex, R8 . . 651: SVC 4.97s 4.97s 652: MOVW R0, ret+40(FP) . . 653: RET . . 654: . . 655:// int64 clone(int32 flags, void *stk, M *mp, G *gp, void (*fn)(void)); . . 656:TEXT runtime·clone(SB),NOSPLIT|NOFRAME,$0 . . 657: MOVW flags+0(FP), R0 ``` IMO (but I'm no ASM expert) it's very strange that only the `MOVW` take that long. If I understand correctly (again), on a 10s session, ~5s is spend on a `MOVW` not all the futex, just the `MOVW` in that futex. If the futex was very intensly used, I believe other instructions would have longer times but it's only this instruction that is slow. Once again, feel free to correct me. This issue is blocking my projet for now 😞 ### How to reproduce Build the example bellow on mobile. ### Screenshots _No response_ ### Example code ``` package main import ( // "log" // "net/http" // _ "net/http/pprof" "strconv" "fyne.io/fyne/v2" "fyne.io/fyne/v2/app" "fyne.io/fyne/v2/container" "fyne.io/fyne/v2/widget" ) func main() { // go func() { // log.Println(http.ListenAndServe(":6060", nil)) // }() a := app.NewWithID(`MyApp`) w := a.NewWindow(`MyApp`) w.SetContent(newHome()) w.Show() a.Run() } func newHome() fyne.CanvasObject { d := make([]fyne.CanvasObject, 0, 300) for c := range 300 { d = append(d, widget.NewButton(`Test` + strconv.Itoa(c), nil)) } g := container.NewGridWithColumns(1, d...) v := container.NewVScroll(g) return v } ``` ### Fyne version cli: v1.6.1 library: v2.6.2 ### Go compiler version 1.24.6 ### Operating system and version Manjaro Linux with kernel 6.12.41-1 ### May be related #1062

milestone.title: "I" Release - late 2026
milestone.description:

fyne-io/fyne.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://github.com/fyne-io/fyne/issues) for open issues that relate to the same feature, before opening a new one.
- [x] This issue only relates to a single feature. I will open new issues for any other features.

### Is your feature request related to a problem?

I ran into this problem I never had with other GUI toolkits and makes for unnecessary complication of an otherwise simple operation.

In my app I needed to _temporarily_ disable a top-level menu (`*fyne.Menu`) attached to a main menu (`*fyne.MainMenu`). This top-level menu obviously has several (child) menu items (`*fyne.Menuitem`).

To my surprise, there was no way to do it, even what AI suggested and then stood corrected by me LOL. 

**Workaround:**

Programmatically iterate over all MenuItems of the **top-level** menu and disable them to make the top-level inoperable. While this works in some situations, it is not a proper way to do it.

**Issue**

The issue is two-fold. First, what would otherwise be a single statement like `Actions.Disable()` becomes a loop in which we must find and disable each of the _subitems_. Later, we have to do the same to enable them.

The other consequence it that assuming all child `MenuItem`s are the same is too simplistic. `MenuItem`s are usually tied by cause-effect to other widgets in the GUI app that may require to individually enable/disable menu items of a top-level menu without affecting the others. 

In case I did not make myself clear, imagine you had worked around it by disabling ALL child menu items. Then when you want to _re-enable_ a top-level, you want to retain the disabled state of those child menu items that were (and still need to be) disabled. This is currently not possible unless the programmer spends extra time (and memory) keeping track of their status at the moment they got disabled. 

### Is it possible to construct a solution with the existing API?

The workaround covers only a simplistic use case in which all children follow the parent's state. But unless extra administration code is added, it does not fulfill situations in which the children have their own state management.

In other words, it is a half workaround.

### Describe the solution you'd like to see.

- Disabling the `*fyne.Menu` top-level menu would make it greyed out (disabled) without the need to iterate through its `*fyne.MenuItem` children. Disabling the top-level effectively makes the children invisible because the top-level menu cannot be clicked.
- When enabling `*fyne.Menu` again (clickable) all its `*fyne.MenuItem` children retain their current Enabled/Disable state; therefore, some may appear enabled, some may appear disabled depending on application logic.

Thus, simply adding a `Disable()/Enable()` method or property on the `*fyne.Menu` would achieve the desired solution (as done in other toolkits) without adding complicated code that may be prone to errors.

As usual, the idea is to make it easier for programmers to concentrate on conforming to the application workflow by simple means, rather than requiring them to over-and-over-again be in the necessity of writing extra code. In other words, simplicity.

```go
type DatePickerNillable struct {
	widget.DateEntry
	Validator fyne.StringValidator
}

func NewDatePickerNillable(bind **time.Time) *DatePickerNillable {
	dp := &DatePickerNillable{}
	dp.ExtendBaseWidget(dp)
	dp.Wrapping = fyne.TextWrap(fyne.TextTruncateClip)

	dp.SetDate(*bind)

	dp.Validator = func(s string) error {
		fmt.Println("My custom vlaidator is being executed")
		if s == "" {
			return nil
		}
		if dp.DateEntry.Validator != nil {
			return dp.DateEntry.Validator(s)
```

```go
	}

func NewNumberKeyboardEntry() *numberKeyboardEntry {
	e := &numberKeyboardEntry{}
	e.Wrapping = fyne.TextWrap(fyne.TextTruncateClip)
	e.ExtendBaseWidget(e)
	return e
}

func main() {
	app := app.New()
	window := app.NewWindow("Bugtest - Mobile NumberKeyboard Entry")
	window.SetPadded(false)
	window.Resize(fyne.NewSize(500, 600))
	window.CenterOnScreen()

	onSubmitted := func(s string) {
		dialog.ShowInformation("Typed", s, window)
	}

	nk := NewNumberKeyboardEntry()
	nk.OnSubmitted = onSubmitted
	numkey := widget.NewFormItem("NumberKeyboard", nk)

	ee := widget.NewEntry()
	ee.OnSubmitted = onSubmitted
	norkey := widget.NewFormItem("Normal", ee)

	nk2 := fx.NewNumericalEntry()
	nk2.OnSubmitted = onSubmitted
	nk2.AllowFloat = true
	nk2.AllowNegative = true
	numkey2 := widget.NewFormItem("FyneX Numkey", nk2)

	window.SetContent(widget.NewForm(numkey, norkey, numkey2))
	window.ShowAndRun()
}
```

fyne-io/fyne.title: Support Data Binding in Widgets Defined Outside of fyne
fyne-io/fyne.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://github.com/fyne-io/fyne/issues) for open issues that relate to the same feature, before opening a new one.
- [x] This issue only relates to a single feature. I will open new issues for any other features.

### Is your feature request related to a problem?

fyne provides functionality to bind data values to widgets that are defined in fyne. However, the binder struct required for this (widget.basicBinder) is not exported from the fyne widget package. Therefore, it is not possible to add binding to widgets that are defined external to the fyne widget package (for example, in fyne-x, or in user-developed code).
It is possible to add binding, but only by copying code from fyne. (i.e. copying `widget/binder_helper.go` to whatever package contains the new widget.)

Issue #2836 requests binding for both the selected value and the list of option strings. Select.Bind and Select.Unbind were added in fyne version 2.6. One suggestion in the discussion for that issue is to extend the Select widget in fyne-x to add BindOptions and UnbindOptions methods. This is only possible once a binding mechanism is available outside of fyne.

### Is it possible to construct a solution with the existing API?

I am not aware of any way to construct a solution using the existing API.

### Describe the solution you'd like to see.

One solution would be to export the basicBinder struct (i.e. rename it to BasicBinder). There are 14 places in fyne where renaming basicBinder to BasicBinder would be required, including in one comment.

fyne-io/fyne.title: Rework tab containers to handle refresh in a better way

labels.name: optimization
labels.description: Tickets that could help Fyne apps run faster

fyne-io/fyne.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://github.com/fyne-io/fyne/issues) for open issues that relate to the same feature, before opening a new one.
- [x] This issue only relates to a single feature. I will open new issues for any other features.

### Is your feature request related to a problem?

The tab containers create their renderers but then set a lot of state and then refresh. Given that the widget is refreshed automatically when first shown, much of this work is unnecessary and just create unnecessary overhead. We ought to refactor as much of this code to be computed dynamically without relying on initial set up state.

The second problem is that most of the refresh updates seem to come from the layout function and not the  refresh function. This is a bit counter intuitive to how widgets should work and I believe we might even be refreshing stuff twice.

I generally find that the tab containers are hard to follow what they are doing in the code. A large refactor might be necessary to make it more understandable.

I handled the low hanging fruit, but had lack of time and got a bit lost in weird test failures locally, in https://github.com/fyne-io/fyne/pull/5846 but there is more to be done.

### Is it possible to construct a solution with the existing API?

I think so yes. We might need to rework tests which assume things incorrectly.

### Describe the solution you'd like to see.

I would like the code to be refactored to be be cleaner and more in line with that we expect from widgets. Renders should only set up the minimum required state and not do any refreshes. The layout updates should only move and positions things, not refresh.

fyne-io/fyne.title: Widgets should not use cache.Renderer

labels.name: optimization
labels.description: Tickets that could help Fyne apps run faster

fyne-io/fyne.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://github.com/fyne-io/fyne/issues) for open issues that relate to the same feature, before opening a new one.
- [x] This issue only relates to a single feature. I will open new issues for any other features.

### Is your feature request related to a problem?

Per discussion with @dweymouth on Discord, we should make sure to update all of the widgets to not rely on `cache.Renderer()` from the internal packages. This breaks the model we have where a widget should not reference it's renderer and is bad practice as it makes it hard to replicate the same function outside of this repository (given that it depends on internal details from the renderer cache). The renderer lookup is also quite expensive (at least a map lookup and some other logic) so in the cases where we are doing a refresh anyway, it is much cheaper to just set a field and refresh.

### Is it possible to construct a solution with the existing API?

Yes, I rewrote Activity (see https://github.com/fyne-io/fyne/pull/4861) and InfiniteProgressbar (see https://github.com/fyne-io/fyne/pull/4848/files) a while back to avoid this. The general approach is to set fields inside the widget instead and let the renderer look at them when it is being refreshed.

### Describe the solution you'd like to see.

Widgets (or containers that are widgets) which do use `cache.Renderer` should be reworked not to. A quick grep on `develop` gives:
- [ ] internal/widget.Scroller
- [ ] widget.Entry
- [ ] widget.Form
- [ ] widget.RichText
- [x] widget.TextGrid
- [ ] widget.Tree

fyne-io/fyne.title: boundTreeItem data race with boundTree

labels.name: unverified
labels.description: A bug that has been reported but not verified

fyne-io/fyne.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://github.com/fyne-io/fyne/issues) for open issues that relate to the same problem, before opening a new one.
- [x] This issue only relates to a single bug. I will open new issues for any other problems.

### Describe the bug

`boundTree` and `boundTreeItem` share a pointer to a single map `val`.  When using this map in `boundTree`, the `binding.base` lock is used to prevent data races.  When using the same map in `boundTreeItem`, the `binding.base` lock of this new binding is used (a different lock entirely!) which results in data races when setting the map and reading it simultaneously.

Possible solutions in the code might be to pass in the `binding.base` lock from the `boundTree` when creating the `boundTreeItem`, or to create a copy of the map for the `boundTreeItem` since they could all share a read-only map.

A workaround is to ensure the `.Get()` and `.Set()` are run on the serialized fyne thread (can use `fyne.Do` block), since if all these fyne APIs are called in serial then locking isn't necessary.

### How to reproduce

Call `.Get()` on a `boundTreeItem` on the fyne thread while calling `.Set()` on the `boundTree` for that tree on another thread.

### Screenshots

_No response_

### Example code

Please see steps to reproduce.

### Fyne version

fyne-io/fyne.title: Spinner Widget
fyne-io/fyne.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://github.com/fyne-io/fyne/issues) for open issues that relate to the same feature, before opening a new one.
- [x] This issue only relates to a single feature. I will open new issues for any other features.

### Is your feature request related to a problem?

There is no spinner widget in fyne or fyne-x. There have been multiple issues in the past requesting a spinner widget and PRs for both fyne and fyne-x but all were closed without implementation.

### Is it possible to construct a solution with the existing API?

It is possible to combine either text or an Entry widget with two buttons, but does not look as good as a specific widget would.

### Describe the solution you'd like to see.

I can see at least two spinner widgets:
1. A numerical text spinner.
2. A spinner based on NumericalEntry.

In both cases, a stacked pair of buttons to the right of the text or entry would be used to increment or decrement the spinner value by `step` amount.

To support more than one spinner type, there should be a SpinnerBase widget that contains the spinner data fields: min, max, value, step, and the spinner buttons. This base widget would contain all of the functionality that is shared between the final widgets, which would inherit from the base spinner widget. The final spinners would be responsible for display of the widget, and where necessary, passing events off to the base spinner.

The base spinner could also be used as the base of any other spinner types that might be found to be useful in the future.

The base spinner and the text Spinner could be added to fyne or to fyne-x.
Since the NumericalEntrySpinner would use a NumericalEntry widget, it would have to be placed in fyne-x unless the NumericalEntry widget was moved to fyne.  There is a fyne-x PR (107) for NumericalEntry that is awaiting review. This PR should be handled before work on a NumericalEntrySpinner widget is started.

I have done a number of prototypes of both the text and NumericalEntry spinners to determine the contents of BaseSpinner, so I do not expect that it will take too long to implement this feature request.

fyne-io/fyne.title: Keyboard Access Keys for menus
fyne-io/fyne.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://github.com/fyne-io/fyne/issues) for open issues that relate to the same feature, before opening a new one.
- [x] This issue only relates to a single feature. I will open new issues for any other features.

### Is your feature request related to a problem?

On desktop applications with menus (I'm familiar with Windows), usually there is the ability to press Alt+<a letter> to activate a main menu.   This is called the "access key".  For example if the File menu has F as the access key, then F will be underlined and I can open the menu with Alt+F.  For and example of desktop environment that already does this is  windows forms: [Create access key shortcuts](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/desktop/winforms/controls/how-to-create-access-keys)

-  When the user holds the Alt key down the F in File will be underlined i.e. F͟ ile and the similar with other main menus
- When the user holds Alt+F the File menu is activated, and any items with shortcuts, will be underlined, e.g. Open menu item, has O underlined.
- Then the user can press O to open the open dialog.

This is a long-standing accessibility functionality in Windows, for example see this example from Windows.Forms, that was in .net v1.1 (2003):   [MenuItem.Shortcut Property](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.windows.forms.menuitem.shortcut?view=netframework-1.1), windows forms uses "&" to specify the access key for the menu item, e.g.:
```
       menuItem1.Text = "&New";  // The & before N signifies that "N" is the access key for this menu item.
       // Assign a shortcut key.
       menuItem1.Shortcut = Shortcut.CtrlN;

```
I observe this functionality in many applications in KDE as well.

I asked about this functionality on [stack overflow](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/79668437/how-to-activate-the-file-menu-with-a-keyboard-shortcut-in-fyne/79668968)

### Is it possible to construct a solution with the existing API?

No, there is no API to activate a menu itself.  Currently pressing Alt by itself will activate the main menu in Fyne on desktop, but Alt+F will not activate a main menu called File.

### Describe the solution you'd like to see.

1. Ability to set an access key for a menu and underline a menu item.  This is distinct from the keyboard shortcut functionality that already exists (like below), because it cannot be used to activate a menu itself.
Existing functionality is , e.g. Ctrl-Q by this code:

> printMenuItem.Shortcut = &desktop.CustomShortcut{KeyName: fyne.KeyP, Modifier: fyne.KeyModifierControl}

4. The underlined main menu it is activated by Alt+<access key>.  Menu items can also be underlined.

fyne-io/fyne.title: Consider using weak pointers in internal caches

labels.name: optimization
labels.description: Tickets that could help Fyne apps run faster

fyne-io/fyne.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://github.com/fyne-io/fyne/issues) for open issues that relate to the same feature, before opening a new one.
- [x] This issue only relates to a single feature. I will open new issues for any other features.

### Is your feature request related to a problem?

Memory usage is quite high already and we might be holding on to memory too long if a user is creating a lot of objects which have to wait until our cache cleaning task runs the next time. Because we are holding pointers to the memory, it prevents the GC from deallocating the objects. Using weak pointers using the `weak` package in Go 1.24 might allow us to have caches cleaned somewhat automatically when the objects go out of scope by letting the container and user code basically own the references.

### Is it possible to construct a solution with the existing API?

Use the new `ẁeak` package (https://go.dev/blog/cleanups-and-weak) and switch internal cache maps to use it.

### Describe the solution you'd like to see.

Related to https://github.com/fyne-io/fyne/issues/3242, it requires bumping the minimum Go version to Go 1.24.

fyne-io/fyne.title: Improved handling of heterogeneous data in tables
fyne-io/fyne.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://github.com/fyne-io/fyne/issues) for open issues that relate to the same feature, before opening a new one.
- [x] This issue only relates to a single feature. I will open new issues for any other features.

### Is your feature request related to a problem?

It's too hard :tm:  to develop a good looking table when the data is non-homogeneous, which is a common scenario.  
It's also tricky to handle expanding the row when the contents of a cell wrap to multiple lines (which  HTML `<table>` does  by default).

So, after discussion with the team, I'm opening this request to refine the details  before a lot of code gets written.

### Is it possible to construct a solution with the existing API?

Yes, the existing API does allow rendering this kind of data, but it involves a lot of code and requires the dev user to be very aware of the nuances of layout and Refresh() (both when to do it vs when it's already done for you, and avoiding creating rendering loops with redundant Refresh()).

### Describe the solution you'd like to see.

The key scenario we're trying to support is the display of *heterogeneous* data, especially the case where the columns of data are homogeneous within themselves but different from one column to the next.  A good example is displaying the results of a DB query, where each column is typically a different data type with different formatting.  
My test case is a simple bank transaction report with these columns:

* date (some date format), 
* amount (currency), 
* transaction description (a potentially long string that might need truncation or word wrapping) and 
* (for extra spice) a running balance (another currency column).

The user developer wants to query the DB, possibly convert all the values to formatted string and display them in a table.  S/he can make good guesses for the widths of date and currency columns, is willing to set an ad-hoc, fixed width for the description column, but would like the widget to handle wrapping the description in the rows that need it without much fuss.

 Goals and requirements, without diving into design:
* It should be "easy" to handle column-wise heterogeneous data, like the test case above.
* There should also be a way  to handle data that is heterogeneous in application-specific ways, relying on the user developer to define the classification.   User might want to define additional classes for alternating row styling, or  might know that several columns can use the same class, and should have a way to express that to the widget.
* Cell templating and caching should support the homogeneity classification described above.  (Let's just call it the "class" of a cell).  
 The API should guarantee that it only provides an instance of the appropriate class to the update cell callback for a given row/column index.  Then the update cell callback can update just the *content* and can assume the styling is as it was initialized (for that class).  For the typical case, the styling of a class of cells doesn't change over time, so static initialization should be enough most of the time.
(this is my big gripe with the current API, that you must currently update *all* styling in each update cell call if you change styling for any other cell.)
* row height should be adjusted by default to fix long, wrapped content.  The dev user in the above scenario doesn't expect content to  wrap into the next row and overlay  the cell below.  That's never the right rendering.  
* However, it's OK to not adjust column widths automatically, dev user in the scenario above can make good guesses what they should be and will not be surprised that s/he must provide this at initialization time.

 
### design issues

API compatibility:

We could try to find a compatible extension to the existing Table API, or, if it becomes just too awkward, we could build a new collection widget  whose API rhymes with Table but differs where functionally necessary.

In any case, there has to be a new callback that classifies a cell given its position in the table and a new type to represent the class value itself ( an int or a typed int).  

There are big compatibility issues trying to make CreateCell return a different template for each cell class. In the existing Table API, CreateCell has no input, so it's tricky to have it generate different classes of output.  There could be an internal method it invokes to get this information, if we needed that.

But I'm inclined to create a brand new "UpdateCellEx" interface which doesn't need a CreateCell.  In the existing Table API, I'd make it an initialization error to specify both Create/UpdateCell *and* UpdateCellEx.  
There'd have to be a new NewTableEx method that takes just the UpdateCellEx callback.  That's just barely a compatible extension of the existing API.

The UpdateCellEx would not depend on CreateCell.  It  would be invoked with row and column but *no* input object.  It would  return an output object.  

On invocation, UpdateCellEx would:
* determine the cell class from row and column
* call into the cache looking for an existing cell *of that class*  
* If there isn't one, return nil or err.  User code in UpdateCellEx would allocate a new widget and initialize it as appropriate for the class.
If there is one, it should already have all the styling appropriate for that class. (Unless user code in the callback *does* muck with styling)
* Either way, user code now has an instance of the correct class.  It  sets  the content in the cell  and returns that object to the Table.
* The returned value is rendered and eventually becomes a candidate for caching.  

* cache performance should not be slower than existing API.  It might use more space, since there are now multiple classes of objects to cache.

Comments on any/all of above eagerly solicited!

I noticed in Hegelmote that the popup of for example a widget.Select doesn't handle the bottom edge of the window in a good way. When the popup is too long, it is moved up over the intended position so it fits in thw window. However, this does not seem to consider the window border padding. With a select widget, this can be seen in the height sense where the bottom of the popup hugs the bottom of the window,

### How to reproduce

1. Run example code.
2. Click on the select widget.
3. Notice that the popup is right at the edge of the bottom window edge.

```go
	a := app.New()
```

On desktop Linux, I can highlight selectable labels and copy the text as expected.

On Android (tested on Android 15/LineageOS 22.1), I can still highlight the contents of the labels, but dragging to expand the selection opens the on-screen keyboard and does not provide a copy option. 2. Hold and drag to select text
3. Observe that the keyboard opens and no option to copy the selected text is provided

### Is your feature request related to a problem?

Numerical values generally look better when right justified, but the Entry widget only left-justifies text.

### Is it possible to construct a solution with the existing API?

This could be accomplished by creating a custom widget that inherits from Entry.

### Is your feature request related to a problem?

I am developing a search feature for a mobile app. There are a several filters that the user can toggle, which are shown as a row of filter chips under the search bar. There are usually more chips then fit on the width of the screen, so the chips can scroll horizontally.

The chips are currently inside a `container.NewHScroll()`. However, this widget shows a scroll bar and I would like to be able to scroll the chips horizontally without a scroll bar. In my opinion the scrollbar is not strictly necessary in this case, so I like to avoid the additional visual clutter. Also, other mobile apps don't have a scroll bar for this feature (e.g. IMDB search). 

Example: 

![image](https://firebasestorage.googleapis.com/v0/b/design-spec/o/projects%2Fgoogle-material-3%2Fimages%2Flztl1l2l-39.png?alt=media&token=aa26cef5-6cec-4944-a832-c7ea345183ed)

No

I would suggest to add a field like `HideScrollBar` to the [widget.Scroll](https://pkg.go.dev/fyne.io/fyne/v2@v2.5.3/internal/widget#Scroll) type. Similar to the current `Direction` field or the `HideSeperators` fields in the List widget.

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://github.com/fyne-io/fyne/issues) for open issues that relate to the same feature, before opening a new one.
- [x] This issue only relates to a single feature. I will open new issues for any other features.

### Is your feature request related to a problem?

After the migration to the new threading model, we now have a lot of places where the old concurrent object pools are now accessed on a single thread. With migrations enabled, we can replace these with a simpler and more efficient single threaded variant.

### Is it possible to construct a solution with the existing API?

Yes. We can likely do something similar to what we do with the async packet for maps in that async.Pool changes the backend when we turn on migrations.

### Describe the solution you'd like to see.

Implement a single threaded pool either via a slice (fast to clear out and fast to get an element from thanks to good data locality but poor growth) or some linked list (good growth but poor data locality and slow pool clearing).

labels.name: Driver:web

fyne-io/fyne.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://github.com/fyne-io/fyne/issues) for open issues that relate to the same feature, before opening a new one.
- [x] This issue only relates to a single feature. I will open new issues for any other features.

### Is your feature request related to a problem?

We are currently parsing the string of `navigator.platform` to judge if we are running on mobile. This is not fool-proof as it depends a lot on which browser is used and so on. It has been deprecated in favour of `navigator.userAgentData?.mobile` which is a simple boolean telling us if we are running on mobile. Using the value would allow us to enable our mobile mode correctly on more devices (not sure if Linux mobile is working on our current setup even) but the downside is that [userAgentData](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Navigator/userAgentData) only is available over HTTPS and only in Chrome-based browsers as of today.

Related to https://github.com/fyne-io/fyne/issues/4754

### Is it possible to construct a solution with the existing API?

Yes. See https://github.com/fyne-io/fyne/blob/967702162d53cbc8ea9a84c0d1ad148bc99e1dfc/internal/driver/glfw/device_wasm.go#L12.

### Describe the solution you'd like to see.

Use the new API when available but fall back to parsing userAgent platform otherwise.

fyne-io/fyne.title: Replace untyped bindings with generic implementations

labels.name: optimization
labels.description: Tickets that could help Fyne apps run faster

labels.name: data binding
labels.description: Issue related to bug or improvement of data binding

fyne-io/fyne.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://github.com/fyne-io/fyne/issues) for open issues that relate to the same feature, before opening a new one.
- [x] This issue only relates to a single feature. I will open new issues for any other features.

### Is your feature request related to a problem?

We do currently have a couple untyped bindings that rely on runtime reflection to look up types and set their values appropriately. This reflection is slow, does not give the developer any type safety (which may lead to crashes or potential security issues popping up) and it might lead to larger binaries as the Go compiler needs to embed more type information that can be used at runtime. We should avoid runtime reflection to as large extent as we can.

It has been proven with #5378 that generics are a great fit for reducing code duplication within binding types. A generic implementation for bindings should be possible to use for this purpose.

### Is it possible to construct a solution with the existing API?

Yes

### Describe the solution you'd like to see.

I propose that we expose a generic binding that lets the compiler generate a type safe binding implementation for the specific type that the developer wants to use instead.

fyne-io/fyne.title: Unbounded internal cache sizes can lead to unbounded RAM use

labels.name: optimization
labels.description: Tickets that could help Fyne apps run faster

fyne-io/fyne.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://github.com/fyne-io/fyne/issues) for open issues that relate to the same problem, before opening a new one.
- [x] This issue only relates to a single bug. I will open new issues for any other problems.

### Describe the bug

Internal caches are currently unlimited in size, and are cleaned out on a fixed 1-minute schedule. This means that within a minute, apps can grow in RAM use unboundedly, possibly leading to out of memory errors, if they create a huge number of cached objects (especially text textures) within that time. For example, scrolling quickly through 10s of thousands of text-heavy list rows (which could contain on the order of 10 canvas.Texts each).

Possible ideas are to take inspiration from the Go GC itself - run our clean tasks more frequently based on use patterns, and have a "soft limit" on cache size which is based on the past patterns of use.

### How to reproduce

scroll through many many rows of a text-heavy collection widget (eg extend the list or table in fyne_demo to be a million rows long)

labels.name: unverified

fyne-io/fyne.body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://github.com/fyne-io/fyne/issues) for open issues that relate to the same problem, before opening a new one.
- [X] This issue only relates to a single bug. I will open new issues for any other problems.

### Describe the bug

When adding a Widget to the `Canvas().Overlays()` without first setting its `Size()` to `Canvas().Size()` it is displayed with **it's** current `Size()` (Usually its `MinSize()`) instead of the size of the Canvas. Upon resizing the Window (Not via code) it is then resized to the full `Canvas().Size()` as you would have expected when it was initially added. The 'correct' behavior would be for the Widgets `Layout()` to be called with the `Canvas.Size()` when `Canvas().Overlays().Add(widget)` is called.

- Occurring on Linux/Windows (@andydotxyz was unable to reproduce on MacOS)
- Reproducible with provided widget/canvas objects (`canvas.Rectangle`, `widget.Label`, etc)
- Reproducible using a custom Widget with custom renderer (or provided `widget.NewSimpleRenderer()`)
- Not occurring with provided widgets that handle their own interaction with the `Canvas().Overlays()` such as `ModalPopup`.



### How to reproduce

1. Using the provided example code launch the application.
2. Press "Space" - This will add a Black Rectangle to the `Canvas().Overlays()`. It will be 100, 100 instead of spanning the full Canvas.
3. Resize the window by dragging the corner (or however your Display Manager handles resizing) - The Black Rectangle will now span the full Width/Height of the Canvas.

### Screenshots

Using the example code provided, when you press "Space" it will add `bar` to the `Canvas().Overlays()` which in this case is a simple `canvas.Rectangle`. When this is added to the overlay it's using the current `Size()` value of 100, 100.
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ddd18d8a-f77e-405c-8454-5b66763f03ab)


If you resize the window by dragging it out slightly, it updates to span the Width/Height of the full Canvas.
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/73985ce0-5f74-42f5-bdd3-900e1d9b51dc)


### Example code

```
package main

import (
	"image/color"

	"fyne.io/fyne/v2"
	"fyne.io/fyne/v2/app"
	"fyne.io/fyne/v2/canvas"
	"fyne.io/fyne/v2/container"
	"fyne.io/fyne/v2/widget"
)

type Foo struct {
	canvas fyne.Canvas
}

func main() {
	a := app.New()
	w := a.NewWindow("Test")

	foo := &Foo{
		canvas: w.Canvas(),
	}
	mainView := container.NewVBox(widget.NewLabel("SOME CONTENT"))

	w.SetContent(mainView)
	w.Canvas().SetOnTypedKey(foo.keyHandler)
	w.ShowAndRun()
}

func (f *Foo) keyHandler(e *fyne.KeyEvent) {
	switch e.Name {
	case fyne.KeySpace:
		bar := canvas.NewRectangle(color.Black)
		bar.Resize(fyne.NewSize(100, 100))
		f.canvas.Overlays().Add(bar)
	}
}
```

### Fyne version

v2.5.2

### Go compiler version

1.22.6

### Operating system and version

NixOS

### Additional Information

Reproducible on NixOS with both Hyprland and Gnome as well as Window11, with multiple different hardware setups.

Another method for viewing this behavior. This requires you to launch the application in debug mode `go run -tags debug .` This method will add a Label instead and you will see that it's bounding box is it's MinSize() when first added but after resizing the window the bounding box spans the Width/Height of the canvas the same as the Rectangle example.
```
package main

import (
	"fyne.io/fyne/v2"
	"fyne.io/fyne/v2/app"
	"fyne.io/fyne/v2/container"
	"fyne.io/fyne/v2/widget"
)

type Foo struct {
	canvas fyne.Canvas
}

func main() {
	a := app.New()
	w := a.NewWindow("Test")

	foo := &Foo{
		canvas: w.Canvas(),
	}
	mainView := container.NewVBox(widget.NewLabel("SOME CONTENT"))

	w.SetContent(mainView)
	w.Canvas().SetOnTypedKey(foo.keyHandler)
	w.ShowAndRun()
}

func (f *Foo) keyHandler(e *fyne.KeyEvent) {
	switch e.Name {
	case fyne.KeySpace:
		bar := widget.NewLabel("LABEL")
		f.canvas.Overlays().Add(bar)
	}
}
```

### Is your feature request related to a problem?

Fyne provides drawing capabilities, including text. What is not supported is the ability to print the resulting drawing.

I do realize that printing is more typical of a framework than a toolkit, but it would allow a much larger range of applications to be built using fyne.

### Is it possible to construct a solution with the existing API?

Well, yes, but this involves saving the drawing as some sort of image and then opening a separate app to print the image, so not really.

Add printing capabilities to fyne. Most likely this would require printing of or from a canvas.

fyne-io/fyne.title: NewFileOpen needs file path information in the callback
fyne-io/fyne.body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://github.com/fyne-io/fyne/issues) for open issues that relate to the same feature, before opening a new one.
- [X] This issue only relates to a single feature. I will open new issues for any other features.

### Is your feature request related to a problem?

You cannot easily get the file path in the callback of `NewFileOpen`. That's a huge problem because for many operations you need to check certain file properties before accepting a file for being opened. My use case is the user opening an avatar image file that is not allowed to be larger than 4 MB. Right now, I cannot prevent a user from opening a 20GB image file that potentially crashes the machine.

### Is it possible to construct a solution with the existing API?

Partly. URIReadCloser has an URI(), from which the filepath can be extracted and the input stream can be closed. However, at that time the file has already been opened, so the interaction can only be: User opens file, an error is displayed. That's not a good GUI flow.

It is not possible to create the desired GUI interaction: User selects file, explanation why file cannot be chosen is shown, Open is blocked.

### Describe the solution you'd like to see.

Add a FileValidator that gets a filepath as argument and returns an error. If it returns an error, the error is displayed in the filename field of the dialog and the Open/Confirm button is disabled. As opposed to filters, FileValidators allow the display of the file but may block opening it. FileValidators could have a general enough API to be usable in other places, for example whenever a file is to be probed for having the right format before actually reading it.

Note that a filter before display is not desirable for such use cases. It would be very confusing to the user to not being able to see e.g. a "jpg" file without any further explanation when they know it exists. They'd consider this a bug.

fyne-io/fyne.title: Replace strcpy and strcat with safer alternatives in C-code on Android
fyne-io/fyne.body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://github.com/fyne-io/fyne/issues) for open issues that relate to the same feature, before opening a new one.
- [X] This issue only relates to a single feature. I will open new issues for any other features.

### Is your feature request related to a problem?

The functions `strcpy` and `strcat` are generally regarded as unsafe as they do not check the length of the buffer they are writing into. I don't know if the current uses in  https://github.com/search?q=repo%3Afyne-io%2Ffyne%20strcpy&type=code and https://github.com/search?q=repo%3Afyne-io%2Ffyne%20strcpy&type=code can be abused in any way (I couldn't see something strange at first glance) but it does not hurt to stay on the safe side.

We should try to replace these with [strlcpy](https://linux.die.net/man/3/strlcpy) and [strlcat](https://linux.die.net/man/3/strlcat) respectfully assuming that they exist.


### Is it possible to construct a solution with the existing API?

Yes, assuming that the improved APIs exist in the Android c-library.

### Describe the solution you'd like to see.

Replace functions with `strlcat` and `strlcpy` to avoid potential issues with writing outside of buffers.

fyne-io/fyne.title: Menu shortcuts should be disabled while a dialog is open
fyne-io/fyne.body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://github.com/fyne-io/fyne/issues) for open issues that relate to the same feature, before opening a new one.

### Is your feature request related to a problem?

In a desktop app with a menu the menu shortcuts are still active while a dialog is open. This can be a problem, because if there are shortcut that opens a dialog (e.g. a settings dialog), this allows the user to open multiple instances of the same dialog, one on top of each other. It may also be weird for users to be able to open menu items through shortcuts while a supposedly modal dialog is open. In general this behavior breaks the expectation of modality for dialogs in desktop apps.

### Is it possible to construct a solution with the existing API?

As a workaround one could manually remove all menu shortcuts before a dialog is open and re-add them again when it is closed. This would have to be done for each and every dialog in the app and would result in a lot of additional boilerplate code.

### Describe the solution you'd like to see.

Menu shortcuts should be automatically disabled when a dialog opens and re-enabled when it is closed. Any other shortcuts should not be affected.

fyne-io/fyne.body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://github.com/fyne-io/fyne/issues) for open issues that relate to the same problem, before opening a new one.
- [X] This issue only relates to a single bug. I will open new issues for any other problems.

### Describe the bug

Typing a wrong value into an entry-field, which is bound to a variable will update the variable despite the entry's validator returning an error.



### How to reproduce

The example offers two entry-field, each using the same validator.
The validator returns an error if the input is greater than 0.
The entry-fields use the same binding.

On input in any field the binding's `Set` method should only be called if the validation succeeds.

Currently the validator is seemingly only used to provide feedback to the user, while it could already prevent the propagation of a wrong value.


### Screenshots

_No response_

### Example code

```go
package main

import (
	"fmt"
	"strconv"

	"fyne.io/fyne/v2"
	"fyne.io/fyne/v2/app"
	"fyne.io/fyne/v2/container"
	"fyne.io/fyne/v2/data/binding"
	"fyne.io/fyne/v2/widget"
)

func main() {

	app := app.New()
	w := app.NewWindow("Validate before calling binding's Set()")
	w.Resize(fyne.NewSize(800, 100))

	const MAX int = 0

	stringValidator := func(s string) error {
		v, err := strconv.Atoi(s)
		if err != nil {
			return err
		}

		if v > MAX {
			return fmt.Errorf("max: %d got: %d", MAX, v)
		}

		return nil
	}

	str := binding.IntToString(binding.NewInt())

	in1 := widget.NewEntryWithData(str)
	in1.Validator = stringValidator

	in2 := widget.NewEntryWithData(str)
	in2.Validator = stringValidator

	w.SetContent(container.NewVBox(
		in1,
		in2,
	))

	w.ShowAndRun()
}
```

fyne-io/fyne.body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://github.com/fyne-io/fyne/issues) for open issues that relate to the same problem, before opening a new one.
- [X] This issue only relates to a single bug. I will open new issues for any other problems.

### Describe the bug

I have created a new fyne repository interface that implements a subset of webdav functionality. This repository should work with js / wasm since it does not rely on local filesystem calls.

This repository is working with dialog.NewFolderOpen(callback, parent) + Show() when built for Windows. Using a verrsion of fyne with the fix for https://github.com/fyne-io/fyne/issues/5200 included. This dialog.NewFolderOpen(callback, parent) + Show() does NOT work with this repository when built for js / wasm. 

Instead of Show() displaying a File/Foler open dialog box, nothing happens.

I assume this issue is due to the other ties that fyne.io\fyne\v2@v2.5.2\dialog\file.go has with the fyne "file" repository. See the following issues for examples of the above:
https://github.com/fyne-io/fyne/issues/5207
https://github.com/fyne-io/fyne/issues/5204

### How to reproduce

1. Create a non "file" fyne repository that does not rely on local filesystem calls.
2. Use the example code below to create a Folder Open dialog using that repository.
3. Build the application for js / wasm with "fyne package -os web"

fyne-io/fyne.title: func (f *fileDialog) setLocation(dir fyne.URI) error { does not work with non "file" repository
fyne-io/fyne.body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://github.com/fyne-io/fyne/issues) for open issues that relate to the same problem, before opening a new one.
- [X] This issue only relates to a single bug. I will open new issues for any other problems.

### Describe the bug

There is "file" respository specific code in fyne.io\fyne\v2@v2.5.2\dialog\file.go: func (f *fileDialog) setLocation(dir fyne.URI) error {}

Here is the code where the issue is:
newDir := storage.NewFileURI(buildDir)
		isDir, err := storage.CanList(newDir)
		if err != nil {
			return err
		}

Notice that setLocation takes a fyne URL as input (dir fyne.URI). If the fyne URL has a scheme of "file" then the call to  storage.NewFileURI(buildDir) above will work. If the fyne URL in the parameter (dir fyne.URI) has a scheme different than "file". Then the call to storage.NewFileURI(buildDir) will return a URL with the "file" scheme instead of the scheme passed in dir fyne.URI.

I found this bug when trying to use the respository "httpfile" that I created.

### How to reproduce

Create a non "file" repository. 
Create a new file dialog pointing to the non "file" repository
Try traversing directories in the non "file" repository. The UI will stop once storage.NewFileURI(buildDir) resturns an invalid "file" URI.

### Screenshots

_No response_

### Example code

Create a new file dialog using the following code:
```
locationURI, err := storage.ParseURI("httpfile:///")
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	listableURI, err := storage.ListerForURI(locationURI)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	folderdialog := dialog.NewFolderOpen(callback, parent)
	folderdialog.SetLocation(listableURI)
	folderdialog.Show()
```

2.5.2

1.23.1

fyne-io/fyne.title: dialog.New(File/Folder/...)Open() only works with "file" repository

labels.name: FileDialog
labels.description: Improvements to the builtin file dialogs

fyne-io/fyne.body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://github.com/fyne-io/fyne/issues) for open issues that relate to the same problem, before opening a new one.
- [X] This issue only relates to a single bug. I will open new issues for any other problems.

### Describe the bug

I have written a new repository interface which is intended to allow dialog.New(File/Folder/...)Open() to work with remote filesystems in a similar manner as WebDav. I have found that the current implementation of dialog.New(File/Folder/...)Open() has
a number of ties to the operating system / filesystem that fyne is running on. This works fine when it is displaying content from the "file" repository. However, it pretty much breaks down when you try to use it with a different repository. Here is an example of code that looks like it is currently broken for anything other than the "file" repository:
[fyne.io](http://fyne.io/)\fyne\v2@v2.5.2\dialog\file.go

```
func (f *fileDialog) loadFavorites() {
  favoriteLocations, err := getFavoriteLocations()
  if err != nil {
    fyne.LogError("Getting favorite locations", err)
  }
  favoriteIcons := getFavoriteIcons()
  favoriteOrder := getFavoriteOrder()
```

getFavoriteLocations() is platform (not repository) specific code.

Here is another snippet from the same file:
```
for _, file := range files {
		if !f.showHidden && isHidden(file) {
			continue
		}
```
isHidden() is platform (not repository) specific code.

I suspect that the file/folder dialog objects are going to need some pretty major work to get them to work with repositories other than "file". 

### How to reproduce

This is bug is not possible to reproduce with the current codebase as a new non "file" repository needs to be written to exercise the code. I have written a new repository called "httpfile" which supports a subset of webdav functionality.

### Screenshots

_No response_

### Example code

I would provide the package "httpfile" I have written but it looks like attaching go files is not supported.

### Fyne version

2.5.2

### Go compiler version

1.23.1

### Operating system and version

Windows 11

### Additional Information

_No response_

fyne-io/fyne.title: Add fyne repository implementation for WebDav
fyne-io/fyne.body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://github.com/fyne-io/fyne/issues) for open issues that relate to the same feature, before opening a new one.
- [X] This issue only relates to a single feature. I will open new issues for any other features.

### Is your feature request related to a problem?

WebDav is a common tool used for browsing remote filesystems. It is fully supported in Golang.
This feature request is to support WebDav using the fyne repository interface

### Is it possible to construct a solution with the existing API?

Yes. Its just a new instance of the existing repository interface.

### Describe the solution you'd like to see.

A new repository interface for the webdav schema following RFC 4918

- [X] This issue only relates to a single bug. I will open new issues for any other problems.

### Describe the bug

I'm creating an app with a Grid of Cards. If the Title or Subtitle are too large, the text spills out of the card.  Ideally, the same properties (such as truncate or warp) could be set for these strings.

### How to reproduce

Run the attached code.  Note that very long text is neither truncated nor wrapped and flows out of the card.

### Screenshots

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b9bfcc7e-8078-4c67-aa00-98e13bb9c87c)


### Example code

```go
package main

import (
	"fyne.io/fyne/v2"
	"fyne.io/fyne/v2/app"
	"fyne.io/fyne/v2/container"
	"fyne.io/fyne/v2/widget"
)

func main() {
	app := app.New()
	win := app.NewWindow("Card Test")
	win.Resize(fyne.Size{Width: 500, Height: 500})

	cards := []fyne.CanvasObject{
		widget.NewCard("ReaLLLLLLLLLLLLy Long Title", "ReaLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLy Long Subtitle", nil),
		widget.NewCard("Really Long Title", "Really Long Subtitle", nil),
		widget.NewCard("Really Long Title", "Really Long Subtitle", nil),
		widget.NewCard("Title", "Subtitle", nil),
	}

	gw := container.NewGridWrap(fyne.NewSize(200, 200), cards...)

	win.SetContent(gw)
	win.ShowAndRun()
}
```

v2.5.1

1.22.5

macOS Ventura 13.7

fyne-io/fyne.body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://github.com/fyne-io/fyne/issues) for open issues that relate to the same feature, before opening a new one.
- [X] This issue only relates to a single feature. I will open new issues for any other features.

### Is your feature request related to a problem?

The current Toolbar widget displays the toolbar objects aligned horizontally only. Allowing the Toolbar to align the objects vertically would allow the toolbar to be placed along the left edge of an app window. For example, if the toolbar is placed in the left portion of a Border layout or in an HBox layout, then display the toolbar vertically.
I am not familiar with iOS or Android, but assume that on those systems, the toolbar would need to be displayed horizontally.

### Is it possible to construct a solution with the existing API?

Not directly. It is possible to create a VerticalToolbar, but that would be a custom solution and would not provide automatic layout based on the container that the toolbar is in.

### Describe the solution you'd like to see.

Modify the Toolbar widget to display the toolbar objects either horizontally or vertically based on the orientation of the container it is placed in. For example, if the toolbar is placed in the top portion of a Border layout or in an VBox, display the toolbar objects horizontally, but if placed in the left portion of a Border or in an HBox, display the objects vertically. Display on iOS and Android as currently done for other widget displays.

fyne-io/fyne.body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://github.com/fyne-io/fyne/issues) for open issues that relate to the same problem, before opening a new one.
- [X] This issue only relates to a single bug. I will open new issues for any other problems.

### Describe the bug

On MacOS, when you send an app notification, the icon doesn't correspond to the icon of the app. Instead, the script editor icon is shown. Clicking the notification doesn't open the app but instead opens the script editor.

This seems to be a regression of this old bug #935 that was solved back in 2020. I tried adding a simple notification e.g. to the [GoTune](https://github.com/tejashwikalptaru/gotune/) app. Everything works as it should on my machine there. To me, this implies the problem is **not** related to my version of Go or MacOS but rather to the Fyne version. Or, naturally, it could mean that I'm doing something wrong. But, I tried both the `FyneApp.toml` approach and setting the icon on the app manually.

### How to reproduce

1. Clone https://github.com/tadeaspetak/fyne-notifications
2. `make` to package the app
3. `make run` to run the app

- [X] This issue only relates to a single bug. I will open new issues for any other problems.

### Describe the bug

When there are nested fyne.Draggable Objects there is an issue which one should get the Dragged event. Most of the time this is not noticeable, especially on desktop, and was exposed on [a side project](https://github.com/BieHDC/fynedev-swipetabs) that adds swipe gestures for the mobile experience.  
The simplest way to quickly encounter the issue is when you have a lot of sliders inside a scroll container (see example code).
On desktop this is not an issue because we have the mouse scroll wheel and the slider on the right to scroll.  
However [on mobile the scrolling](https://github.com/fyne-io/fyne/blob/7d813563712924b381ced18c04869c059e2cb4c6/internal/widget/scroller.go#L447) is implemented through the Dragged event. The slider will always take priority and the only way to scroll is if you start to scroll on a non Draggable element (the widget.Label on the left in the example code) or empty space like padding.

### How to reproduce

1. Build Mobile App
2. Run the App on the mobile device
3. Try to scroll (see video)

### Screenshots

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2fb2d237-69e6-4240-9650-51fa981de8b8

### Example code

```go
package main

import (
	"fmt"

	"fyne.io/fyne/v2"
	"fyne.io/fyne/v2/app"
	"fyne.io/fyne/v2/container"
	"fyne.io/fyne/v2/widget"
)

func main() {
	app := app.New()
	window := app.NewWindow("Bugtest - Nested Dragged")
	window.SetPadded(false)
	window.Resize(fyne.NewSize(500, 600))
	window.CenterOnScreen()
	window.SetContent(container.NewVScroll(container.NewVBox(bunchOfSliders()...)))
	window.ShowAndRun()
}

func bunchOfSliders() []fyne.CanvasObject {
	var sliders []fyne.CanvasObject
	for i := range 20 {
		sliders = append(sliders,
			container.NewBorder(nil, nil,
				widget.NewLabel(fmt.Sprintf("%d", i)), // the label
				nil,
				widget.NewSlider(0, 100)))
	}
	return sliders
}
```

fyne-io/fyne.title: Add Access to Table's Current Focus
fyne-io/fyne.body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://github.com/fyne-io/fyne/issues) for open issues that relate to the same feature, before opening a new one.
- [X] This issue only relates to a single feature. I will open new issues for any other features.

### Is your feature request related to a problem?

The Table widget keeps track of the current focus location, which helps with keyboard navigation.  The Table keeps track of this separate from the Selected information.

By adding access to Current Focus, both reading it and a callback for when it updates, the cells can render whole row effects.  For example, highlighting the row for very wide tables which otherwise would be difficult to visually distinguish.

### Is it possible to construct a solution with the existing API?

No.  The table stores this data as a private member, and Go prohibits access to it.  The `ScrollTo` like functions allow limited access to write to the member, but there exists no way to read it.

### Describe the solution you'd like to see.

I would like to see the Table structure to provide read access, and a callback function to signal when the value changes.

fyne-io/fyne.title: Table Keyboard Navigation with Header Row Hides First Data Row
fyne-io/fyne.body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://github.com/fyne-io/fyne/issues) for open issues that relate to the same problem, before opening a new one.
- [X] This issue only relates to a single bug. I will open new issues for any other problems.

### Describe the bug

I created a Table widget and included a header row.  I filled the row with enough data to allow the table to have a scroll bar.

When I use the keyboard to navigate up and down, before scrolling, the "current focus" cell moves correctly up to row 0.  However, if you scroll with the keyboard such that the table scrolls down, then scroll back to the top, the "current focus" row will move what seems like under the header and will no longer be visible.  It means the top row (row 0) will never be viewable in this table view without using the mouse.


### How to reproduce

1. Create a table with a header, and fill the cells with simple data.
2. Click on a cell to allow keyboard navigation.
3. Press the "up" key.  The active cell correctly remains visible even when the up key is pressed with row zero active.
4. Scroll down with the "down" key such that the displayed cells scroll.
5. Press the "up" key to return to the top.  The displayed active cell will disappear, and the top row does not show up, as though it's hidden under the table header.

### Screenshots


![TableKeyboardScroll](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/18ee66f8-7e4b-4378-82e3-907353753d12)


### Example code

```
package main

import (
	"strconv"

	"fyne.io/fyne/v2"
	"fyne.io/fyne/v2/app"
	"fyne.io/fyne/v2/container"
	"fyne.io/fyne/v2/widget"
)

func main() {
	a := app.New()
	w := a.NewWindow("Table Scroll")

	t := widget.NewTable(
		func() (rows int, cols int) { return 1000, 1 },
		func() fyne.CanvasObject { return widget.NewLabel("000") },
		func(tci widget.TableCellID, co fyne.CanvasObject) {
			co.(*widget.Label).SetText(strconv.FormatInt(int64(tci.Row), 10))
		},
	)
	t.ShowHeaderRow = true
	t.CreateHeader = func() fyne.CanvasObject { return widget.NewLabel("Row") }
	t.UpdateHeader = func(id widget.TableCellID, template fyne.CanvasObject) {}
	w.SetContent(container.NewStack(t))
	w.Resize(fyne.Size{Width: 100, Height: 250})

	w.ShowAndRun()
}
```

fyne-io/fyne.title: Handle huge amount of Text in Entry Widget
fyne-io/fyne.body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://github.com/fyne-io/fyne/issues) for open issues that relate to the same feature, before opening a new one.
- [X] This issue only relates to a single feature. I will open new issues for any other features.

### Is your feature request related to a problem?

![QQ_1723130286687](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d09bceda-8d5d-4af3-8b0e-20ce4febce1d)


https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/53c4c302-ecb5-4c75-ac03-5d6f157da58c









### Is it possible to construct a solution with the existing API?

Some applications require a text editing box for extremely long content, but the current Entry widget is very sluggish when rendering large amounts of text. I have customized a canvas widget to support extensive text input, which dynamically adjusts its height based on content changes using container.NewVScroll. However, I haven't fully implemented cursor control and basic input functionalities as efficiently as the standard Entry. Due to time constraints, I haven't been able to refine these features. I see that Fyne has progressed to version 2.5.0 now. My approach involves creating a virtual container to handle large text portions and rendering them based on scroll positions. While my CustomCanvasEntryText offers basic editing capabilities, it doesn't match the completeness of Entry. I've found developing this from scratch quite time-consuming. I'm uncertain if Fyne's current or future versions will support extended content in text inputs.

### Describe the solution you'd like to see.

Certainly, if Fyne currently has no plans to support input boxes for extremely long content, I wonder if the Entry widget could expose a scroll interface. This would allow experimenting with virtualization directly on the Entry to achieve partial rendering of extensive text, thus addressing the performance and resource consumption issues associated with rendering large text. By exposing the scroll interface of Entry, I believe it should be possible to customize and implement my own rendering using canvas (leveraging the Entry directly, avoiding the need to separately draw an input box).

fyne-io/fyne.title: Showing an overlay widget using the canvas.Overlays().Add() API blocks interaction with rest of window
fyne-io/fyne.body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://github.com/fyne-io/fyne/issues) for open issues that relate to the same problem, before opening a new one.
- [X] This issue only relates to a single bug. I will open new issues for any other problems.

### Describe the bug

It's unclear if this was intended behavior or not (it's certainly intended for the PopUp case), but the overlay API documentation is just:

```go
// OverlayStack is a stack of CanvasObjects intended to be used as overlays of a Canvas.
type OverlayStack interface {
	// Add adds an overlay on the top of the overlay stack.
	Add(overlay CanvasObject)
	// List returns the overlays currently on the overlay stack.
	List() []CanvasObject
	// Remove removes the given object and all objects above it from the overlay stack.
	Remove(overlay CanvasObject)
	// Top returns the top-most object of the overlay stack.
	Top() CanvasObject
}
```

It says nothing about blocking interaction with what's underneath the overlays, and the documentation suggests you could use it to just show any floating content, which is not the case. If it is intended behavior, the documentation of the OverlayStack should be updated to reflect that, and we should consider introducing a non-blocking variant (#4836). If it isn't intended, we should remove the behavior by default and have some way for overlays like PopUps and Dialogs to indicate that they should block interaction and have their own focus manager.

### How to reproduce

show an overlay using the overlays api over any Fyne app

### Describe the bug

When users use Fyne apps with high-speed gaming mice, e.g. 1000 Hz, the scrolling is very laggy and continues to process a backlog of scroll events after the user stops dragging the scroll bar.

### Describe the bug

Closing a docTabItem will not call OnSelected on the next tabItem if this one is located after the closed item.

### How to reproduce

Run the provided code, open 2 tabs (tab 1, tab 2)
Selected tab 1, then close it
Tab 2 selected should be called, but it is not.

### Screenshots

_No response_

### Example code

```go
package main

import (
	"fmt"

	"fyne.io/fyne/v2/app"
	"fyne.io/fyne/v2/container"
	"fyne.io/fyne/v2/widget"
)

func main() {
	a := app.New()
	w := a.NewWindow("")

	var i int
	docs := container.NewDocTabs()
	docs.CreateTab = func() *container.TabItem {
		i++
		return container.NewTabItem(fmt.Sprintf("tab %03d", i), widget.NewLabel("Tab content"))
	}
	docs.OnSelected = func(ti *container.TabItem) {
		fmt.Println("Tab", ti.Text, "selected")
	}
	docs.OnUnselected = func(ti *container.TabItem) {
		fmt.Println("Tab", ti.Text, "unselected")
	}

	w.SetContent(docs)
	w.ShowAndRun()
}
```

2.4.5

1.20.14

Windows 10

fyne-io/fyne.title: iOS notifications only work in the foreground
fyne-io/fyne.body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://github.com/fyne-io/fyne/issues) for open issues that relate to the same feature, before opening a new one.
- [X] This issue only relates to a single feature. I will open new issues for any other features.

### Is your feature request related to a problem?

IOS notifications are working in the latest develop branch. The app asks correctly if notifications are allowed to show. But then notifications are shown only while the app is running in the foreground. 

If I create a notification to be shown a few seconds later and send the app to the background nothing happens. Only going back to the app will trigger showing the notification (which can be much later or never).


### Is it possible to construct a solution with the existing API?

This might be related to some bug or configuration problem on iOS.

### Describe the solution you'd like to see.

On Android this works correctly: even while an app is in the background, notifications from that app will be shown at the required moment.

Only showing notifications while the app is in foreground is not very useful. The app already has full attention.

fyne-io/fyne.title: Mobile simulator should follow light/dark mode

labels.name: mobile-simulator
labels.description: Issues relating to the mobile siumulator.

fyne-io/fyne.body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://github.com/fyne-io/fyne/issues) for open issues that relate to the same feature, before opening a new one.
- [X] This issue only relates to a single feature. I will open new issues for any other features.

### Is your feature request related to a problem?

The mobile simulator on Linux (maybe MacOS as well if it works similar there?) does not follow the dark theme preference set by the desktop operating system. Given that the apps will adapt to the set theme on Android and iOS, it makes sense to try to follow the theme even when they are simulating a mobile on the desktop. Support for this would  allow developers to test their apps with both themes easily.

I suspect that this might apply to Linux phones as well?

### Is it possible to construct a solution with the existing API?

Yes. The handling for themes that looks at the XDG dark mode preference is already working in the desktop driver.

### Describe the solution you'd like to see.

The code for the desktop driver has code for checking theme preference of light/dark mode. This code can likely be moved into the mobile simulator code.

described above

- [X] This issue only relates to a single bug. I will open new issues for any other problems.

### Describe the bug

When gridwraplayout initially runs, it gets a size of 0,0. This results, as noted in the docco, in a single column grid. Where there are a lot of items, the resulting initial min size has a very large height. While gridwraplayout modifies layout and minsize on subsequent runs, once the window is up and working and resized, parent containers/layouts continue to use the first very large height resulting in windows that go off the screen and are undraggable to resize and have a huge gap below the content. This has been tested with GridLayout containing GridWrapLayout. Sample code below. It is also affected by the size of the screen vs initial min height. The bug happens when the initial large height is greater than the screen real estate height.

### How to reproduce

Run the example code with the number of displayed numbers large enough to push the content off the bottom of the screen before display.

### Screenshots

![image](https://github.com/fyne-io/fyne/assets/150400275/c2fdb403-d207-4cab-bef1-2453cb88f9e1)


### Example code

```go
package main

import (
	"image/color"
	"strconv"

	"fyne.io/fyne/v2"
	"fyne.io/fyne/v2/app"
	"fyne.io/fyne/v2/canvas"
	"fyne.io/fyne/v2/container"
	"fyne.io/fyne/v2/layout"
)

func main() {
	myApp := app.New()
	myWindow := myApp.NewWindow("Grid Wrap Layout")
	myWindow.Resize(fyne.NewSize(1800,300)) 

	grid := container.New(layout.NewGridWrapLayout(fyne.NewSize(50, 50)))
    for i := 0; i < 100; i++ {
    	grid.Add(canvas.NewText(strconv.Itoa(i), color.Black))
    }
    
	myWindow.SetContent(
		container.New(
	    	layout.NewGridLayout(1),
	    	grid,
	    	layout.NewSpacer(),
	    ),
	)

	//myWindow.Resize(fyne.NewSize(180, 75))
	myWindow.ShowAndRun()
}
```

go version go1.22.2 linux/amd64
