fyne-io/fyne.title: Use Flatpak portals for notifications
fyne-io/fyne.body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://github.com/fyne-io/fyne/issues) for open issues that relate to the same feature, before opening a new one.
- [X] This issue only relates to a single feature. I will open new issues for any other features.

### Is your feature request related to a problem?

Fyne applications, like https://beta.flathub.org/apps/details/io.github.jacalz.rymdport, currently have to enable `--talk-name=org.freedesktop.Notifications` to support notifications over Dbus. It would be better to instead use the Flatpak portal for this as it would avoid having to enable more than permissions and also would allow the Gnome/Plasma applications settings to turn on and off notifications for the application.

### Is it possible to construct a solution with the existing API?

Yes. We should just send the notification in a different way that what we currently are doing.

### Describe the solution you'd like to see.


I don't know if this has been done using Go before but seems, per https://libportal.org/libportal.html, like this should be doable over Dbus. Worst case, we need to create an optional CGo wrapper around https://github.com/flatpak/libportal.

Using `go build -tags flatpak` might be required to solve this.

fyne-io/fyne.title: Use Flatpak portals for file handling
fyne-io/fyne.body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://github.com/fyne-io/fyne/issues) for open issues that relate to the same feature, before opening a new one.
- [X] This issue only relates to a single feature. I will open new issues for any other features.

### Is your feature request related to a problem?

Fyne applications, like https://beta.flathub.org/apps/details/io.github.jacalz.rymdport, running in Flatpak containers currently require the developers to allow a few XDG-directories to be enabled for the file and folder dialogs to work. Any other directories that the application needs access to will require those directories to be added as well.

It would be better to instead use the [Flatpak portals](https://libportal.org/) (over DBus presumably) to open OS file dialogs that then let the user select a file or folder that the application then will get access to.

### Is it possible to construct a solution with the existing API?

Yes. We need to make sure that the file and folder dialogs open the corresponding Flatpak portals for selecting or creating files/folders. The code for URI and storage code might also need to be adapted to handle this correctly.

### Describe the solution you'd like to see.

I don't know if this has been done using Go before but seems, per https://libportal.org/libportal.html, like this should be doable over Dbus. Worst case, we need to create an optional CGo wrapper around https://github.com/flatpak/libportal.

Using `go build -tags flatpak` might be required to solve this.

### Describe the bug

Running app in C:\Windows\System32 gives the error `rundll32 resolves to executable in current directory (.\rundll32.exe)`

The code calls `fyne.CurrentApp().OpenURL(url)`

Which hits this code (windows):
```golang
func (a *fyneApp) OpenURL(url *url.URL) error {
	cmd := a.exec("rundll32", "url.dll,FileProtocolHandler", url.String())
	cmd.Stdin, cmd.Stdout, cmd.Stderr = os.Stdin, os.Stdout, os.Stderr
	return cmd.Run()
}
```

But with the go 1.19 changes to PATH lookups this fails.  The same error will happen for all other fyne calls to "rundll32".  I assume the fix is to reference the full path to it: "C:\Windows\System32\rundll32"

See https://go.dev/doc/go1.19 - PATH lookups for details.



### How to reproduce

1. Create fyne app with golang 1.19 on Windows that calls `fyne.CurrentApp().OpenURL(url)`
2. Run the app with the working directory as `C:\Windows\System32`
3. Notice the error.

fyne-io/fyne.title: Access to (FTDI) USB serial device (on Android)
fyne-io/fyne.body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://github.com/fyne-io/fyne/issues) for open issues that relate to the same feature, before opening a new one.
- [X] This issue only relates to a single feature. I will open new issues for any other features.

### Is your feature request related to a problem?

We have developed a Fyne based UI for a sensor hardware which consists of a microcontroller and a FTDI based USB-Serial interface (a lot like many Arduinos have).

This was easy to implement for _Linux_ and _Windows_ with [ziutek](https://github.com/ziutek/ftdi)'s libftdi/libusb1 package.

But now we struggle with the Android platform port:
We have not yet succeeded in getting ziutek/ftdi compile and link correctly into Fyne projects.
Probably the best way would be to let CGO compile the libftdi + libusb1 sources as [karalabe](https://github.com/karalabe/usb) does, but this seems quite complicated and a lot of effort.
It seemed to be a lot more straightforward to use [mik3y](https://github.com/mik3y/usb-serial-for-android)'s `usb-serial-for-android` Java lib for the Android platform, but according to https://stackoverflow.com/questions/65278073/reverse-java-bindings-with-gomobile-and-fyne-io it is not possible to add and use Java APIs with Fyne.

Especially for the zillions of Arduino fans out there it should be interesting to have a working solution to access their devices from Fyne apps in a platform independent way.

How could we solve this best? 
Is there any interest for a more general approach?

### Is it possible to construct a solution with the existing API?

The only current solution we know of is to implement USB device access in a separate app using the mentioned Java lib and make our Fyne app communicate with it.

### Describe the solution you'd like to see.

Best would be a platform independent interface for accessing (USB) serial devices, including RTS/CTS/DTD/DTR handling, baudrate and parity configuration ... which abstracts on platform specific implementations using whatever libs there are available.

While this can certainly only be a future goal, any kind of workaround/hint/proposal/idea of how to solve our actual problem is appreciated.

One could think of either a FTDI specific approach or a more general approch to access also usb serial devices of other vendors.

fyne-io/fyne.title: Go version upgrade checklist

labels.name: future
labels.description: Features that might take a while to be sheduled

fyne-io/fyne.body:
# Description

Before anyone wonders, I just want to clarify that this ticket is not about saying that we should upgrade the minimum Go versions. Our minimum version supported is still following what is in the latest version of Debian and this issue is not trying change that in any way.

The reason for open it is purely to write down what we can and should improve on when we one day upgrade the minimum Go version. This makes sure that we don't miss anything important. If you notice anything that I have missed, especfially when it comes to using better APIs where available, please update the issue or comment accordingly.

## Go 1.15 (removes 10.11 El Capitan support)

- [x] Remove [work114.go](https://github.com/fyne-io/fyne/blob/master/internal/driver/mobile/gl/work114.go) and remove the build tag for `go115` from `work.go`.
- [ ] Remove any code for 32-bit `darwin` operating systems (means dropping iPhone 5 support). See https://github.com/fyne-io/fyne/issues/2369 and potentially others.
- [ ] Remove any potential code specific to macOS versions before 10.12 Sierra (Sierra is now the minimum).
- [x] Check usages of `timer.Ticker` to see if we can make use of the `.Reset()` method.

## Go 1.16

- [x] Remove the vendor folder now that module support is on by default.
- [x] Remove documentation related to versions without the new module commands (using `install` over `get`).
- [x] Stop using deprecated `io/ioutil` functions and use the new ones in `io` and `os` instead.
- [x] Replace `filepath.Walk` usages with faster `filepath.WalkDir`.
- [ ] Add adapter for `io/fs`. Tracked in #2680.

## Go 1.17 (removes 10.12 Sierra support)

- [x] Tidy the module with support for pruned module graphs: `go mod tidy -go=1.17`.
- [ ] Remove any potential code specific to macOS versions before 10.13 High Sierra (High Sierra is now the minimum). See https://github.com/fyne-io/fyne/pull/2594
- [x] Use the new math.MaxInt contant in table: https://github.com/fyne-io/fyne/blob/be9cd4b67990836a8d9f518b0c3b5a59b1f0349e/widget/table.go#L16

## Go 1.18 (removes iOS 11 support, but no model is stuck on iOS 11, see [iosref](https://iosref.com/ios) )

- [x] Look at some of the `interface{}` and template generated code to see if generics make sense.
- [x] Look at usages of [Index](https://tip.golang.org/pkg/strings/#Index), [IndexByte](https://tip.golang.org/pkg/strings/#IndexByte), [IndexRune](https://tip.golang.org/pkg/strings/#IndexRune), and [SplitN](https://tip.golang.org/pkg/strings/#SplitN) and replace with [Cut](https://tip.golang.org/pkg/strings/#Cut) where it makes sense. Similarly applies to `bytes` as well.

## Go 1.19 (removes FreeBSD 11 support) - Debian 12 Bookworm
- [x] Switch to new atomic types in places where it makes sense.
- [ ] Look at potentially using new functions [Append](https://tip.golang.org/pkg/fmt/#Append), [Appendf](https://tip.golang.org/pkg/fmt/#Appendf), and [Appendln](https://tip.golang.org/pkg/fmt/#Appendln) that append formatted data to byte slices.
- [x] Stop using the `execabs` package now that it is fixed in the `os/exec` package.
- [ ] Switch to the `unix` build tags.
- [x] Run `go fix ./...` to clean up old code.
- [x] Replace `interface{}` with `any`.

## Go 1.20
- [x] Update fast map implementation (using `async.Map`) from https://github.com/fyne-io/fyne/pull/5552 to use `K` over `any` for the type of the map key.
- Use new time constants.

## Go 1.21 (removes support for Windows < 10 and macOS 10.14 Mojave)
- [ ] Switch to new `min` and `max` builtins. Deprecate existing `Min` and `Max` APIs. (#6506)
- [ ] Use `slices` and `maps` package to clean up some custom code.
- [ ] Make sure to switch to the new faster sort functions in `slices`.
- [x] Use the new `clear()` builtin for emptying out slices and maps (look at for-loops with `delete()` in the case of maps).

## Go 1.22
- [ ] Remove workarounds for capturing loop variables.
- [ ] Use range over int in places where it is helpful.
- [ ] Look at using the new `AppendDecode`  and `AppendEncode` methods in encoding packages.
- [ ] Use the new `go/version` package for version handling?
- [ ] Use the new `slices.Concat` function?
- [ ] Remove unnecessary zeroing from slices code now that it is handled correctly.
- [ ] Update `yuin/goldmark` to get much smaller binaries and make wasm-opt be able to handle more aggressive optimisations: https://github.com/WebAssembly/binaryen/issues/7644#issuecomment-2956876721

## Go 1.23 (removes support for macOS 10.15 Catalina)
- [ ] Replace custom iteration constructs and similar functions with built in iterators.
- [ ] Replace any potential path localization (slashes to backward slashes) using new `path/filepath` Localize function.
- [x] Remove any `sync.Map` clearing code in favour of `.Clear()`.

## Go 1.24 (requires Linux kernel 3.2 or later) - Debian 13 Trixie
- [ ] Consider adding `#cgo nocallback` and `#cgo noescape`, where applicable, to improve performance.
- [ ] Use `os.Root` to limit path traversal by only doing operations within a specific directory.
- [ ] Use the new benchmark function `b.Loop()` and then remove global benchmark result variables.
- [ ] Use `weak` package and corresponding pointers for internal caches. See https://github.com/fyne-io/fyne/issues/5770.
- [ ] Use new strings and bytes iterator functions instead of allocating slices (useful for `strings.Split()` etc. when looping over it afterwards). This reduces allocations and should generally be faster.
- [ ] Consider using `t.Context()` and `t.Chdir` in tests where useful.
- [ ] Update `golang.org/x/*` packages now that they require Go 1.24.

## Go 1.25 (removes support for macOS 11 Big Sur)

fyne-io/fyne.title: Entry OnValidationChanged behavior

labels.name: unverified
labels.description: A bug that has been reported but not verified

fyne-io/fyne.body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://github.com/fyne-io/fyne/issues) for open issues that relate to the same problem, before opening a new one.
- [X] This issue only relates to a single bug. I will open new issues for any other problems.

### Describe the bug

Hello all :), I have noticed that the changes in `entry_validation.go` by using `errors.Is(...)`, actually change the way OnValidationChanged works. That is because `errors.Is` actually compares an error to a value, according to https://go.dev/blog/go1.13-errors:
> In the simplest case, the errors.Is function behaves like a comparison to a sentinel error

Then validators that do not return a pre-existing sentinel error (using for example `return errors.New(...)`) will trigger validation change even if the error has actually the same error message, because they will actually have different values (different instances).

So for example these validators:
```go
entry.Validator = func (s string) error {
     if s == "" {
         return errors.New("Required")
     }
     return nil
}


entry.Validator = func (s string) error {
     _, err := mail.ParseAddress(s)
     return err
}
```

Will trigger OnValidationChange (and also refreshing the widget) even if the error in "practical terms" has not change.

Is this the desired behavior? Note that before that change, the behavior was different and above validators worked as expected, but not sure if this behavior change was intentional.


### How to reproduce

1. Run the example code.
2. Focus the entry and type "abcd".
3. Notice that the error "mail: missing '@' or angle-addr" has been printed 4 times.
4. That error is printed from the OnValidationChanged, normally it should be printed just 1 time, as it is the "same" error.
5. If you run the same code using `fyne.io/fyne/v2@v2.1.4`, that error will be printed just once.

### Screenshots

_No response_

### Example code

```go
package main

import (
	"fmt"
	"net/mail"

	"fyne.io/fyne/v2/app"
	"fyne.io/fyne/v2/container"
	"fyne.io/fyne/v2/widget"
)

func main() {
	a := app.New()
	w := a.NewWindow("Hello")

	e := widget.NewEntry()
	e.Validator = func(s string) error {
		_, err := mail.ParseAddress(s)
		return err
	}
	e.SetOnValidationChanged(func(err error) {
		fmt.Println(err)
	})
	w.SetContent(container.NewVBox(e))

	w.ShowAndRun()
}
```

1.18.4

macOS

Big Sur 11.5.1

fyne-io/fyne.title: Unable to run application twice, even after quitting first one
fyne-io/fyne.body:
### Describe the bug:

An app cannot be stopped and either started again or replaced with a new, working instance of an app.

When starting an app and showing a window, quitting it, and trying to start the app again, no window is shown the second time. The app cannot be run twice even when the first instance of it is removed. Code provided below shows this in a minimally reproducible example.

Looks like the code at [L69](https://github.com/fyne-io/fyne/blob/master/internal/driver/glfw/loop.go#L69) of the loop blocks on the second run and doesn't go any further with debugging. Andrew from slack reckons "It's possible we don't signal `funcQueue`". 

[Suspected related issue](https://github.com/fyne-io/fyne/issues/920).

### To Reproduce:

Expectation from the following code is that a window should appear repeatedly, but it is only shown once. The same issue happens even with `app.New()` placed within the loop.

```
a := app.New()

for {
  w := a.NewWindow("title")
  w.Resize(fyne.Size{Width: 800, Height: 600})
  
  go func() {
    time.Sleep(2 * time.Second)
    a.Quit()
  }()
  
  w.ShowAndRun()
  time.Sleep(4 * time.Second)
}
```

 - **Version:** 1.4
 - **Go version:** 1.18.3

fyne-io/fyne.title: Vet and cleanup module dependencies
fyne-io/fyne.body:
### Summary

We currently have 28 direct dependencies listed in the [go.mod](https://github.com/fyne-io/fyne/blob/develop/go.mod) file on develop as of writing this (note that those are for all packages here and an app built with Fyne will have nowhere near that many dependencies). These dependencies have of course been added as they have been needed but they have, more or less, started to pile up (it is entirely natural that it happens; I don't mean anything bad by saying so) and I think it might be time that we look into seeing if we can improve our dependency list.

I propose that we look through the list and try to remove potential dependencies that we might not need and replace some with better alternatives if available. We should also try to move away from unmaintained dependencies for security and maintainability reasons.

### The list

fyne-io/fyne.title: Issues with Validation
fyne-io/fyne.body:
This is based on a discussion I had with @andydotxyz on discord.

TL;DR: Currently, `Form`s do not treat validation as a black box, and contain special behavior for an `Entry`. 
The problem with just removing this behavior is that we need to do something different to ensure that we don't startle the end user with errors until they interact with them and currently this works by affecting the internal state of an `Entry`. 
The question at hand is: How can we fix this so a `Form` exhibits the same behavior for all `Validator`s and can it be done without changing the `Validator` interface?

> Edit (6/5/22): added a note about user interaction state
> Edit (8/5/22): added note about multiple consumers and TL;DR

## Problem:

We have two categories in validation: Producers (`Validator`s) and Consumers (any thing that uses `SetOnValidationError()`).

The contract for producers and consumers (and the user) is as follows:
- Producers must always pass on an update to the validation state.
- Consumers can also be Producers (and perhaps they should always be).
- All producers and consumers that are user facing mustn't alert the user to their invalid state (unless there is no other way to indicate their invalid state) until after the user has interacted with them at least once.

The current problem is two-fold:
1. This contract is currently only fulfilled when the producer is an `Entry` and the consumer is a `Form`.
2. This contract is not really always fulfilled because the current convention is that producers only pass on the new state when it has changed meaningfully from the previous one.

To be clear: on a lower level, currently this contract is only fulfilled from the end user's stand point and not internally. 

## Solutions:

### Solution A:
Add `SetValidationError()` to the `Validator` interface and set an initial error on the children. This fulfills the contract by using an error that everything knows to ignore, but also is still an invalid state. 

Pros:
- We use this technique already for `Entry`s, so it should work elsewhere (considering that it is the reference implementation for other `Validator`s).
- Because any change in the validation status will not be this initial error, it will for certain be a meaningful change (so it will always update).
- It would require the least changes to existing logic (I think).
- Having this method also allows us to quickly circumvent a validation error if we want.

Cons:
- This would constitute a breaking API change.
- An additional rule would be added to the contact: Producers must pass on an update of state from their parent to their children.
- Every consumer would need to implement the logic to set this "initial error" on initialization (because there is no guarantee that it has a parent). So ultimately this solution isn't really better.
- This requires allowing modifying what is effectively internal state of a producer, which is almost definitely a bad idea. 

Ultimately, this solution is probably the wrong one and therefore:

### Solution B:
Fully divorce the presentation of the error from the (change in) state of it. So when the widget is first rendered it will not show anything alerting (i.e. red colored) until `Validate()` has been called.

Pros:
- This method fully fulfills the contract.
- It allows us to treat each `Validator` as a black box (like it should be).
- This method should be a bit more clear in the implementation.

Cons:
- There doesn't appear to be a way to determine if a widget has been rendered (this is mainly a problem for anything that extends a widget).
- I think this is enough of a behavior change that it could be considered breaking. 
- The logic for this is a bit more complicated and we don't yet know what it would actually look like.

## Notes:

### Different reactions based on state of user interaction:
There is reason to amend the the third rule of the contract to: 
  > - All producers and consumers that are user facing mustn't alert the user to their invalid state (unless there is no other way to indicate their invalid state) until after the user has **finished interacting with them.**

  If we accept this change (which `Form` and `Entry` already adheres to), this will complicate how the state is passed on. 
  The problem with the way `Form` does it, is that is gets the internal state from `Entry` (by virtue of being in the same package) to determine if the `Entry` is focused. This causes it not to work on anything other than an actual `Entry`. So one way to fix this would be to add a clause to the first rule:
  > - Producers must always pass on an update to the validation state **only as long as the user is not interacting with them**.

   However, this would mean that the validation state (at least in the consumer) isn't updated at all until after the user is no longer interacting with the producer, which is no good. It is useful for a consumer to demonstrate that the producer state is valid (ex. the submit button on a `Form` is enabled as soon as valid input is provided), so there needs to be some way to pass up that the state has changed while also including the fact that it hasn't finished changing (or something like that, i.e. the widget is still focused), or there needs to be a way to determine it's still being edited.

### Multiple Consumers:
Another question is should `SetOnValidationChanged()` not overwrite previously set callbacks? This would add a clause to the first rule: 
  > - Producers must always pass on an update to the validation state **to all it's consumers**.

  Additionally, this would likely require adding a `Delete()` method to the `Validator` interface, or to just create a new interface (something like `MultipleParentValidator`) that includes `Delete()`. The second method is fine as it is makes no real difference to a parent as long as it receives an update. But honestly, I don't think being able to delete a callback is strictly required.

fyne-io/fyne.title: Improvement on handling image decoding inside Fyne

labels.name: optimization
labels.description: Tickets that could help Fyne apps run faster

fyne-io/fyne.body:
### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe:
Currently there is a bit of an oddity with Fyne canvas image. They are sized and decoded inside the rendering goroutine, triggering a Refresh from it. Basically the first frame rendering a freshly decoded image is likely going to be incorrect and automatically trigger a second redraw.

Also as filename instead of handler are used, especially for cache, it is possible that the file that was on disk at the moment of Refresh, at the moment the image was decoded for the first time and at the time it is finally displayed to not match properly.

Finally Decoding image in the rendering thread will lead to all the CPU heavy task to be serialized and slow down rendering when this happen.

### Is it possible to construct a solution with the existing API?
We might need a new API if we want to introduce asynchronous image decoding (aka delay Refresh until the image is decoded).

### Describe the solution you'd like to see:
The idea would be to use a TeeReader and do a DecodeConfig inside the canvas.Image code before any rendering. This would properly do MinSize and friends on the canvas.Image directly. On Refresh and if necessary, it would spawn a goroutine that will do the Decode of the image and send the resulting image.Image over a channel. The render thread would block on that render thread until the image is decoded.

For an asynchronous decode facilty, instead of Refresh sending things to a channel to the rendering goroutine, it would introduce a new call that would trigger instead a callback to notify us when the image is decoded.

Doing so would address all the issue above.

Even if not detected by go, this could be considered a race condition like reported in #1028 for example.

fyne-io/fyne.title: Font scale doesn't respect Gnome settigs
fyne-io/fyne.body:
<!-- Please search for open issues that relate to the same feature before opening a new one. -->

### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe:
I remark that all Fyne application are displayed with very large police size. I generally need to set `FYNE_SCALE` environment variable to 0.8 to make the application like my others windows.

I realized that I set up "font scale factor" in Gnome to 0.9, and of course Fyne doesn't read the value.

Of course we can configure this in "settings" but the "default" is badly set to "1" if no configuration is set. IMHO Fyne should get the Gnome scale factor in consideration.

### Is it possible to construct a solution with the existing API?
Yes, I do it with this:

```go
func GetScaleFactor() string {
	// if the OS is Linux and gsettings is installed
	// get gsettings get org.gnome.desktop.interface text-scaling-factor
	// and return it
	// else return 1
	if runtime.GOOS == "linux" {
		if _, err := exec.LookPath("gsettings"); err == nil {
			out, err := exec.Command("gsettings", "get", "org.gnome.desktop.interface", "text-scaling-factor").Output()
			if err != nil {
				log.Println("Error while getting gsettings", err)
				return "1"
			}
			// we only get 3 runes
			scaleString := string(out)
			// remove \n and spaces
			scaleString = strings.Trim(scaleString, " ")
			scaleString = strings.TrimRight(scaleString, "\n")

			// set to float to round the value
			scale, err := strconv.ParseFloat(scaleString, 64)
			if err != nil {
				log.Println("Error while parsing gsettings", err)
				return "1"
			}
			// round to 2 decimals
			scale = float64(int(scale*100)) / 100
			return strconv.FormatFloat(scale, 'f', 2, 64)
		}
	}
	return "1"
}
```
Then I do in my `init` function:
```go
os.Setenv("FYNE_SCALE", GetScaleFactor())
```

And magically, everything is OK

### Describe the solution you'd like to see:
Maybe my function can be called automatically from Fyne, in `init()` or something more internal.

My function doesn't break anything on others OS.

fyne-io/fyne.body:
Although this feature is not extremely important for me, but I want to point out that at present there is no simple and clear API to create sequential animations, when each animation from the sequence is executed after the previous animation is completed.
With today's API, animations by their writing look like they are executed sequentially, but in fact they are executed in parallel. 
Why in the Go language should I write as in JavaScript when I specifically want to get away from that? 
Unfortunately, this can no longer be fixed due to backward incompatibility.

**Describe the solution you'd like to see:**

It is proposed to have two objects for navigation sequences:
```go
anim1=canvas.newParallelAnimation(
	rgbanim1 := canvas.newRGBAAnimation(),
	moveanim1 := canvas.newPositionAnimation(),
	...
)
anim1.start()

anim2=canvas.newSequentialAnimation(
	rgbanim2 := canvas.newRGBAAnimation(),
	moveanim2 := canvas.newPositionAnimation(),
	...
)
anim2.start()
```

fyne-io/fyne.title: Form with multiple columns
fyne-io/fyne.body:
### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe:
If you have a form with lots of form items, the form's minimum height grows but the minimum width stays the same. If the form get's too long you have to put it inside a VScroll but that makes it cumbersome to enter the data, since you need to enter some, scroll a bit and repeat. This also makes it so you can't see all your entered data at a glance (potential errors too) and wastes most horizontal space.

### Is it possible to construct a solution with the existing API?
You can put multiple forms side by side, therefore using more horizontal space. The problem with this approach is that you have to juggle multiple forms now (all but one without a submit button and one with) and prevent the submission of the last if any of the others have an error.

### Describe the solution you'd like to see:
Instead of having the form only growing vertically, it would be good to extend it so it can have multiple columns of form item to make better use of the available space. It should also be possible to set the amount of those columns (this should be 1 by default) and the form should automatically balance the form items on these: If you have 3 columns, the first three form items should go on the first row, the next three on the second row and so on.

fyne-io/fyne.title: List with databinding has issues when the list gets too long and the user is scrolling fast
fyne-io/fyne.body:
<!-- Please search for open issues that relate to the same problem before opening a new one. -->

### Describe the bug:
My test app is based on the data binding tutorial. While the tutorial binds a StringList to the list widget, I need a list of custom structs. So I implemented all the required interfaces for Person (simple custom struct) and PersonList (the actual list of Person). I also exchanged the Label in the List widget with an Entry, since I need the possibility to change items in my list. I did not fully implement RemoveListener() but I verified it is never called, so it is not relevant. My test app has 2 buttons rather than one: "Give Birth" adds a single Person to PersonList, "Open Orphanage" adds 1,000 new Person to PersonList. So far, so good. Everything looks fine at a first glance. Adding persons works. My custom back-end list knows about all the persons added in the frontend. Name changes applied in the Entry widget are updated in the backend. Unfortunately scrolling fast down and up again will make things messy: somewhere the rendering of the widgets doesn't get updated anymore. There must be some kind of race condition: I can see my CPU being busy on multiple cores when scrolling (4 out of 12). At the end, all names are shuffled on the screen.


### To Reproduce:
Steps to reproduce the behaviour:
1. Run app, resize window to reasonable size
2. Click on 'Open Orphanage'
3. Scroll down to the end
4. The last items are supposed to be ..., "Child 997", "Child 998", "Child 999"
5. Scroll up to the start
6. The first items are supposed to be "Adam", "Eve", "Child 1", ...

See errors in step 4 and 6...

### Screenshots:
Sorry, my screenshot tool is not compatible to Gnome 41. ... Just run the example... you will see.


### Example code:
```go
package main

import (
	"fmt"
	"log"

	"fyne.io/fyne/v2"
	"fyne.io/fyne/v2/app"
	"fyne.io/fyne/v2/container"
	"fyne.io/fyne/v2/data/binding"
	"fyne.io/fyne/v2/widget"
)

type Person struct {
	lastName  binding.String
	firstName binding.String
	listeners []binding.DataListener
}

func (p *Person) AddListener(listener binding.DataListener) {
	log.Println("LISTENER on Person added")
}

func (p *Person) RemoveListener(listener binding.DataListener) {
	log.Println("LISTENER on Person removed")
}

type PersonList struct {
	persons   []Person
	listeners []binding.DataListener
}

func (pl *PersonList) GetItem(index int) (binding.DataItem, error) {
	return &pl.persons[index], nil
}

func (pl *PersonList) Length() int {
	return len(pl.persons)
}

func (pl *PersonList) AddListener(listener binding.DataListener) {
	pl.listeners = append(pl.listeners, listener)
	log.Println("LISTENER on PersonList added")
}

func (pl *PersonList) RemoveListener(listener binding.DataListener) {
	log.Println("LISTENER on PersonList removed")
}

func (pl *PersonList) Append(p Person) {
	pl.persons = append(pl.persons, p)
	for l := range pl.listeners {
		pl.listeners[l].DataChanged()
	}
}

func main() {
	myApp := app.New()
	myWindow := myApp.NewWindow("List Data")

	var adam = Person{lastName: binding.NewString(), firstName: binding.NewString(), listeners: make([]binding.DataListener, 0)}
	adam.lastName.Set("Mayer")
	adam.firstName.Set("Adam")
	var eve = Person{lastName: binding.NewString(), firstName: binding.NewString(), listeners: make([]binding.DataListener, 0)}
	eve.lastName.Set("Mayer")
	eve.firstName.Set("Eve")

	var rawList = PersonList{persons: make([]Person, 0), listeners: make([]binding.DataListener, 0)}
	rawList.Append(adam)
	rawList.Append(eve)
	log.Printf("length of raw list: %d", rawList.Length())

	list := widget.NewListWithData(&rawList,
		func() fyne.CanvasObject {
			var w = widget.NewEntry()
			w.SetText("Template")
			return w
		},
		func(i binding.DataItem, o fyne.CanvasObject) {
			o.(*widget.Entry).Bind(i.(*Person).firstName)
		})

	add := widget.NewButton("Give Birth", func() {
		var child = Person{lastName: binding.NewString(), firstName: binding.NewString(), listeners: make([]binding.DataListener, 0)}
		child.firstName.Set(fmt.Sprintf("Child %d", rawList.Length()-1))
		child.lastName.Set("Mayer")
		rawList.Append(child)
	})
	mess := widget.NewButton("Open Orphanage", func() {
```

fyne-io/fyne.title: Adapter from Repository to fs.FS

labels.name: Storage
labels.description: changes relating to Storage Repositories and URIs

fyne-io/fyne.body:
Starting in Go 1.16, the [`io/fs`](https://pkg.go.dev/io/fs) package provides a set of interfaces for abstracting filesystem access. Where possible we should inter-operate with these types with the storage repository system. It will be a bit of an odd fit though - storage repositories are designed to handle arbitrary URIs, while `io/fs` assume you have an explicit filesystem root.

My instinct would be to create two adapters. One would adapt a storage repository to an `fs.FS` rooted at a particular URI, something like `NewFSFromURI(uri fyne.URI)`. Nearly all of the methods translate directly or almost directly, except for stat-related things (see also: #2233, #2134). The other adapter would go the other way around, creating a repository from an `fs.FS`, probably something like `RegisterFSAsRepository(protocol string)`. The latter may be the impetus for finally implementing the "routed repository" (a repository which registers for a protocol as usual, but internally routes access to specific URIs to nested sub-repositories).

These two things are probably separate PRs.

**NOTE**: we still support back to Go 1.14. Until 1.16 is our minimum supported version, we can't implement this in a way that makes the build depend on it. 

- [ ] `fs.FS` -> repository
    - [ ] proposal (insert link here)

- [ ] repository -> `fs.FS`

fyne-io/fyne.title: Don't bundle fonts where possible
fyne-io/fyne.body:
<!-- Please search for open issues that relate to the same feature before opening a new one. -->

### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe:
<!-- A clear and concise description of what the problem is. Ex. I'm always frustrated when [...] -->
Binary sizes are relatively large which means that they both take up more disk space but also require more time to download and so on. To save space, I would suggest that we avoid bundling fonts into the binaries in situations where we don't have to.

I realise that we still need to do so for some platforms if we want to be sure that we can show text correctly. I guess this would be Linux and BSD? However, I think we should try and don't bundle them on systems where we can expect there to be correct fonts installed. I guess this would be macOS, iOS and possibly Windows and Android as well?

### Is it possible to construct a solution with the existing API?
<!-- If this is an enhancement have you been able to create something similar,
or is your desired outcome not possible at this time? -->
I think it would be possible to just check the operating system using build constraints and then read fonts from the operating system where when where we can.

### Describe the solution you'd like to see:
<!-- A clear and concise description of what you want to happen. -->
Bundling fonts where we have to and not doing so when we don't have to.
I have done a very rough test (the binaires without fonts were not changed to be runnable) using Go 1.16 and these were the results that I got:
| Build                 | Before  | After   | Difference |
|-----------------------|---------|---------|------------|
| With debug symbols    | 16.9 MB | 14.7 MB | 2.2 MB     |
| Without debug symbols | 12.9 MB | 10.7 MB | 2.2 MB     |

Thus it seems that we can remove 2.2 MB when avodinging bundled fonts.

<!-- Please search for open issues that relate to the same feature before opening a new one. -->

### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe:
<!-- A clear and concise description of what the problem is. Ex. I'm always frustrated when [...] -->
I would really like to embed a code editor into a Fyne app. The closest match to the features expected of such a widget is the `TextGrid`, but it's read-only with no selection model.

### Is it possible to construct a solution with the existing API?
<!-- If this is an enhancement have you been able to create something similar,
or is your desired outcome not possible at this time? -->
Talking with @andydotxyz it seems like it could be possible with one of two approaches:
1. Use the rich text support coming in 2.2-ish to support things like syntax highlighting, but (AFAIK) rich text doesn't support things like line numbers, tab width, addressable row/column, etc.
2. Do the work of making an editable derivative like `EditableTextGrid`. It sounds like the initial approach would be copying a lot of code from `Entry` over to the derivative.

### Describe the solution you'd like to see:
<!-- A clear and concise description of what you want to happen. -->
I think it's too much to ask for an IntelliJ code editor window, so here's a summary of features outside of just editing that would satisfy my use case or allow me to build additional features around it like working with feedback from a language server.
* Line numbers
* Different text styles within the widget (syntax highlighting)
* Monospace font
* Addressable row/column
* Viewing whitespace if desired
* Tab width

Personally, I think `TextGrid` is closer to what I would like to see than the rich text widget. However, it sounds like some thought would need to go into collecting text handling like input, selection, shortcuts, and mouse clicks into an abstraction over the widget handling those sorts of gestures.

I think that Entry is really great for its designed use, which is providing a consistent look and feel for general purpose text entry. With the creation of the rich text widget Fyne is graduating from general purpose I/O to purpose built widgets that provide a ton of value. I think that an editable `TextGrid` would add tremendous value to your users by allowing them to build the software that builds other things, and it could also be very useful in Defyne for giving people a familiar experience.

fyne-io/fyne.title: Binding "Must*" variants
fyne-io/fyne.body:
<!-- Please search for open issues that relate to the same feature before opening a new one. -->

### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe:
<!-- A clear and concise description of what the problem is. Ex. I'm always frustrated when [...] -->
Struct binding is a little clunky to use with all of the error handling involved. First the user must bind to the struct, and then they'll want to bind to fields within the struct. Consider this example.
https://play.golang.org/p/Afw8NqQv6lR

Another case shown in the playground link is when manipulating a bound value with `Get` and `Set`. In this case it's not immediately clear to the user why either method *should* return an error in the first place, but an error returned must be an error handled. This is troublesome enough that even fyne examples don't always handle this error, and the user should be able to opt out of handling it in favor of panicking.

An idiomatic way to accomplish this behavior could be borrowed from something like the regexp package in the standard library. It has "Must" variants of functions for situations where the user knows that if the regex fails to compile, something critical will not work, so the best option is to panic.
https://pkg.go.dev/regexp#MustCompile

### Is it possible to construct a solution with the existing API?
<!-- If this is an enhancement have you been able to create something similar,
or is your desired outcome not possible at this time? -->
The current solution is the problem. Errors must be handled - in some cases it's not clear why - and there should be an alternative.

### Describe the solution you'd like to see:
<!-- A clear and concise description of what you want to happen. -->
Provide "Must" variants of binding interaction functions. See the go playground link above for comments showing suggestions with struct binding and working with field binding Get/Set.

fyne-io/fyne.title: Should Unbind() guarantee that widgets stop responding to data changes?

labels.name: data binding
labels.description: Issue related to bug or improvement of data binding

fyne-io/fyne.body:
<!-- Please search for open issues that relate to the same feature before opening a new one. -->

### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe:

**That's not a bug, more like an API design question.** So I'm not sure if the issue tracker is a good place to put it. Suppose we have a `binding.DataItem` with some listener L. Then calling `RemoveListener(L)` does not guarantee that L will not be called in the future. This behavior is not explicitly documented, but it's clear from the implementation: some calls to listener L may be already scheduled in the global queue (see `queueItem` in `data/binding/queue.go`), and removing L from the DataItem has no impact on the contents of the queue.

I think every listener currently used in fyne source code (i.e., in widgets bind/unbind methods) is implemented carefully enough to avoid crashes even if the listener is invoked at a wrong time. Listeners are typically closures, holding references to many different things. Not crashing is good, but the listeners in widgets Bind/Unbind have side effects. For example if you 

1. bind a slider to `sliderData binding.Float`
2. modify sliderData a lot
3. unbind the slider data
4. modify sliderData one last time

Then almost surely the slider would switch to the value you set in the fourth step. I've attached some example code below. (*Exercise*: if you do the same with a Label bound to `binding.String`, something else would happen almost every time. Why?)

**Of course, Bind/Unbind() API give no explicit guarantees**, so a developer expecting some different outcome is technically in the wrong. It just feels like a footgun. I mean, the current API design makes it very natural to write invalid code with concurrency bugs. If I were to write a moderately complicated application that uses data binding and custom listeners on data items, I would probably not be vigilant enough to avoid concurrency bugs.

For example, create a widget with bound data, modify it a bit, then destroy that widget (e.g., close a secondary window in the application). Then modifying the bound data may have invisible side effects even if the widget is now inaccessible from your code. If you are not careful, this may lead to a crash, but it could also lead to nasty concurrency bugs if the listener also modifies some shared state!

### Is it possible to construct a solution with the existing API?

I don't really have any specific opinions about what should be done. There are many options.

**Option 1.** Maybe the API is OK as is. The developers should pay attention to promises and lack of promises provided by the Bind()/Unbind(), just like any other concurrent API.

**Option 2.** Maybe RemoveListener should have an annoying warning in the docstring, something like

```go
// Warning: RemoveListener(L) does not guarantee that L will not
// be called in the future. You may need to call waitForItems()
// and accept an unpredictable delay if you need that guarantee.
```

And then also each Unbind() method should get a similar annoying warning.

**Option 3.** Maybe Unbind() should first call RemoveListener(), then call waitForItems() to empty the queue, and only then start to modify the internal widget state (references to `binding.DataItem` etc). This would make it harder for developers to accidentally write invalid code that uses Bind/Unbind. This may be good enough: custom data listeners are an advanced topic, but using Bind/Unbind seems to be designed to be convenient for developers, so making them more ergonomic may be worth it. But this may be very slow for use-cases like a data-bound list that constantly Binds/Unbinds list items while scrolling.

**Option 4.** Maybe already RemoveListener() is not user-friendly, and should be fixed to also cancel all scheduled calls to the specified listener. It's also a public API, so it may be worth trying to make it more ergonomic. So maybe the global listeners queue should have more responsibilities: for example, it could accept a request "please ignore all currently scheduled calls to listener L" and store this information internally. This would be easier when the queue will stop pretending to be a channel (#2561). There are probably efficient data structures to store the exclusion list. It would be self-expiring: each ignore request should be tracked only until the task that was the last at the ignore request moment is fulfilled.

There are many other solutions, I guess.

### Describe the solution you'd like to see:

Choosing a solution here is kind of a global decision that requires a full vision of what fyne wants to be, so I don't know.

### Example code

If you run the following code, you'll see that:
1. Slider is always set to 1.0 at the end, even though this assignment never happens while the slider is bound to sliderData.
2. Label is almost never set to "OUT OF THE LOOP", which is kind of good, but it's also almost never set to "Loop 3999", which may not be what you expect. Instead of 3999, you get "Loop 3987", "Loop 3992", and other random numbers.
3. A joint stress-test of bindings produces slightly wilder results due to heavier queue load.

```go
package main

import (
	"fmt"

	"fyne.io/fyne/v2"
	"fyne.io/fyne/v2/app"
	"fyne.io/fyne/v2/container"
	"fyne.io/fyne/v2/data/binding"
	"fyne.io/fyne/v2/layout"
	"fyne.io/fyne/v2/widget"
)

func main() {

	a := app.NewWithID("test")
	w := a.NewWindow("Binding stress test")

	labelData := binding.NewString()
	labelData.Set("First value")

	sliderData := binding.NewFloat()
	sliderData.Set(0.5)

	label := widget.NewLabelWithData(labelData)
	slider := widget.NewSliderWithData(0, 1, sliderData)
	button1 := widget.NewButton("Label stress test", func() {
		label.Bind(labelData)
		go func() {
			for i := 0; i < 4000; i++ {
				labelData.Set(fmt.Sprintf("Loop %d", i))
			}
			labelData.Set("After the loop")
			label.Unbind()
			labelData.Set("OUT OF THE LOOP")
		}()
	})
	button2 := widget.NewButton("Slider stress test", func() {
		slider.Bind(sliderData)
		go func() {
			for i := 0; i < 4000; i++ {
				sliderData.Set(float64(0.5) - (float64(i) * float64(0.00001)))
			}
			sliderData.Set(float64(0))
			slider.Unbind()
			sliderData.Set(float64(1))
		}()
	})
	button3 := widget.NewButton("Joint stress test", func() {
		label.Bind(labelData)
		slider.Bind(sliderData)
		go func() {
			for i := 0; i < 4000; i++ {
				labelData.Set(fmt.Sprintf("Loop %d", i))
				sliderData.Set(float64(0.5) - (float64(i) * float64(0.00001)))
			}
			labelData.Set("After the loop")
			sliderData.Set(float64(0))
			label.Unbind()
			slider.Unbind()
			labelData.Set("OUT OF THE LOOP")
			sliderData.Set(float64(1))
		}()
	})

	vbox := container.New(layout.NewVBoxLayout(), label, slider, button1, button2, button3)

	w.SetContent(vbox)
	w.Resize(fyne.NewSize(600, 300))
	w.ShowAndRun()
}
```

fyne-io/fyne.title: An idle application with no visible windows still uses noticeable CPU time

fyne-io/fyne.body:
<!-- Please search for open issues that relate to the same problem before opening a new one. -->

### Describe the bug:
I am writing a desktop GUI application that would be usually running in the background, with minimized window that is opened from time to time. I've discovered that any fyne application, including `fyne_demo` or even a simple window with a single label in it, puts some consistent CPU load even if the application window is not visible and no work is being done. It's not a large amount of CPU usage, but over time it adds up to a battery drain, making even the most basic fyne application the 8th largest energy consumer on my laptop if left running for 20 hours (assuming that a large portion of those 20 hours are spent in the web browser). That's more demanding than, e.g., Telegram chat client even though that program is actually being used actively for some portion of those 20 hours, not just stalling in the background.

On my computer, the background load (of any fyne application that does no work in the background) is 3-4% CPU usage, as reported by "Activity Monitor" of my OS. This can be confirmed with standard golang CPU profiling: it reports 1.27s of CPU time during 30.03s of running in the background:

[![Profiling idle fyne application](https://i.ibb.co/rpC9qDT/default-settings.png)](https://svgshare.com/i/a_f.svg)

As one can see from this not very informative graphic, a small amount of work (~0.17s out of 1.27s CPU usage) is being done in `glfw.PollEvents` as invoked in `runGL`, but the majority of time is spent by golang's scheduling mechanism (`runtime.schedule` and its friends). I don't know what exactly is this scheduling mechanism working on. It is my impression that channel communication, for example, performing`select` over several channels, may be part of this.

### Ticker tuning helps, but not completely

Fyne's `runGL` from `internal/driver/glfw/loop.go` is an event loop which, in particular, polls GLFW events 60 times a second, triggered by the messages on a channel created by `time.Ticker`. This frequency is constant, regardless of whether the application window is visible or not. Even though profiling does not indicate that `runGL` is a significant CPU consumer, it is possible that some part of `runtime.schedule` CPU usage is the overhead for the `select` statement reading from several channels in `runGL` loop, since that `select` is performed 60 times per second. This is in fact the case.

As an experiment, I reduced the ticker frequency (by editing `loop.go`) to a rather extreme "1 event per second". This reduced background CPU load by a factor of two. Only 0.63s of CPU time were used during 30s of running in the background:

[![Ticker tuning](https://i.ibb.co/D7FK4g4/ticker-tuning.png)](https://svgshare.com/i/aZi.svg)

Thus I would suggest **some dynamic tuning of the ticker frequency** as an enhancement of `runGL`: if the application window is not visible, maybe run the ticker only 10 times per second, or something like that. This would significantly improve the energy usage for fyne applications running in the background.

However, a consistent 1-2% CPU load is still not the best experience for a background application that does absolutely nothing. This is worse than the majority of background applications my computer is currently running. I'm not sure what can be done to reduce the scheduler load since I don't know what causes it. I haven't checked whether the channel `funcQueue` in `runGL` wakes often -- if it is, maybe the same `select` loop in `runGL` is responsible for the entire background load.

Another option that I didn't try is to update Go: maybe new versions of golang have a more efficient runtime scheduler. But probably something can be done on the fyne level to reduce the load anyway.

### To Reproduce:
Steps to reproduce the behaviour:
1. Run any fyne application, e.g., fyne_demo.
2. Keep it in the background.
3. Check your CPU load with whatever process monitor you have.

 - **Go version:** go1.15.3 darwin/amd64
 - **Fyne version:** 6e90820ea9ca4df836db5a99384c51073415571e

fyne-io/fyne.title: Custom widgets implementing TappedSecondary() are not selectable in widget.List
fyne-io/fyne.body:
<!-- Please search for open issues that relate to the same problem before opening a new one. -->

### Describe the bug:
<!-- A clear and concise description about the bug. -->
The list widget can handle custom widgets as items. However, if the widget used as a list item implements TappedSecondary() callback, user loses the ability to select list elements by left-clicking on them, even though the behavior of the left click should not change.

Additional notes:
1. If a custom widget also implements Tapped() callback, it works as expected: it is called when the user clicks on the widget in the list. However, I haven't found any way to propagate this event to the list item widget, so the ability to select elements still does not work.
2. Clicking very close to the separator lines in the list widget selects the nearby list items, as expected.

### To Reproduce:
Steps to reproduce the behaviour:
1. Run the minimal example given below.
2. Tap list items.
3. Observe that the items do not become selected.

### Example code:
```go
package main

import (
	"log"

	"fyne.io/fyne/v2"
	"fyne.io/fyne/v2/app"
	"fyne.io/fyne/v2/canvas"
	"fyne.io/fyne/v2/theme"
	"fyne.io/fyne/v2/widget"
)

// === CUSTOM WIDGET BOILERPLATE ===

type CustomWidget struct {
	widget.BaseWidget
	text string
}

func (w *CustomWidget) Resize(size fyne.Size) {
	w.BaseWidget.Resize(size)
}

type CustomWidgetRenderer struct {
	textWidget *canvas.Text
	objects    []fyne.CanvasObject
	w          *CustomWidget
}

func (r *CustomWidgetRenderer) MinSize() fyne.Size {
	return fyne.NewSize(float32(400), float32(20))
}

func (r *CustomWidgetRenderer) Layout(size fyne.Size) {
	textSize := r.textWidget.MinSize()
	r.textWidget.Resize(textSize)
	r.textWidget.Move(fyne.NewPos(float32(0), float32(0)))
}

func (r *CustomWidgetRenderer) Refresh() {
	r.textWidget.Text = r.w.text
	r.Layout(r.w.Size())
}

func (r *CustomWidgetRenderer) Destroy() {
}

func (r *CustomWidgetRenderer) Objects() []fyne.CanvasObject {
	return r.objects
}

func (w *CustomWidget) CreateRenderer() fyne.WidgetRenderer {
	w.ExtendBaseWidget(w)
	r := &CustomWidgetRenderer{
		w: w,
	}
	r.textWidget = canvas.NewText(w.text, theme.ForegroundColor())
	r.objects = []fyne.CanvasObject{r.textWidget}
	return r
}

func newCustomWidget(text string) *CustomWidget {
	w := &CustomWidget{
		text: text,
	}
	w.ExtendBaseWidget(w)
	return w
}

// === DEFINING TappedSecondary() METHOD FOR THE CUSTOM WIDGET ===

func (w *CustomWidget) TappedSecondary(_ *fyne.PointEvent) {
	w.ExtendBaseWidget(w)
	log.Printf("Tapped secondary event\n")
}

// NOTE:
// Extending Tapped() is also possible.
// If this is uncommented, the callback is correctly invoked by fyne, but
// I don't know how to propagate the tap event back to the list widget.

// func (w *CustomWidget) Tapped(_ *fyne.PointEvent) {
// 	w.ExtendBaseWidget(w)
// 	log.Printf("Tapped event\n")
// }

// === WINDOW CREATION AND THE DEMONSTRATION OF THE BUG ===

func main() {
	app := app.New()
	w := app.NewWindow("List with custom widgets")

	listContents := []string{"Item 1", "Item 2", "Item 3"}

	list := widget.NewList(
		func() int {
			return len(listContents)
		},
		func() fyne.CanvasObject {
			return newCustomWidget("")
		},
		func(id widget.ListItemID, o fyne.CanvasObject) {
			o.(*CustomWidget).text = listContents[id]
			o.Refresh()
		},
	)

	list.OnSelected = func(id widget.ListItemID) {
		log.Printf("Selected item %d\n", id+1)
	}
	list.OnUnselected = func(id widget.ListItemID) {
		log.Printf("Unselected item %d\n", id+1)
	}

	w.SetContent(list)
	w.Resize(fyne.NewSize(float32(500), float32(300)))
	w.ShowAndRun()
}
```

fyne-io/fyne.title: widgets with scroll may stop responding to mouse
fyne-io/fyne.body:
### Describe the bug:
Widgets such as Entry, List, Tree, Table and Menu will create a new Scroll when a CreateRenderer is called.
Because renderer cache may be cleared, the new Scroll (and others) will be recreated again. 
However, the Scroll will not resize and mouse events won't be delivered to the widget because walkObjectTree can't see any objects inside the Scroll since the clipSize is zero.
The only way to gain control over the rouge Scroll is to resize the window.

### To Reproduce:
The easiest way to reproduce is to have an application with two windows.
1. Run code from https://gist.github.com/zdima/46f522c359de7d6dc75f7fdf00ca15de, and arrange windows so you can see both.
2. Select the entry field of a main window.
3. Switch to another app on a desktop
4. Wait for about 90-120 seconds
5. Click on entry field to gain window focus.
6. Wait for 3-5 seconds and try to hover or select an item in the list of the second window - not possible.

### Device (please complete the following information):
 - **OS:** MacOS (should have the same issue on other desktop platforms) 
 - **Version:** 11.4 Big Sur
 - **Go version:** go version go1.16.5 darwin/amd64
 - **Fyne version:** fyne-dev

fyne-io/fyne.body:
Hi !

### Describe the bug:
In the following code, the w.Content().(*container.Scroll).Content  function works to save a scroll image to the disk. There is only one important detail that I noticed : in order to save the whole image, the scroll has to be positioned to show the top left corner. Otherwise the saved PNG is truncated. 


### To Reproduce:
Steps to reproduce the behaviour:
1. save a large PNG image with the name "image.png" in the code directory
2. execute the code
3. Scroll the image and click the button "screenshot" with different positions of the image in the scroll
4. open the output "test.png" : depending on the image position it is truncated or no


### Example code:

```
package main
import (
    "fyne.io/fyne/v2"
    "fyne.io/fyne/v2/app"
    "fyne.io/fyne/v2/canvas"
    "fyne.io/fyne/v2/container"
    "fyne.io/fyne/v2/driver/software"
    "fyne.io/fyne/v2/theme"
    "fyne.io/fyne/v2/widget"
    "image"
    "image/color"
    "image/png"
    "log"
    "os"
)
func main() {
    a := app.New()
    w := a.NewWindow("Sign")
    wContent := container.NewScroll(makePicture())
    w.SetContent(wContent)
    w.Resize(fyne.NewSize(120, 120))
    w.Show()
    // save image button
    w2 := a.NewWindow("Tool Box")
    but := widget.NewButton("screenshot", func() {
        // save the scroll containt to file
        c := w.Content().(*container.Scroll).Content
        img := software.Render(c, theme.DarkTheme())
        saveimage(img)
    })
    w2.SetContent(but)
    w2.ShowAndRun()
    w.ShowAndRun()
}
func makePicture() fyne.CanvasObject {
    image := canvas.NewImageFromFile("image.png")
    image.FillMode = canvas.ImageFillOriginal // this line is responsible for the bug
    bg := canvas.NewCircle(color.NRGBA{255, 0, 0, 255})
    bg.StrokeColor = color.White
    bg.StrokeWidth = 5
    bg.Resize(fyne.NewSize(100, 100))
    bg.Move(fyne.NewPos(10, 10))
    c := container.NewMax(image, bg)
    return c
}
func saveimage(out image.Image) {
    path := "test.png"
    outputFile, err := os.Create(path)
    if err != nil {
        log.Println("The image cannot be saved to the file")
    }
    png.Encode(outputFile, out)
    log.Println("Saving image to ", path)
    outputFile.Close()
}
```

Linux Manjaro
Go version: 1.6.3
Fyne version: 2.0.3

fyne-io/fyne.title: storage: Support for getting an os.FileInfo (or similar) from URI

labels.name: Storage
labels.description: changes relating to Storage Repositories and URIs

fyne-io/fyne.body:
### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe:
For regular operating system file management, `os.FileInfo` (renamed to `fs.FileInfo` and used within the `fs` package as well as of Go 1.16) is a standardized way of getting information about certain parts of data. 
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/25466657/113511726-9e971580-9561-11eb-9134-e25d191a38d8.png)
This opens up the possibility of getting data such as size, permissions and modification date (if the URI has that data) and so on. While a URI technically does not need to be a file, it would be good to have it be able to return this type in order to thus be compatible with many other use cases and we can just fill in the data with as much as we have.

My personal use case for this is in wormhole-gui where I need to know how big the file is before it is being sent, and without buffering all the data to memory first, it is not quite possible to know that.

### Is it possible to construct a solution with the existing API?
<!-- If this is an enhancement have you been able to create something similar,
or is your desired outcome not possible at this time? -->
I think so. For regular files, this should be easy enough to just wrap `os.Stat()`. For other URI handling on mobile platforms, I think we would need to hook into platform specific APIs to get the data and then fill the `os.FileMode` with as much data as we can get.

### Describe the solution you'd like to see:
<!-- A clear and concise description of what you want to happen. -->
We should be able to do something like `Stat(uri fyne.URI) (os.FileMode, error)`. 

cc @andydotxyz @charlesdaniels

fyne-io/fyne.title: focus-responsive Edit Menu (for use in MainMenu)
fyne-io/fyne.body:
### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe:

While you can `SetMainMenu` and make an `Edit` Menu with its various entries... they would not update to reflect the user's focus, and the condition of the focused widgets (such that you can only `Select All` and `Copy` from a Readonly widget, and probably not anything for a Disabled one.)

Common/Standard `Edit` Menu Entries:

```
Undo       # ext
Redo       # ext
---        # ext
Cut
Copy
Paste
Delete     # ext
---        # ext
Select All # ext
```

Anything marked `#ext` is an "Extended Edit" Menu Entry, e.g: not available in 100% of applications implementing an `Edit` menu. However, anything without this mark should be considered a standard.

### Is it possible to construct a solution with the existing API?

Yes, but it wouldn't be pretty. (see "solution")

Since `Menu` is not an interface, we can't have a literal `EditMenu` struct with a toggle, hence the bool in the constructor.

### Describe the solution you'd like to see:

```golang
// package fyne
NewEditMenu(extended bool, items ...*MenuItem) *EditMenu
```

#### Sample 1

```golang
	w.SetMainMenu(fyne.NewMainMenu(
		fyne.NewMenu("File", /* ... */),
		fyne.NewEditMenu(false),
		fyne.NewMenu("Tools", /* ... */),
		fyne.NewMenu("Help", /* ... */),
	))
```

**Expected**

```
File -> ...
Edit ->
  Cut
  Copy
  Paste
Tools -> ...
Help -> ...
```

#### Sample 2

```golang
	w.SetMainMenu(fyne.NewMainMenu(
		fyne.NewMenu("File", /* ... */),
		fyne.NewEditMenu(true),
	))
```

**Expected**

```
File -> ...
Edit ->
  Undo
  Redo
  ---
  Cut
  Copy
  Paste
  Delete
  ---
  Select All
```

#### Sample 3

```golang
	w.SetMainMenu(fyne.NewMainMenu(
		fyne.NewMenu("File", /* ... */),
		fyne.NewEditMenu(false, fyne.NewMenuItem("Preferences", func(){})),
	))
```

**Expected**

```
File -> ...
Edit ->
  Cut
  Copy
  Paste
  ---
  Preferences
```

---

Further, it is expected this menu would be omitted or hidden on mobile, where it's not applicable.

A `storage.Walk(root fyne.URI, walkFn storage.WalkFunc) error` function to walk over a uri. Using something like a `type WalkFunc func(uri fyne.URI, info os.FileInfo, err error) error` function.

fyne-io/fyne.title: Color Pipette in Picker

labels.name: future
labels.description: Features that might take a while to be sheduled

fyne-io/fyne.body:
In future, we may wish to support a "color pipette" in our color picker dialog. When clicked, it should allow the user to click somewhere else on the screen, sample the color there, and set that as the currently selected color. Many other color pickers support this, for example gcolor:

![](https://cdn.linuxiac.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/08/color-picker2.png)

Notice the pipette icon in the bottom left.

This may prove challenging, since different platforms may have different APIs in order to do this. It may require changes to the driver.

If we ever offer a screenshot API, this would likely go hand-in-hand, since the access to the display at OS level would be very similar I think.

I think this is probably a long way off, 3.X at the earliest. Putting this issue up to track discussion and progress. This is non-trivial enough that if someone wants to work on this, the next step would be to [create a proposal](https://github.com/fyne-io/fyne/wiki/Contributing:-Proposals). In particular, any proposal would need to include a plan for the implementation details of how we interface with the host OS in a cross-platform way.

labels.name: Accessibility

fyne-io/fyne.body:
We should expose some kind of function, such as a special key combination, button, menu element, etc. that will cause interactible elements to be highlighted clearly. This is distinct from adding a high-contrast theme, which will not distinguish interactable elements from non-interactible elements.

This will be useful to users to discover which elements they can interact with, and will also be valuable to the hard-of-vision for finding things on the screen.

fyne-io/fyne.title: Visualization Colors

labels.name: Accessibility
labels.description: Issues relating to accessibility, such as colorblind users, hard-of-sight users, etc.

fyne-io/fyne.body:
We should add a collection of theme colors for use in visualizations, rather than having downstream widget creators hard-code them. Example use cases:

* Drawing a graph where *n* different distinct colors are needed for *n* different lines
* Syntax-highlighting code in a text grid

This will allow themes to also control how visualizations and similar types of widgets appear easily, which will help the visual style remain more consistent when using custom themes. This will also make it easier to accommodate colorblind and hard of sight users who may need or want to utilize different color schemes for visualizations.

This has been discussed in the 2020-12-18 and 2021-01-08 meetings.

fyne-io/fyne.title: Fyne's handling of keys doesn't allow implementation of a remote control client
fyne-io/fyne.body:
### Describe the bug:

I'm working on a remote control application (think VNC or Remote Desktop) using Fyne and Fyne's handling of keys doesn't work for me for a number of reasons:

* It is impossible to differentiate between digits in keypad and main keyboard, however other keys will be differentiated (for example Enter and Keypad Enter are different into Fyne). I need to be able to send the correct events to the remote machine based on which keys are pressed so the result will match what the user is expecting.
* Fyne will translate some keys on non-US keyboards (for example A becomes Q in azerty) which means the wrong key will be sent for non-US keyboards.
* For keys that fyne doesn't know about, no event will be generated at all, meaning people with more keys (French 101 keys or Japanese 109 keys keyboards for example) will be missing some keys. 

I was able to workaround this with only one simple trick: exposing the original glfw key through the event data (see https://github.com/MagicalTux/fyne/commit/2309f844dff19df4b25f98289275c0494a7e4b6a - note: this is a temporary fix and isn't meant to be implemented as is).

This is not only fully compatible with Fyne (except for the fact that the event key name can be an empty string, this could be added in key.go as `KeyUnknown KeyName = ""`) but allows anyone who needs to access the original event data to do so easily.

This said revamping Fyne's keyboard handling is I believe needed, as not everybody will want keys to be adapted to the keymap, this depends strongly on the purpose. This event shouldn't have a `Sys interface{}` value, but maybe a `RawKey fyne.RawKey` value.

fyne-io/fyne.title: Make keyboard controls a first class citizen
fyne-io/fyne.body:
I hereby want to propose to make keyboard controls a first class citizen in the design of Fyne and especially its widgets.

Some other tickets already talk about accessibility (#1093 and #1285), so I think thinking about inputs is a very important step in that direction. There are multiple disabilities that make it hard to properly navigate a mouse or touchpad, and even with voice control (or joysticks) it is easier to give directional commands (up, down, left, right, next, back) than moving a cursor around.

A *widget* is already the base for every active component of the application. It can therefore be assumed, that each widget will in some way deal with user input (clicking, scrolling, entering content, etc.).

My proposal would therefore be, to implement the `Keyable` interface on the base `Widget`. (Bonus: expose `OnKeyDown`, `OnKeyUp`, `OnKeyTyped` etc. callbacks for custom code *outside* the widget (for the user of the widget; not for a sub-"class").)

The *FocusManager* (#1294) can likely deal with the tab order and deal with switching focus.

## Examples of key behavior:

* [x] **Global**: *tab* focuses the next component, *shift+tab* the previous
* [x] **List**: up/down moves the currently selected item.
* [ ] **Accordion**: up/down moves to the previous/next item, left/right folds/expands the current item
* [ ] **Tabs**: depending on the orientation left/right or up/down moves between tabs
* [x] **Select**: up/down changes the current selection
* [ ] **Slider**: space/enter toggles the state and arrows move to next position
* [x] **Table**: left/right/up/down navigates between cells
* [x] **Tree**: up/down changes selected node, left/right expands/folds a node with children
* [x] **Check**: space/enter toggles the state
* [x] **Radio**: up/down selects the previous/next item

### Special scenario: focus trap

For example a text control with formatting might want to use tab and shift+tab to actually indent or unindent text. For these cases, it must be possible to differentiate between "edit" and "navigate". Giving such a textbox focus, does *not* enter edit mode. Pressing *enter* would enter edit mode. Then tab/shift+tab are no longer used for navigation, but are propagated to the widget for use. Hitting *escape* will leave edit mode and switch back to navigiation mode. The widget is still highlighted/focused (so pressing *enter* would go back into edit mode, but tab/shift+tab would now navigate between controls).

Therefore it should be possible to mark a widget as *FocusTrappable* (or something like that). In this case, the *FocusManager* allows hitting "enter" to enter said trap. Afterwards *tab* and *shift+tab* are propagated to this widget (while it has focus). *Esc*(ape) however is handled by the *FocusManager* to take that exclusive/trap mode away again.

Focusing a trappable widget via mouse or finger tap whould immediately enter trapped mode.

## Why do this "soon"?

The more widgets Fyne has, the more will have to be reworked to get a proper input flow. Given the current recommendation on how to extend widgets (implementing input interfaces yourself) would likely break when implementing those same interfaces on the base widget already. So the sooner this functionality moves to the core, the less trouble will be encountered later.

Also it's easier to design a widget with keyboard control in mind, than reworking existing widgets to be keyboard controlled.

This is also why I propose to implement the `Keyable` interface on `Widget`, so every widget implementation knows it has to deal with this. During design.

fyne-io/fyne.title: Consistent Selection API
fyne-io/fyne.body:
### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe:
Selection APIs in widgets and collections are inconsistent.

### Is it possible to construct a solution with the existing API?
n/a

### Describe the solution you'd like to see:
```go
Radio.ClearSelection()
Radio.SetSelectedOption(option string)
Radio.OnSelectionChanged(option string)

Select.ClearSelection()
Select.SelectedIndex() int
Select.SetSelectedOption(text string)
Select.SetSelectedIndex(index int)
Select.OnSelectionChanged(option string)

TabContainer.SelectedTab() *TabItem
TabContainer.SelectedIndex() int
TabContainer.SetSelectedTab(item *TabItem)
TabContainer.SetSelectedIndex(index int)
TabContainer.OnSelectionChanged(item *TabItem)

List.ClearSelection()
List.SelectedItem() int
List.SetSelectedItem(index int)
List.OnSelectionChanged(index int) // -1 == no selection

Table.ClearSelection()
Table.SelectedCell() (int, int)
Table.SetSelectedCell(row, col int)
Table.OnSelectionChanged(row, col int) // -1, -1 == no selection

Tree.ClearSelection()
Tree.SelectedNode() string
Tree.SetSelectedNode(uid string)
Tree.OnSelectionChanged(uid string) // tree.noSelection = "nothing" == no selection
```

Deprecation warning will be added in 1.4 and the APIs will be renamed in 2.0

n/a

On the Linux default file browser, you can press Ctrl-L to convert the row of buttons that show the current path into a text entry that allows you to cut and paste the present working directory. Thanks!

fyne-io/fyne.title: Remove CGo on Windows
fyne-io/fyne.body:
Installing a C compiler that works with Go on Windows means installing MinGW or Cygwin, both of which are no fun at all. I would like to be able to build a fyne application on Windows without dependencies. Another issue on Windows are missing OpenGL drivers. Windows works with DirectX natively. Yet another issue is cross-compiling for Windows from another OS which means installing the C compiler that produces Windows binaries there.

As long as fyne uses OpenGL on Windows it is complicated to replace CGo. I have not yet seen an OpenGL wrapper for Go that does not use CGo so you would have to create one. A C-less OpenGL still has other problems on Windows. Windows natively only supports GL 1.1 so you depend on a newer graphics driver to be installed on the user's computer. See issue #410 where OpenGL drivers are hard to install on a virtual machine.

I suggest creating a driver for Windows that replaces GLFW and OpenGL with the native WinAPI and Direct3D9. DirectX version 9 has been shipping with Windows XP and is still supported to this day, meaning it supports the widest range of Windows computers currently out there. This solves both the CGo and the driver problem.

I have been creating Windows desktop programs in Go for some years now. I have a [WinAPI wrapper](https://github.com/gonutz/w32) and a [Direct3D9 wrapper](https://github.com/gonutz/d3d9) in pure Go. I use these for example in my [Windows GUI library 'wui'](https://github.com/gonutz/wui) and in my [game framework 'prototype'](https://github.com/gonutz/prototype).

With these libraries it is possible to compile Windows binaries from pure Go and that do not depend on any extra DLLs at runtime. If you build a 32 bit binary, it can be run on any Windows OS >= XP. Cross compiling is supported by the Go toolchain so you just have to set `GOOS=windows` and can compile.

I would be very happy to contribute. Looking at the code I see that `glfw` and `go-gl` are only used in the `driver/glfw` and `painter/gl`. I will soon look to see what is necessary to replace these. I wanted to start the issue to see if this is wanted at all and what others have to say first.

fyne-io/fyne.title: Propose new raster scroll/zoom widget
fyne-io/fyne.body:
On the #fyne Slack channel @andydotxyz asked me to write up a list of wants for purposes of discussion.

For context, I come from a background of writing Engineering Design Automation (EDA) tools for chip design and would like to use `fyne` as a playground for some ideas I have. I stumbled across `fyne` recently and threw together a simple prototype (that needs some serious performance optimization) that can be tried out here: https://github.com/gmlewis/go-gerber/tree/master/examples/bifilar-coil with `go run main.go -view -n 20`.

The `canvas.NewRaster` turns out to be a fantastic way to render complex objects (although my quadtree needs serious help right now).

Additionally, I would like to see the following things supported on a `canvas.Image`:

* scroll events with `(x,y)` location of cursor at the moment of scroll.
  - This would allow you to recenter the design at the point of scrolling... but only if the next feature is available as well:
* re-position the cursor.
  - Upon the first scroll, you would recenter the design and immediately move the cursor to the center of the canvas so that further scrolls would keep the design centered there. This is amazingly intuitive and useful for the viewer to zoom into a particular feature no matter where it starts out on the screen.
* drag events with button modifier and `(x,y)` location of cursor during the drag.
  - For left mouse button, this would be used to move the design under the cursor as the mouse is being dragged with the button down
  - For 3D applications, middle and right mouse buttons could be used to zoom and rotate the design. Ideally, the cursor position would also be available for drag events in case the rotation might be around a different axis depending on where the drag started.

I hope this makes sense. Basically, with the above features, `fyne` could be used to make 3D apps and all sorts of EDA/CAD-like tools.

Oh, and while I have a wish-list platform, making it easier to manage a complex 2D or 3D scene would be greatly appreciated, although might be beyond the scope of this request. :smile:

fyne-io/fyne.title: Flexbox - like layout API
fyne-io/fyne.body:
Goal is to have something that is close to a HTML flexbox - like an N column grid, with colspans, and each column shrinking in width to fit the largest element. Useful for forms management.

First step is to create a custom layout, will use the xkcd example as a proof of concept.

Im thinking the API would end up something like this, passing in an options object, so each CanvasObject is wrapped in a higher order struct that has metadata about layout options  :

```
type gridOpts struct {
  Span uint
  OnChange func()
  ... all sorts of other options
}

type Account struct {
  Name string
  Address string
 Comments string
}

func (m *Account) ChangeAddress(old, new string) error {
  fmt.Println("Address was", old, "is now", new)
  return nil
}

// model to bind to
myAccount := &Account{}

g := NewFliexGrid(6) // 6 column layout
g.Add(NewLabel("Name"), nil)    // nil options == default  1 col
g.Add(NewInput(&myAccount.Name), nil)
g.Add(NewLabel("Address", nil)
g.Add(NewInput(&myAccount.Address), &gridOpts(Span: 2, OnChange: myAccount.ChangeAddress)) // uses up the 6th col - onto a new row
g.Add(NewLabel("Comments", nil)
g.Add(NewInput(&myAccount.Comments, &gridOpts(Span: 5)) // use the whole row 
```
